Enforced: a hull is a closed convex polyhedron with flat faces of at most 256 edges and no two neighbours that are one plane split in two, within about 0.8 degrees with every corner within half of FLAT, 1e-4 of the hull's size, of the other's plane (a mesh with such faces loses contact points, Gregorius 2015, so `addHull` refuses it); a real crease under 0.8 degrees between faces too wide to be one flat face is taken, as a hull of random points has them; its rows last for the world's life. By method: the separating axis test is linear in vertices per face and quadratic in edges, with no hill climbing or cached axis yet, so a hull of hundreds of faces costs a step more than it should until the quiet pass. By method: GJK stops after 64 descents, and the expanding polytope holds 96 vertices and 192 faces; a depth search that runs out gives no contact for that step and the next step tries again. By method: a point with a new id continues an old one within 2 cm on the first body, so a contact that jumps further starts its impulses from zero. By method: a contact's normal is found once a step and held for its substeps, and a point the body has not yet reached acts as a plane (Catto 2013's speculative point), so a fast body passing a corner can feel a ghost of that plane; not measured, batch 126 owns it. Contact defaults: 8 substeps, 2 passes, 120 Hz capped at a quarter of the substep rate, damping ratio 10, slop 0.2 mm, push speed 3 m/s. By method (2026-11-08): at one pass a substep a contact between two dynamic bodies that neither dominates is capped at an eighth of the substep rate (30 Hz at 4 substeps) while it carries under 50 times the lighter body's weight, as one pass settles no pile at a quarter; the ground, kinematic and dominant bodies and heavier loads keep the quarter. Measured at 4 substeps of one pass: the 20-row pyramid sleeps at 2.3 s, its top moved 32 mm, its bottom row 1.19 mm into the floor; 30 rows, whose bottom pairs carry about 40 times a cube's weight, sleep at 2.0 s and rest at 5.9e-4 m/s with sleeping off; the 1:100 and 1:1000 stacks keep the quarter and sag 14.4 and 137 mm. A deeper pile whose bottom pairs pass 50 times takes the quarter there; not measured past 30 rows. By method (2026-11-07): a substep relaxes as many times as it pushes, so 2 relaxing passes of joints and contacts at the defaults where there was 1: one pass left the friction anchors' push in a pile of 14 rows or more as speed, and it rocked for good. By method: a manifold's normal rows sweep until no impulse moves by more than rounding, at most 16 sweeps a pass, on the points' speeds alone; a relaxing pass settles in 3 to 8 sweeps on the 1:1000 stack. By method (2026-11-08): a manifold of four points ends each sweep with the exact step along the one pattern of its impulses that moves no body, the points' shares of one load among themselves, which the sweeps settled only by the leak (about 3 percent a sweep), so a soft pass ran all 16; it now settles in about 4 (perf-history 80). Friction keeps one sweep. By method (2026-11-08): inside the slop a biased pass closes a point rigidly to the slop's depth, (gap + slop) / h as a speculative row (Catto's Solver2D soft step), and the soft push acts only past it, so every point of a resting manifold rests at the same depth whatever its load: a cube released on a slope below tan t = mu holds under 1e-6 m from its first second (it moved up to 3.8e-5 m as its points sank at speeds that followed their loads). Measured on the harness, defaults and 4 substeps of one pass: creep 5.5e-5 and 5.9e-6 m to 0; the 1:1000 stack's top drifts 1.6e-8 and 1.4e-7 m (6.6e-7 and 3.7e-6 m before the exact step of the four points' shares); the 20-row pyramid at the defaults sleeps at 1.50 s (1.78 s before that step, 3.2 s earlier), and at 4 substeps of one pass, which fails its bars either way, moved its top 0.291 m (0.277) and its fastest box at 30 s 0.51 m/s (0.18); with the exact step of the four points' shares (2026-11-08) 0.270 m and 0.28 m/s, still awake until the eighth-rate spring of two movable bodies at one pass (above) let it sleep. By method (2026-11-08): a ball or a capsule meets the other surface at its core plus its radius along the normal, wherever it has turned to, so a rolling ball's point stays on the floor; its lever arm stays the step's contact point. A ball from rest at 30 degrees rolls within 1e-5 of 5/7 g sin t (it ran 1.0033 in its first second). By method (2026-11-08): a point struck while its gap is still open notes the speed it will meet the surface with, v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a d over the gap, gravity's gain added, so a ball from 1 m at e 0.5 peaks at 0.2487 m at the defaults and 0.2473 m at 4 substeps of one pass (was 0.2481 and 0.2432). By method: a resting contact sags by its load over its stiffness, which follows the lighter body, so a heavy box on a light one sits deeper: 3.9 mm at 1:100 and 3.5 cm at 1:1000 with metre cubes. A rolling ball slips 0.35 percent of its speed by 2.5 s, as friction is a stiff spring, and lands 0.13 percent over 5/7 g sin t. Enforced: a manifold holds four points. By method: the reduction always keeps the deepest point, so its area can fall short of the best four: 0.711 of the best at worst and 0.9915 on average over 3,000 random sets. Enforced: 536,870,912 pair rows and 32-bit offsets inside the block; a step throws when memory cannot hold the pairs. By method: pairs are found once a step over the motion expected at its start, so a body a contact turns round mid-step can leave its fat box until the next step; the margin is 0.04 m at any body size; a fixed body written by hand needs `touch`; a collider's row comes back only after a step. A single add or removal costs one pass over the lists, so adding one collider a frame to a very large world pays for the whole list. Until the narrow phase lands, two bodies touch when their fat boxes overlap, so islands run larger than they will. Writing a sleeper's columns does not wake it. A body at a steady pose with its energy under the threshold can go to sleep mid-air if nothing pushes it, as gravity is not a force the sleep test sees: a body at rest under gravity moves, so this needs zero gravity or `gravityScale` 0. A snapshot is the whole block, so its size follows capacity, not the bodies in use. By method: f32 state, as a far world needs `FloatingOrigin`. Needs Wasm SIMD, as core's kernel already does, so there is no second blueprint. `Physics`, `PhysicsBody` and `PhysicsCollider` of the entry serve free motion only: `setType`, `follow`, friction and the other contact settings, joints, queries, character controllers and `addModel` throw `unsupported` until their batch. `body.sleep()` and impulses take effect at the next step. A snapshot reads only in the kernel build that wrote it, and a `Physics`-level restore waits for `/snapshot`. Measured (LIM-366): 10,000 steps hash-equal in Node, native x86-64, Chromium 156 and Firefox 157 on one Windows PC; Safari, WebKit, ARM and any other machine are unmeasured. On that PC Windows will not start Playwright's Firefox from the home folder (a side-by-side error on `mozglue`, as Chromium's full `chrome.exe` gives there), so the run used a copy of it under the worktree through `REPLAY_FIREFOX`. | The kernel is staged behind `/next` until the switch; the root entry still runs Rapier. Bit-equal results hold for one kernel build, not across kernel versions. | Use the root entry, which still runs Rapier. |
| Own physics joints (`@margoengine/physics/next`, preview, 2026-11-07) | By method: locks are exact along a path of joints, so a chain of 50 hung straight holds a 1000:1 end mass to under 1e-5 of its length, at rest and swung at 3 m/s. By method: a lock's turning arm is read at the start of a substep, so a light link under a large pull turns as an explicit spring of stiffness about twice the pull times its arm; past about two radians a substep of that turn it grows. A chain of 50 laid out level with a 1000:1 end mass passes 1e-4 of its length at step 32 and 2 times by step 60 with 1 kg links of a sphere's inertia (0.001 kg m2 at 0.05 m arms); 16 substeps hold it to step 66, 32 to step 229, ten times the inertia to step 219 (`docs/known-bugs.md`). Where a branch or a ring ends a path, paths meet pass by pass: a grid under its own weight opens 0.18 mm at 8 by 8 and 0.95 mm at 30 by 30, a heavy hub with three arms 7.3 mm, and 5.3 to 8.7 mm with the hub started a micrometre to 0.3 mm aside, as the widest gap is the peak of a swing that rounding steers, but 1000 kg on the corner of an 8 by 8 grid of 1 kg links opens 69 mm and still moves at 0.2 m/s after 10 s (8 passes: 13 mm). By method: limits are one row at a time, so a long run of hinges on their stops carries its moment slowly: six links droop 48 mm, twelve droop 0.91 m and still move at 0.29 m/s in the last 5 s of 10. By method: a limit past its edge pushes back with the mass its row sees, as a contact does, so a limb a floor holds past its cone rests there: a hand of 0.36 kg comes to 0.02 rad past its cone, one of 3.6 g stays 0.49 rad past it under its 1.5 kg arm. At the edge a limit holds any load: a link of a hundredth of the mass carries a full one 0.008 rad past a cone of 0.2. By method: a rope is one row at a time, so two ropes under a 1000:1 end mass rest 35 mm long, 1.7 percent, and stay there. By method: a spring is implicit Euler, so with no damping one of 5 rad/s loses 23 percent of its amplitude in 10 s. `/articulation` (batch 128) is where branches and limits go exact. By method: one walk over every joint row a step, and rows and factors refreshed twice a substep, which the quiet pass may halve. By design: 2 passes at least for joints, so `iterations: 1` adds a settling pass for them; `generic` is not served yet. By design: a sensor reads the pose a step starts from, so an event comes up to a step after the overlap; two fixed bodies never meet, sensor or not; a disabled collider keeps its mass; dominance acts in contacts, not in joints. By method, four limits on the lock solve, each with a test that fails without it. (1) A row with under n u of its size left after the rows before it depends on them and carries nothing, n the rows of its path and u f32's epsilon (Higham 1990, stop 4.3 at his n u), read off Householder QR of M^-1/2 J^T so the doubles round each row only by its own length: a body held by ten rows on six freedoms stands still where it used to reach 18,904,462 m/s, and a path with 13 rows on 12 freedoms no longer keeps its dependent row (4e-7 of its size by elimination of J M^-1 J^T, 1e-32 now). Cost: a row within about sqrt(n u) radians of depending, 1.3e-3 rad on a path of 14 rows, is dropped too; and the kernel grew 4,449 B deflated (125,328 to 129,777 B). (2) A lock closes a gap at 3 m/s plus what the turning carries its anchors, the clamp of Buss and Kim 2005, whose D_max,i = d_i + D_max this is. A valid scene reaches it when a body is moved by hand off its joint or a hub turns at 8 rad/s at 100 m. Pairs are found once a step, so without it a joint 6 m open jumps a body past a wall in one substep. Cost: a wide gap takes more steps, and on the proof scenes it acted on 5 rows of 6,960 in the limb and moved no figure. (3) Where rows nearly depend on each other a push is a Gauss-Newton step outside its model, so a body's turn may rise by at most 0.2 rad a substep times N / M, and its centre by that much of its arm, N what the path asks and M what its bodies would each move (Buss and Kim 2005, section 4; they use 0.79 rad for inverse kinematics, here 0.79 lets a taut chain reach 39 m/s and 0.1 starts to cut the chain of fifty). A valid scene reaches it when a chain is pulled straight between two points further apart than it is long, the same pose as an arm reaching past its reach. Cost: what is cut stays open into the next substeps, and the whole path's push is cut, not only its bad direction, as a path has no singular value decomposition. It cut nothing in any scene of `kernel/tests/joints.rs`. (4) A warm start that would add more than a push's energy, half the island's mass times 3 m/s squared, is taken only as far as the minimum of the quadratic the passes descend. A valid scene reaches it when a limit catches a swing, as what the row holds is an impact and no load: once per catch on the proof scenes, keeping 0 to 7 percent. Cost: that row starts its substep cold, and no figure in `kernel/tests/joints.rs` moved. No paper does this; the line search is standard, its use here is our own. By method: a lock is exact and a contact is a capped spring, so a joint stretched through a wall drags its body through at about 1.5 m/s. By method: a turn past about 1 rad a substep leaves rows nothing to read, so a lock on a hub at 77 rad/s holds with 2 substeps, to 13 m on a radius of 10, and with 1 substep runs away and is refused after 59 steps. By design: a body past 1e15 in position or speed stops the world with `failed`, checked at the end of a step: a run away faster than that within one step would get past it, not seen in 200 random webs of 10,000 steps. Their top, 1.3e8 m/s for one step, is a kinematic turn of 77 rad/s forcing locks near a toggle, where the exact speed is one over the angle: only the pushing pass's bias is cut, after its speeds are solved in full, so a speed is answered in full. Scenes with no answer are only kept in the numbers: 60 random webs of unsatisfiable joints stay under 1e5 m/s, seed 45 spins under the 18,400 rad/s its kinematic turns can carry (2,559 rad/s; a cut of the whole solve once gave 162,278), and which seed is fastest changes with any constant; seeds 1 and 35 spin under 18,400 rad/s and hold every joint under the 56.85 m the scene's cube allows (956 rad/s and 38.0 m to step 400, 1,354 rad/s and 40.9 m to step 600), but near a toggle a row that does not yet depend is answered in full, so seed 49 reaches 10,991 m/s and a joint 165.8 m open and the 60 webs have no gap bar yet (`docs/known-bugs.md`). By method: each joint of the chain of 50 hung straight opens under 2e-5 m at rest and swung, under the same 1e-4 of its length as its stretch; laid out level and let fall, a joint opens 7.0 mm at 1:1, 9.7 mm at 10:1, 23 mm at 100:1 and 0.38 to 0.45 m at 1000:1 within 20 s, from rows that turn within a substep (`docs/known-bugs.md`) | A joint in a branch, a loop or on its limits settles over passes, so its gap under a far heavier load is the price; a chain is exact. | A grid or ring of joints under a far heavier load opens a gap (0.95 mm at 30 by 30; 69 mm for 1000 kg on the corner of an 8 by 8 grid), and a long run of hinges on their stops droops. | Use a chain, which is exact. Set `iterations` to 8, which narrows the 69 mm gap to 13 mm. An `/articulation` entry (batch 128) is planned and does not exist yet. |

Measured against Rapier 0.21 as a black box (`tests/next-revolved.test.js`): the mass, centre and principal moments of sharp shapes within 1e-5 of Rapier's; 1,600 random rays hit the same body as Rapier, within 2e-5 m of an exact f64 surface and 1e-4 of its normal, never further off than Rapier; casts within 1e-5 m of the exact first touch, where Rapier's are up to 9.4e-4 m off; a cylinder on its cap and on its side and a cone on its base rest within 0.01 m of where Rapier rests them. A ray from 20 to 400 m away meets a sharp cone within 4 float32 rounding units of its length (`kernel/tests/revolve.rs`). By method: contacts by GJK and the expanding polytope on the core with the border as a margin, plus the cap, side line or apex that faces the other shape; a cap's contact points lie on a 16-sided polygon whose corners are on the rim, inside it by at most 1.9 percent of the radius between corners; mass and inertia are integrals over the rounded profile turned about the axis, so a round shape weighs its border too. | The border is a margin on GJK, so a round shape needs no mesh and no extra rows; faces held as faces let a cylinder stand on its cap with a full manifold. | A round shape weighs more than on Rapier, which weighs only the core (an accepted difference, more correct); rays and casts on a round shape run GJK's ray cast, slower than the closed forms of a sharp one; between a cap polygon's corners a contact sits up to 1.9 percent of the radius inside the true rim. | Give `mass` instead of `density` to match a Rapier scene's weights. |

The method of Wei, Liu, Ling and Su 2022 (CoACD): concavity max(Hb, 0.3 Rv) on the mesh scaled to a largest side of 1, 3,000 samples per unit area, Monte Carlo tree search over 20 axis planes per axis, 500 iterations, 4 cuts ahead, ternary refinement, merging. Enforced: a closed mesh (each directed edge with its reverse, after welding equal positions when needed), whole triangles, indices in range, finite vertices, a volume; `concavity` above 0; whole `maxConvexHulls`, `planes`, `iterations`, `depth` of at least 1; `timeLimit` above 0. By design: the same mesh, options and seed give the same parts bit for bit in every engine (only + - * / and own roots); `timeLimit` (default 60,000 ms) throws `timeout`, never a part-done answer; `maxConvexHulls` (default 64) stops cutting with the least convex parts cut. By method: neighbours merge only over a whole shared cut face, not over part of one; the candidate planes are the three axes, no PCA (the paper's option). Measured against Rapier 0.21's V-HACD at defaults (`scripts/decomposition-vs-rapier.mjs`, one busy run): tube 4 parts to 7, Eq. 10 0.050 to 0.138; cup of five slabs 12 to 12, 0.032 to 0.035; closed cup 12 to 12, 0.025 to 0.052; torus 6 to 11, 0.036 to 0.030 with 8.8 percent hull volume over the mesh to 3.7; knight 15 to 19, 0.044 to 0.052; 1.1 to 17.3 s where Rapier takes 0.1 to 0.3 s. | A cut mesh keeps fine detail a voxel grid loses, and the tree search finds the cuts a greedy one misses (the paper's Fig. 9), so a body gets fewer, closer parts. | 5 to 120 times Rapier's build time on these meshes (a loss, perf history entry 81); the torus has fewer, looser parts than Rapier's at the same threshold; a mesh with holes is refused where V-HACD voxelizes it. | Decompose once at build time and store the parts; lower `iterations` or `planes` for speed; close a mesh's holes first, or give a fixed body a `trimesh`. |
| Own physics body kinds and mass (`@margoengine/physics/next`, preview, 2026-11-07) | By method: a body that stops being fixed finds the fixed colliders its boxes overlap by one walk over the sorted ends, so `setType` costs the world's collider count once; a body made fixed drops its pairs with fixed bodies. Enforced on both entries: `additionalSolverIterations` takes any whole number from 0 to 4294967295, Rapier's 32 bits, and throws a `RangeError` past it, where the root entry used to wrap 2^32 + 3 to 3 passes without a word; the kernel adds the counts without wrapping. | One body, one walk, no index kept for a rare call. | Measured on the root entry and matched: `setType(type, false)` keeps a sleeper asleep until the next step, which wakes it and what it touches whatever `wakeUp` said, and a body made fixed is not woken before that step; a still kinematic body reads asleep after the sleep window, `sleep()` stops it and a target wakes it (`next-bodies.test.js`). Accepted difference: the own solver wakes a whole sleeping island at the call (`setType(type, true)`, a velocity, an impulse), so between the call and the next step the bodies it touches read awake, where Rapier reads them asleep until its step wakes them; every pose and velocity of every step is the same. Accepted difference: a fixed body always reads `sleeping` false here; Rapier keeps a flag on fixed bodies that `sleep()` sets and that changes nothing. By method: a step runs `iterations` plus the most any awake island asks for, and an island takes the last of them, so it costs what a world of that many passes would for its own rows, plus a lookup per pair and path while any island asks. By design: with no collider mass, `setMassProperties` and `setAdditionalMass` figures are the body's exactly; with collider mass, the sum goes through the Jacobi rotations of `mass.rs` and rounds as any inertia does. The 20-row pyramid's top drops 28.26 mm, 28.35 mm when built top down (Box2D v3 29.11, Rapier 2D 29.56 on the same scene), and a heavy box on three light ones at 1:100 drops 52.29 mm, 0.6 percent from the closed form; nothing moves once resting. The contacts are solved colour by colour, coloured from the top of the scene down along gravity, so a pile rests the same whatever order its bodies were made in. The 100-row pyramid's top drops 684 mm by 10 s (Box2D v3 726, Rapier 2D 735) and its row 30 spreads 48 mm (70, 64): a pair keeps last step's reference face while the two faces' separations lie within one slop (5 mm), and a clipped point keeps the id of the end it replaces, so resting points keep their warm start. Measured against Blender 5.3: 862 of 862 real meshes within 4.58e-5 of their span at level 2; 346 of 348 stand-in runs of face-varying values at levels 1 and 2. | Refinement runs on the CPU at load. | `triangleSubdivisionRule = "smooth"` refines by the standard rule, with an issue. A value shared by faces that touch only at a point counts as one value: in mode `none` it stays sharp, and Blender gives one such value sharp and the other split, so those two runs differ (10 corners at level 1, up to 2.5e-2). Blender splits a value where faces turn opposite ways in UV space, and this entry keeps it one value, as the file has it: of 109 real meshes with mirrored or zero-area UV faces 41 match Blender and 68 differ, by up to 3.13e-1 near the folds. On the washer of usd-wg the split alone explains the whole difference; on meshes with zero-area UV faces the rest is not attributed. Time-sampled `points` refine at the first time only. Level 3 of a large stage is slow and large: each level gives four times the faces. | Pass a lower `level` to `subdivision()` (default 2), or a lower `maxTriangles` for the stage. |
| USD lights and cameras (`@margoengine/usdz/lux`, 2026-11-07) | By method: every area light becomes a punctual one, with no size in the shading; a light's or camera's values are read at the stage's first time, though its transform plays with `/anim`. Measured against OpenUSD 26.08 on 55 real stages: 46 of 46 visible lights, 44 of 44 cameras, within 7e-8. | Core has one directional light, so `applyGLTFLights` uses the first sun. Aperture offsets, `stereoRole`, depth of field and shutter are not read. ### React page

What a minimal React page downloads, and why it is larger than core + stage (23,924 B gzip). The cube page of the
bundler matrix (`Canvas`, `Mesh`, `BoxGeometry`, `PbrMaterial`, `useFrame`, and `OrbitControls` from
`@margoengine/react/controls`), built by Vite 8.3.4, React 19.3 and `@margoengine/react` installed alone with
`@margoengine/controls` (2026-10-27), measured from the build's source maps (minified bytes per package; gzip is each
package's own gzip size, scaled so the parts add up to the chunk's). Core lights every scene by default
(a sun and an ambient term), so this is also the minimal lit page.

| Part | Minified B | Gzip B | Needed for a lit scene? |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `react-dom` (client) | 206,925 | 62,263 | Yes: the app's own UI runtime, not Margo's |
| `react` + `scheduler` | 11,635 | 4,430 | Yes: the app's own |
| `@margoengine/core` (engine, renderer, Wasm kernel, camera, shaders, geometry) | 49,485 | 19,056 | Yes |
| `@margoengine/react` (components, internal, assets, the shadows hook) | 14,241 | 5,488 | Yes: `Canvas`, `Mesh` and the hooks |
| `@margoengine/stage` | 2,771 | 1,405 | Not to draw (core draws and lights the cube); `Canvas` wraps its engine in the stage it hands to `onCreated` and `<Stage>` |
| Vite runtime (preload helper, module preload polyfill), app code and `@margoengine/math` (170 B) | 3,135 | 1,609 | The build's own |
| **Entry, requested before the page runs** | **288,234** | **94,251** | Budget 100,000 B gzip |
| `@margoengine/controls/orbit` + its view helpers + profiles, when `OrbitControls` mounts | 17,999 | 6,951 | Yes, for orbiting |
| **Everything the page fetches** | **306,233** | **101,202** | |

React and React DOM are 66% of the page; Margo's part (core, stage, bindings) is 25,949 B gzip (27,028 B before the
stage feature entries and the React subpaths of 2026-10-27, which took 3,089 B of minified loaders out of the stage). Nothing optional is in
the entry: `PbrMaterial` is core's material and pulls in no other package.

- **Fixed (2026-10-26):** `OrbitControls`, `MapControls` and `CadControls` loaded the `@margoengine/controls` index,
  so mounting them fetched TransformControls, DragControls, the gizmo and the `@margoengine/bvh` raycaster as one
  112,655 B (39,072 B gzip) chunk. They now load `@margoengine/controls/orbit` and `/profiles`, `ArcballControls`
  loads `/arcball` and `TransformControls` loads `/transform`: the mount costs 6,951 B gzip, and a Vite build emits
  107,027 B gzip in all instead of 135,875 B.
- **Emitted, never fetched:** the arcball chunk (3,192 B gzip). Nothing else: since 2026-10-27 neither `Canvas` nor
  the stage reaches an optional package, so there are no stand-in stubs either.
- **A textured model** (`<Gltf src="BoxTextured.glb">` from `@margoengine/react/gltf-pro`, with `@margoengine/gltf-pro`
  installed): the entry grows by
  1,750 B gzip (the `Model` binding), and mounting it fetches gltf-pro (175,257 B, 56,074 B gzip: glTF parsing, the
  PBR material and shader, compression hooks) plus the model. The Draco and Basis Wasm are emitted for files that use
  them; this one does not, and the page does not request them.
- **Through `margoengine/react`:** a page emits no Draco or Basis file. `Model`, `Fbx`, `Animation` and the `materials`
  components reach those decoders, so they are separate entries (`margoengine/react/gltf-pro`, `/fbx`, `/animation`,
  `/materials`); Vite copies a `new URL` file when it reads a module, before tree-shaking.
- **Through a kit or `materials`, `animation`, `fbx`:** no Draco or Basis file either. Only the root of `@margoengine/gltf-pro`
  names the decoders; packages that draw models use `@margoengine/gltf-pro/model`, and `loadGLTF` is imported from
  `margoengine/gltf-pro`, not from `margoengine/game`, `/web` or `/viz`.
- Still on the controls index: `PointerLock` (from `@margoengine/react/controls`), because `@margoengine/controls` has no
  pointer-lock entry; a page that does not use it never emits it.

## External video materials (2026-11-08)

`@margoengine/video/material` adds a caller-owned `HTMLVideoElement` or `VideoFrame` to a `Material.features` list. No JS-side frame upload occurs. The browser/driver may still copy or convert internally; platform zero-copy and throughput are unmeasured. A frame is imported per draw, one sampler per device; there are no mipmaps or repeat wrapping. UV0 (default) and UV1 are supported; `flipY` defaults to true, matching Texture's image orientation (first row at v=1); false puts it at v=0. Sources must be ready/open and origin-clean. WebGL2 returns `MargoError` code `unsupported` with a help link. Core's compact material has no feature slot. Custom WGSL must retain the standard surface/base-colour hook. The existing material's own maps, lighting and other features keep their own costs. External textures consume four sampled-texture slots, one implicit sampler and one uniform slot, in addition to the explicit filtering sampler; a fully mapped material can exceed a device's default limits. Alpha affects colour rendering; auxiliary caster/picking passes retain the material's existing alpha inputs. Generated colour frames and a canvas MediaStream on the RTX A6000/Edge prove imports across tasks, no material-path frame uploads and sRGB byte accuracy within 2 of 255 at 1x and 4x MSAA. Real movie files, other adapters, browser-internal copies, speed and custom shader combinations are unmeasured. Run `node scripts/gpu-lock.mjs run --owner=video-check -- node packages/video/test/material-check.mjs` after a package build.

## Page canvas recording (2026-11-08)

`@margoengine/video/record` records origin-clean page canvases with MediaRecorder, on WebGPU, WebGL2 or 2D. Container support and codecs are the browser's choice: default WebM, optional MP4, otherwise coded unsupported with a help link. The caller supplies optional live audio tracks, cloned so originals remain owned by the caller. No audio mixing is performed. All compressed chunks stay in memory until stop. Real-time capture can drop frames or shorten media on a busy/background page; no exact duration/frame count or A/V synchronization bound is claimed. Stop waits for the final chunk; abort, disposal and errors release owned tracks and discard the result. No Node/OffscreenCanvas API or alternate codec fallback is included. The real RTX A6000/Edge check decodes WebM (VP8/Opus) and MP4 (H.264/Opus) from both backends: generated colour and a tone are stand-ins. Other browsers, players, codecs, microphone permission paths and long recordings are unmeasured. Entry 1,140 B gzip; budget 1,396 B. No speed claim. See LIM-571.

## 360 and stereo video (2026-11-08)

`@margoengine/video/360` uses UV0 of `sphereGeometry`, an unlit back-sided material and a camera at its centre. Image centre -Z, right +X, top +Y. Mono (default) spans the whole source; stereo-left-right holds one complete panorama per half, selected explicitly for a screen material (eye left by default). Stereo sources need at least two pixels across, enforced before binding. Sampling clamps half a texel inside each eye; no mips or repeat wrapping. WebGL2 receives coded unsupported with a help link. One video feature per material; playback and source lifetime remain caller-owned. XR reuses native `XRLayers.video` with an equirectangular sphere, automatic compositor eye choice and radius 0 at infinity; it requires the draft WebXR Layers API and XRMediaBinding. Missing XR support propagates the existing XR error. Generated colour panoramas prove six screen directions and both eyes on RTX A6000/Edge; an integrated stand-in session/binding proves XR delegation and layer lifecycle. No headset, real movie, other browser/GPU or speed evidence. Entry 1,694 B gzip, budget 1,881 B. LIM-573.

## Own 2D certified geometry and solver evidence (2026-11-08)

The optional Rust kernel's exact rectangle SAT path requires a current canonical axis rectangle in pair-local
coordinates, finite vertex squared norms at most 2^120 and B-normal squared norms at most 4. The preferred-face
distance certificate additionally requires a coordinate-magnitude bound M in [1,2^20], positive finite A-face
separation and its finite radius/speculation/result checks. These restrict eligibility for an optimization;
all other inputs retain the full prior collision path. [Proof](architecture/physics2d-manifold-proof.md) and
[entry 101](whitepaper/perf-history.md) record the precise guards and unchanged native/Wasm hashes.

The two-point block solver remains production behavior. Earlier per-point alternatives did not meet all contracts
and establish a browser gain. All original accuracy bars remain unchanged. The subsequent sustained-support fix
establishes the required centered 1:1000 contact stack and deliberately re-pins the mixed scene; see the
[support contract](#own-2d-sustained-contact-support). Owned-2D CCD remains separate T-11 / 127.y work, distinct
from existing 1000:1 joint-chain and 3D CCD evidence.
After browser diagnostics: Edge 3.66/1.69/14.52 ms and Firefox 3.50/1.52/11.20 ms for Margo/Box2D/Rapier; separate
loaded sessions cannot prove before/after speed. The Box2D goal remains open and quiet reruns are required.

### Own 2D input validation

The raw Rust kernel under `packages/physics2d/kernel` exposes checked `Result<_, PhysicsError>` body/shape/chain
creation, world stepping and handle operations, bounds queries, scalar/coherent/four-pair and smooth-chain collision.
The public Rust `solver::solve` entry also checks current inputs and derived outputs; its direct-call substep
must be positive and representable. `World::step` retains its validated nonpositive-step no-op policy.
Use `?` to propagate a refusal, or read `PhysicsError::code()` and `help()`; the latter points to this section.
The Rapier-backed TypeScript facade is a separate API. Pure math and mass-property utilities are not all checked
entry points; in particular, `mass::mass_of` retains its direct `MassData` return.

| Code | Refusal |
| --- | --- |
| `PHYSICS2D_NOT_FINITE` | A required finite input or current-state value is NaN or infinite |
| `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_CORE` | An invalid active core count or radius would make collision data unsafe to index or use |
| `PHYSICS2D_DEGENERATE` | A requested shape/chain has insufficient usable geometry |
| `PHYSICS2D_ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` | Derived arithmetic cannot represent a required finite value, including positive mass/inertia lost to underflow or an overflowing reciprocal |
| `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_HANDLE` | A body, shape, contact or joint relationship refers outside the current valid objects |
| `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_PARAMETER` | A checked parameter violates its domain, such as negative density, friction or restitution |

Body definitions, collision poses and speculative cutoffs require finite used values. Shape material values are
finite and nonnegative. There is no geometry-independent minimum positive density: shape and aggregate mass,
inertia, moments, centres, extents and required reciprocals must remain representable in their actual arithmetic.
This includes the reciprocal of a positive inverse mass/inertia: a finite first reciprocal can round to a value
whose inverse overflows. Both the rounded centre and reconstructed origin are checked before publication.
Derived contact normal/tangent metrics and their required inverses must also be finite: two individually valid
inverse masses can overflow when added. Such a contact returns `PHYSICS2D_ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` before solving.
Computed contact-point relative velocity, normal approach and anchor base are also checked; finite body velocity
alone does not imply a representable `v + w cross r` at a very large contact arm.
Nonzero finite rotation pairs use scale-safe normalization when their squared length overflows or underflows;
ordinary normalization bits are retained. Exact zero pairs in a body definition retain the documented identity
conversion. A directly mutated zero stored body rotation is `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_PARAMETER`; a nonfinite or zero
rotation derived during integration returns the arithmetic error rather than becoming identity or zero silently.
An infinite density and a unit box at `f32::from_bits(1)` are refused before publishing a shape or NaN centre.
Genuine zero density or zero-area geometry keeps its zero-mass behavior; a positive mass/inertia rounded to zero
cannot take that fallback. A dynamic body with no mass retains the existing 1 kg, no-turn fallback.

Body/shape creation and an entire `create_chain` call are transactional for validation/arithmetic failures:
no partial body, shape list, mass state or chain proxies are published, and refused IDs remain available.
`World::step` preflights current public mutable data and relationships before simulation work: body state and
shape lists, current core counts/used vertices/normals/radii, materials/chain ghosts, contact handles/counts/used
values and joint handles/state. A stale broad-phase shape ID is checked before callback indexing. A linear
visitation check over shape references refuses duplicate, missing and foreign-body references.
Used cached normal impulses must be nonnegative. Friction retains the ordinary product/sqrt result when that
product is finite and uses a scale-safe geometric mean when it overflows. Invalid derived scalar or SIMD clamp
bounds propagate to the step's coded arithmetic-error check, rather than asserting inside Rust's clamp.
These checks use current data. Explicit documented sentinels, such as a joint motor's
positive-infinite maximum force for an unlimited motor, remain supported. A later simulation arithmetic error
is returned to the caller; the whole step is not a rollback transaction.

At `47f81f909`, the reproduced collision panic requires both a NaN pose and NaN cutoff: a missing closest-distance
candidate leaves a zero hit mask, whose trailing-zero index escapes the candidate rows. The literal NaN-pose
review call with a finite cutoff returned an empty manifold here. The fix rejects nonfinite public inputs and
checks missing face/distance candidates internally, including the four-pair path; it does not treat invalid
input as an ordinary empty contact. Native regressions cover both forms, overflow, current-array mutations,
creation rollback and valid retained-reference results. Each existing Wasm `check(i)` also exercises invalid
input refusal before comparing the same three production hashes. No hash was re-pinned and no speed result is
claimed. [Reproduce](whitepaper/reproduce.md#own-2d-input-validation) lists the commands and baseline failures.

Input validation closes the input/publication and absent-candidate error class. The separately derived support
correction below establishes the required centered contact bar. Owned-2D CCD is separate T-11 / 127.y work.

## Frame-accurate video decoding (2026-11-08)

Optional `@margoengine/video/codecs` fully buffers nonfragmented, self-contained, unencrypted AVC avc1 MP4. It reads the first video track, one sample description, stsz/stsc/stco/co64/stts/ctts/stss and a rate-1 media edit optionally after an empty edit, including 64-bit headers and edit versions 0/1. Movie times have microsecond precision; colliding timestamps are refused. Each request decodes from sync through the GOP, flushing reordering, selecting the requested timestamp and closing other frames. Requests are exclusive and abortable; caller closes returned frames. Edits expose only frames whose PTS starts inside the media edit; empty lead-in clamps to the first visible frame. No audio, streaming, playback scheduler, arbitrary edits, fragmented MP4, WebM, other codecs, rotation/display transforms or external media references. Large files/long GOPs can need substantial memory/CPU. WebCodecs/AVC support is browser-specific and checked; renderer independent, including beside WebGL2 (the external material remains WebGPU-only). Unit stand-ins prove reordered sample tables, edit boundary regression and ownership. Generated AVC MP4 is decoded/rendered on RTX A6000/Edge. The outside CC0 MDN flower clip adds 150 real AVC High frames with B-frame reordering: every edited timestamp matches FFprobe and all 150 copied decoded-frame byte arrays match the independently demuxed WebCodecs reference exactly. This shares the browser decoder and is not cross-decoder accuracy proof. Edit bounds use exact native ticks, with one microsecond rounding after edits; source decode timestamps must also remain unique. Other browsers/GPUs and speed unmeasured. Entry 3,458 B gzip, unchanged budget 3,593 B. LIM-575.

## Video alpha and chroma key (2026-11-08)

Optional `@margoengine/video/alpha` reuses the external material feature. Stacked colour is top/left, raw grayscale red-channel alpha bottom/right; equal pixel halves require an even packed dimension of at least 2. Both rectangles clamp at half-texel bounds. Colour must be straight, not premultiplied. RGB keying uses sRGB Euclidean distance, threshold 0.15 and softness 0.1 by default, green key [0,1,0]. Threshold is 0..sqrt(3), softness positive through sqrt(3), with distinct float32 edges; feature parameters are fixed on creation. No despill, lighting adaptation or colour/hair recovery. One external video feature per material, UV0/flipY true defaults; caller owns playback and source lifetime. Alpha multiplies source/material alpha before colour-pass alphaTest/blending; enable transparent for soft edges. Existing direct sRGB output-space blending is preserved. Shadow/picking coverage retains its existing material inputs, without external alpha. WebGL2 refuses with code/help link. Real RTX A6000/Edge checks generated masks at 0/64/128/255 for both layouts, fractional keying and cutout; these are stand-ins, not real movies. ## Own 2D sustained contact support

The recovery cap applies to the combined elastic residual, `max(beta*s+C*lambda,-P)`, rather than penetration
bias alone. For positive recovery speed P, stationary positive support retains the original spring root
`beta*s+C*lambda=0`: the cap imposes no finite force ceiling on feasible, representable loads. This is not an
unbounded floating-point magnitude or arbitrary-geometry stability guarantee. P=0 retains disabled recovery
and may have nonunique overpenetrated stationary states; the coupled correction declines it.

The coupled equilibrium correction is limited to a certified dynamic contact path with one static terminal.
It retains physical masses and the original compliance. Branches, cycles, multiple anchors, joints,
kinematic/sleeping terminals, nonzero restitution, original separating motion, open rows, unsupported gravity
wrenches or uncertified ranks use general capped dynamics. Current geometry, unilateral/friction feasibility,
finite arithmetic, casts, rotations and residuals are certified before an atomic component commit. Recovery
displacement uses the existing P*h substep budget. Sleep observes actual substep pose rate as well as final
relaxed speed, with unchanged thresholds/time and island propagation.

All 29 native physical bars pass, including the unchanged 1:100 and required 1:1000 centered contact predicates,
100-row pile sag, slope creep, bounce, friction, joints and sleep. The 1:1000 result is 0.518550681 m sag versus
0.518550736 m closed form, zero final displacement from the one-second sample, asleep at 0.8833334 s. The
unchanged regression fails on verified main 47f81f909: 1.186208290 m sag and 92.105 mm creep. The mixed-scene pin changes
intentionally from `9acb68471fbe6ba0` to `92db6847c4e919d4`; pyramid/joint-grid pins are unchanged.
The same two stack predicates run inside Wasm `check(0)`; native scalar/SIMD and shipped Wasm SIMD agree on
the stack metrics. Wasm always selects SIMD even when its stored `contact_lanes` setting is false.

The preserved geometry-dependent point spring has a negative local bending direction in the sagged 1:1000
column under small lateral perturbations, independently differentiated and checked with Margo's own manifolds.
Centered axial acceptance does not establish arbitrary lateral stability. No artificial angular stiffness or
mass threshold was fitted to hide it. See the [support derivation](architecture/physics2d-support-proof.md),
[bending analysis and executable probe](architecture/physics2d-support-bending.md), and
[reproduction commands](whitepaper/reproduce.md#own-2d-sustained-support).

The normal solver's finite-predicate reduction relies on actual private caller dataflow, not arbitrary
independent helper arguments. It preserves the same accepted/exceptional lane masks, raw-row and used-soft
domain checks, cap membership, post-motion finiteness and coded errors. The
[IEEE proof and compiler inventory](architecture/physics2d-finite-certificates.md) state those restrictions;
static predicate counts do not establish dynamic instruction counts or a browser speed gain.

The frame planner is linear in bodies, contacts and joints. Its flat graph/path/gap buffers retain capacity
bounded by historical maximum body/contact counts, rather than per-body or per-component capacity maxima.
Current graph contents, eligibility and weights rebuild each frame. General branching graphs skip the extra
substep path work; accepted components still use local allocations and two banded factorizations each substep.
Retaining scratch memory trades its lifetime for fewer allocation calls; this is not an allocation-free world
or a Box2D speed-parity claim. CCD remains outside this correction.

## 2D global illumination (batch 55)

Optional `@margoengine/lighting2d/gi` evaluates 1..8 spatial cascades, 1..32 base directions, angular ratio 1..8,
interval ratio >1, base distance >0, 0..4 finite diffuse bounce orders, albedo 0..1, intensity >=0. Defaults are
4/4/4/4/16/1/.5/1 respectively. World probe spacing doubles from one unit; centres are on the .5 lattice.
The far interval ends at baseDistance * intervalRatio ** (cascades - 1), which must fit float32.
Radiance/transmittance merges trace each of four child connectors before interpolation (RASTI appendix A).
Two-sided surface patches are at most baseDistance long; diffuse gathers use 32 normalized cosine samples and
midpoint-constant patch radiance. Surface gathers offset origins by .001 world units and ignore ray/edge
intersections at distances <= .0001 to avoid self-intersection. Small sources and spatial detail below those samples can be missed. The analytic
radius-six circular-source test over eleven distances 8..60 is within 5% of asin(radius/distance)/pi on CPU and RTX A6000;
this is a measured fixture bound, not an arbitrary-scene accuracy guarantee. No speed claim.
Patch count is capped at 65,536. The CPU hierarchy has an 8,000,000 sample-evaluation ceiling per query/grid.
GPU scene/cascade buffers must each fit maxStorageBufferBindingSize and 1D dispatch groups must fit
maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension; excessive combinations throw a coded RangeError instead of truncating work.
Cascade memory is 16 bytes per spatial/angular sample; two surface fields use 64 bytes per patch, plus 32 bytes
geometry per patch, 32 per emitter, 96 per direct light, masks and aligned per-dispatch uniforms.
CPU/GPU options, finite bounce orders, exact opaque visibility/energy fixtures and lifecycle are tested. Native WebGL2
rejects with coded unsupported/help. HDR needs a floating target; an unorm target clamps at presentation. LIM-599.

### Pixel batch 102 review limits (2026-11-08)

Flat CRT mapping uses the same integer centre-coordinate quotient as PixelScale nearest; all-off includes exact source boundaries with no excluded samples. Curved CRT reference comparisons exclude points within 0.001 texel of an edge, where float32 and float64 can choose different texels. Scale/CRT scissor clipping applies to canvas views; an explicit output texture still covers its own fitted rectangle. Palette cycling uses the represented finite product `rate * seconds` modulo the run length; multiplication can already round away fractional steps at large magnitudes, and overflow is rejected with coded `state` and a help link. Tests cover native WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer on one RTX A6000/Edge only; other hardware, physical CRT fidelity and performance remain unmeasured.

## Ambisonic beds (batch 110)

Optional audio/ambisonics: 1,919 B gzip; audio root 7,638 B and core plus stage 23,837 B. First-order four-channel ACN/SN3D W,Y,Z,X buffers only, positive finite duration, explicit convention assumption. Default format ambix; other conventions/channel counts produce linked unsupported. No FuMa/N3D/A-format conversion, higher/mixed orders, appended stereo, CAF adaptor or Opus metadata parser. Loading delegates to existing listener.load with AbortSignal and browser codec support; four-channel 24-bit PCM WAV with 44.1-to-48 kHz resampling is tested.

Default loop true, volume 1 within 0..1, smoothing listener.smoothing (default 0.02 s finite nonnegative time constant). Eight gain paths, one source, splitter and stereo merger per bed. Identity ACN front/left/up maps engine -Z/-X/+Y. Normalized copied world quaternion rotates field; listener forward/up define the inverse head orientation, translation ignored. Collinear directions retain the last independent decoder orientation (initially -Z forward, +Y up). Camera following copies camera.up, including roll and exact poles. Two virtual cardioids at +/-30 degrees output 0.5*(W+direction dot XYZ) times volume. This is stereo ambience, not HRTF/binaural localization or arbitrary loudspeaker decoding. Gain interpolation blends matrices rather than remaining a rigid rotation during fades. Author seamless loops and headroom. Start at/after now; stop/restart resets phase. Listener teardown/dispose cuts sources and frees decoder nodes, preserving buffers.

## React Native target dropped (LIM-615)

React Native is not supported; batch 117 job 6 is dropped. Margo targets the web, including mobile browsers.
The planned native path is the Rust engine. A React Native target would require a native WebGPU surface and
Android/iOS toolchains and devices to prove rendering, loading and lifecycle behavior; this repository provides
no such proof. Checked 2026-11-09: Hermes's current [language feature documentation](https://github.com/meta/hermes/blob/static_h/doc/Features.md)
and [next stable release notes](https://github.com/meta/hermes/blob/static_h/doc/blog/2026-06-05-new-hermes-stable-release.md)
do not document supported WebAssembly execution. The Hermes author's [WebAssembly preview](https://tmikov.blogspot.com/2026/02/webassembly-comes-to-hermes_01829874520.html)
describes experimental execution, not production readiness. This is not a claim that Hermes cannot run Wasm;
neither the preview nor compiling Hermes itself to Wasm establishes Margo phone compatibility.

## Wasm Content Security Policy

A policy that restricts scripts must permit Wasm compilation with `script-src 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` for each Wasm-backed path, including core engine creation and stages. Worker response policies need the permission too. [CSP requirements](csp.md) list the exact header and entries. Blocked initialization reports MargoError code `failed` with a help link; unrelated binary, SIMD and fetch errors retain their identity.

### Lighting2d direct-pass storage and lifetime ceilings

- Rect, circle and polygon masks (including inversion) and layer filtering run on root, soft, cookie and height.
  Circle centres default to world `(0,0)`. Polygon vertices cost 16 bytes each and must fit `maxStorageBufferBindingSize`.
- Height occluders cost 48 bytes each; emissive sprites cost 64 bytes each. Both lists grow to the device storage binding
  limit; the former 64-item truncation is removed. Oversized lists throw before drawing.
- Height light uniforms cost `max(256, minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment)` bytes each, capped by `maxBufferSize`.
  Soft samples are integers 1..64. Cameras require finite values and positive zoom. Mutated lights/sprites are validated.
- Height directional shadow rays are capped at 10,000 world units; elevation for shadow projection clamps to
  `[0.01, PI/2 - 0.01]` radians. Circle footprints are analytic here; ordinary direct shadows use 24-sided circle edges.
- Emissive owns three full-resolution `rgba16float` textures, 24 bytes/pixel, plus caller output and any optional Bloom
  intermediates. HDR values may overflow half precision above 65,504; an unorm presentation clips above 1.
- Native WebGL2 is unsupported by every lighting2d entry. Tests assert the coded rejection rather than a rendered route.
  GPU evidence is one RTX A6000 only. Manually supplied command encoders must be submitted before pass disposal.

## Poisson disk placement (LIM-621)

Optional procedural/poisson: 1,335 B min+gzip JavaScript plus a lazy 29,914 B Wasm file (13,192 B gzip).
CPU-only on WebGPU and WebGL2. Rectangle or area-weighted triangle-soup darts, ambient Euclidean separation,
not geodesic spacing. Finite coordinates within +/-1,000,000; radius 0.000001..1,000,000; maximum 65,536 triangles,
65,536 returned points and 2,000,000 candidates. Defaults: seed 1, 4,096 points, 100,000 candidates.
Zero numerical area carries no probability, including cross products rounded to zero. Finite dart budgets need not
cover a domain or return the point limit. No spectral, maximal-covering or frame-time promise. Output is float64;
conversion to float32 can reduce separation. Signals precede synchronous sampling; workers enable in-flight aborts.
Synthetic fixtures and a float64 oracle prove spacing, bounds, area weighting and exact rejection output.
Real production-browser WebGPU/WebGL2 contexts prove lazy assets below a non-root base and independence from
device/context loss. Authored meshes, hardware speed and cross-platform bit identity are unmeasured.

## Caustic path guiding (batch 99, LIM-622)

`@margoengine/voxel-pathtracer/guiding` adds a pure diffuse continuation proposal toward the existing deflector
table: up to eight static orthogonal pure smooth non-dispersive glass instances and eight mirrors. Visible box
faces are sampled by world area; interior origins use enclosing faces, excluding any face containing the origin.
The PDF converts to solid angle and sums all overlapping bounds. Actual voxel traversal and Fresnel transport
remain unchanged. `guideStrength` is finite `0..0.95`, default `0.5`; zero uses the original kernel exactly,
and empty guide tables retain the baseline random stream. No learning, photons or persistent GPU allocation.

Roulette removes accumulated cosine/mixture factors from its survival heuristic so small importance weights
are not immediately discarded. The heuristic scale is bounded `1e-20..1e20`, with actual survival `0.05..1`
after bounce three and actual throughput divided by that survival. Ordinary bounce caps still truncate paths.
Bounds can contain empty geometry or point below the surface, producing zero-contribution proposals. Other
BSDFs, unsupported deflectors and geometry beyond the table retain ordinary path sampling. A geometry prior
can increase variance when its objects contribute little. No general convergence or wall-time gain is claimed.

`tests/guiding-browser.mjs` keeps a fixed 2x squared-RGB-error bar on a generated small-glass caustic at 64 samples
against a 16,384-sample guided reference, with separate independent original-tracer energy comparisons and an
analytic unit furnace. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility run the shader; native WebGL2 refuses with code
`unsupported` and a registered help link. Native device restoration and disposal are exercised.

Entry size with bare peers external: guiding 2,535 B gzip; new budget 2,791 B includes the standard 256 B headroom.
Root 80,431 B, studio 1,047 B, restir 1,934 B and core plus stage 23,837 B remain unchanged. No existing size,
accuracy or time gate was relaxed.

## WFC worker solving (batch 69)

Local heap solves only, same grid/rule/pair/restart bounds and backend selection as chunks. One dedicated browser worker per job, rules/pins cloned, Uint16 result transferred. Main-thread cloning has a cost. Latest-only single-consumer progress is real work, not a percentage; restarts may revisit cells and Wasm counters wrap after 2^32-1. ## Multiple-scattering tracer sky (batch 99, LIM-626)

The new optional `@margoengine/voxel-pathtracer/sky` imports the optional sky peer's existing `/hillaire` entry.
`traceSkyEnvironment` calls `bakeHillaireEnvironment`, returning a linear RGBA Float32 map plus a separate attenuated
sun. Bake defaults are 256x128, noon, altitude zero, sun illuminance 20, Earth, multiple scattering and stylized
night enabled. Width is 1..2048, height 1..1024 and storage must fit the device's buffers. Altitude is at most
100000000 metres, sun illuminance at most 1000000, coefficients/albedo at most 1, radii/heights at most 100000 km.
The existing 256x64 transmittance and 32x32 multiple LUTs feed a 64-step ray march per texel. Higher scattering orders
are isotropic, geometry spherical and the observer position fixed by altitude. Re-bake when settings change; this
environment adds no local atmospheric attenuation or aerial perspective. Night reuses the stylized gradient,
procedural stars and moon, time zero without twinkle; unresolved stars retain mean integrated light. It does not
include astronomical catalogues, Milky Way, spectral airglow or spectral transport. Numeric night magnitudes other
than normalized moon direction are at most 1000000. A plain WebGL2 context is refused with coded help; a WebGL2
compatibility device executes the same model. Native and compatibility values, analytic vacuum/ground, traced
lighting, cancellation, resource disposal and real native device restoration are recorded in
`docs/whitepaper/results/batch-99-sky-20261109.json`. No speed or reference-renderer equality claim.

The environment bake requires Float32-distinct planet/atmosphere radii and vertical scattering optical depth

discs are outside the bake domain. Both equirectangular dimensions determine the night filtering footprint.

## Space colonisation trees (LIM-631)

Optional procedural/trees generates a branching skeleton, not a surface mesh. Default root [0,0,0],
seed 1, 512 attraction points in an ellipsoid above the root, segmentLength 0.2, influenceRadius 3,
killRadius 0.3, maxNodes 2048 and maxIterations 128. Custom XYZ Float64Array attraction points can
extend below a supplied root for roots; an empty cloud returns only the root. Custom point/root coordinates are finite
within +/-1,000,000. Count is bounded to 8192, nodes to 16384, iterations to 512 and the product of
attractors, node capacity and iteration capacity to 134,217,728. SegmentLength 0.0001..10000,
influenceRadius 0.0001..1,000,000, killRadius at least half the segment length and at most the influence
radius. A cap or lack of reachable attraction can stop growth with points remaining; inspect stopped
and remainingAttractions. No guarantee all attraction points are reached, no collision avoidance,
species, biological validity, tubes/leaves, or artistic-quality claim. Output arrays are owned.
Loading is abortable; generation checks abort before synchronous work, with a worker needed for
interruption in flight. One feature-local Rust/Wasm asset; CPU generation on either rendering backend
survives device/context loss. All proof inputs are STAND-IN. No elapsed-time or SIMD speed claim.
Entry JavaScript 1,540 B gzip, new ceiling 1,796 B; trees.wasm 39,113 B raw / 16,393 B gzip.

identical 674-node skeleton. The count excludes grid lookup and bounding-box operations. Core plus
stage remains 23,837 B gzip below its unchanged strict 25,000 B ceiling.
Shared loading failures now have code failed, help and original cause; caller abort reasons and specific CSP/HTTP faults are preserved. Current Poisson JS 1,335 B and dungeon JS 1,277 B remain within their unchanged ceilings of 1,525 B and 1,479 B; all Wasm assets are unchanged.

### Accumulated planar shadows (batch 56, job 2)

The optional staging/accumulate entry averages equal-weight binary visibility from points on a
horizontal disk. The Y-up receiver is finite; geometry outside its footprint or height is clipped.
Light height above the plane must exceed the casting height after float32 rounding. Receiver sizes
are 1e-6..1e6, world/light coordinate magnitudes at most 1e6, radius 0..1e6, frames integer 1..1024;
blur must be 0 and static false. One sample per rendered frame, then held history; camera changes
do not invalidate world-space shadows. In-place pose/vertex changes need invalidate(); constantly
changing geometry cannot converge. Opacity/displacement/clipping GPU changes conservatively reset.

No inverse-square or cosine weighting, HDR light sampling, indirect light, general receiver surface,
or photographic-product quality claim. Raster resolution and hardware subpixel snapping bound thin
detail. The exact GPU oracle is the Windows Direct3D eight-bit raster grid; other hardware can differ
at subpixel boundaries. WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are tested; native WebGL2 refuses with
linked unsupported. Generated geometry is a stand-in. Entry 9,314 B gzip (ceiling 9,593 B); inherited
root 8,129 B (unchanged ceiling 8,259 B); core plus stage 23,837 B below 25,000 B. No speed claim.

## Sharp SDF models (LIM-632)

Optional procedural/sdf uses a feature-local Rust/Wasm uniform-grid dual contourer.
Default is an axis-aligned box of half size .75 in bounds [-1.5,1.5]^3, 24 cells
per axis. Resolution is 4..64; at most 63 sphere/box/binary CSG nodes; coordinates
within +/-10000, sizes .0001..10000, bounds extent .0001..10000 per axis. All sampled
boundary values must be positive or generation throws, never silently clips.
Analytical primitive gradients, 40 root bisections, mass-point QEF pseudoinverse
with absolute 1e-10 eigenvalue cutoff, 27 active constraint sets. Returns owned
Float64 vertices and analytic unit gradient normals with outward Uint32 triangles; no UVs or materials.
Min/max CSG fields need not be exact distances. No sampled fields, arbitrary
callbacks, rotated primitives, adaptive octrees, topology repair or exact CAD.
Subcell components, multiple edge crossings, tangencies and disconnected patches
inside one cell can be missed or nonmanifold; touching CSG can produce degenerate
triangles. CPU generation is synchronous with pre-abort; worker required in flight.
The independent asset is lazy; output survives real WebGPU/WebGL2 loss and disposal.
Khronos Box (Cesium, CC-BY-4.0) is the external corner/plane/volume/topology reference;
other sphere, CSG, scale and hostile controls are generated stand-ins. No visual,
production-scene, elapsed-time or SIMD claim. Cached edge roots have four cell uses
per solve, a deterministic reduction in root work with identical Hermite data.
Analytic bounds default to tree enclosure plus 10% per-axis margin (at least
0.0001). Explicit bounds retain boundary rejection; automatic bounds outside
coordinate/extent limits give linked failed and request explicit bounds. Updated
entry/asset sizes are recorded with the test-page validation evidence below. Core plus stage is unchanged at 23,837 B gzip, strictly below 25,000 B.

### Batch 76 review corrections (LIM-625, LIM-627, LIM-629)

Root, custom and mask sampling addresses the full capture, using absolute fragment pixels for offset viewports and scissors. Reveal coordinates and custom UVs refer to the full target, not just its viewport. Exact generated spatial-color comparisons cover all four built-in kinds, custom and mask at idle/0/0.5/1, 1x/4x MSAA, and preservation outside a stacked scissor. Evidence: packages/transitions/test/viewport-browser.js. These stand-ins do not establish artistic quality or cross-device behavior.

Custom WGSL must be trusted. Validation checks compilation and the reachable resource interface, not execution work or time; accepted loops can stall a GPU or cause device timeout. The costly-loop regression compiles and disposes without dispatch. User code shares the wrapper module and can read before/after captures and settings (progress, kind index, displacement, zero). Only group 0 bindings 0..2 are exposed: one settings uniform and two read-only textures. Reachable extra texture/sampler/uniform/storage bindings reject before attachment; unused declarations can compile without any extra resources. The interface exposes no host JavaScript, DOM, network, files or other engine buffers. This is no guarantee against browser/driver defects. AbortSignal cancels compilation waiting/attachment only, never attached rendering or GPU execution. Real-compiler boundary regressions are in gpu-browser.js; custom.test.js proves abort after attachment does not detach or stop frames.

Frozen-frame and live output requires a valid normalized or float color render attachment. Supported formats: r8unorm, rg8unorm, rgba8unorm, rgba8unorm-srgb, bgra8unorm, bgra8unorm-srgb, r16float, rg16float, rgba16float, rgb10a2unorm; feature-dependent r8snorm, rg8snorm, rgba8snorm, r16unorm, r16snorm, rg16unorm, rg16snorm, rgba16unorm, rgba16snorm, rg11b10ufloat require enabled WebGPU format capabilities. r32float/rg32float/rgba32float require 1x engine sampling because the 4x path needs resolve support. Output texture shape/usage limits still apply. Live captures remain RGBA8; float output does not recover HDR source data. Integer/depth rejection, unchanged source updates/progress, and baseline normalized/float acceptance are tested in live.test.js and live-browser.js. Capture-side validation shared by built-in/custom/mask is tested in transitions.test.js. See the [WebGPU capability table](https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#plain-color-formats) for device feature requirements.

## Tileable GPU texture baking (LIM-639)

The optional procedural/textures entry compiles one WebGPU compute pipeline and
bakes RGBA8 linear RGB, alpha 1. Native WebGL2 uses a lazy fragment pass on the
source engine canvas, returning an owned WebGLTexture and its gl context; native
WebGPU returns an owned GPUTexture. Neither handle crosses devices/contexts. Five
stylized patterns: periodic value noise, bricks, tiles, longitudinal wood-like
bands and rust-like threshold patches. No photographic, anatomical, corrosion or
PBR material accuracy is asserted. Four fixed noise periods 4,8,16,32, weights
8,4,2,1, quintic interpolation. Every preset shares a caller-set two-colour palette.
Defaults: bricks, 256 square, seed1, repeats[4,8], detail .2, grout .08, stagger .5,
color[.55,.2,.08], secondary[.15,.12,.1], offset[0,0]. Dimensions16..2048 and device
limit; repeats integer1..64, even brick rows; seed uint32; detail/stagger0..1;
grout0...45; RGB0..1; phase +/-1024 reduced modulo1. Repeat affects brick/tile cells
and wood bands, not fixed noise/rust octaves. No mipmaps or analytic antialiasing;
undersampled mortar/noise can alias. Use repeat-addressed sampling. Neighbouring
pixel centres across a repeat boundary are different samples of a periodic field.
Bakes are async and abortable; incomplete resources are released on failure, abort,
disposal or loss. A replacement device requires a new baker. Outputs are owned;
baker disposal destroys retained outputs. No CPU pixel loop or Wasm is involved.
44,415 GPU channel checks match an independent generated oracle within one RGBA8
quantization step. Integer phase translations are byte exact; one-texel shifts
cross both texture edges. Real WebGPU loss, in-flight abort/disposal and replacement
are tested. Native WebGL2 pixel/state/abort/disposal/loss/restoration tests use
the same one-channel-step tolerance. Mortar on an exact floating-point threshold
can differ across rasterizers. Numerical and lifecycle controls are stand-ins. External reference is
limited to a calibrated row-offset measurement from Lefebvre/Poulin 2000 Fig.1(d),
39/88 pitch with two source pixels of uncertainty, plus GPU raster quantization.
Original PDF/JPEG downloaded for measurement, never redistributed. No external
colour reconstruction, wood/rust realism, cross-device bytes or speed claim.
The WebGL2 shader chunk is lazy; no Wasm or external image asset is required.
Updated entry sizes are recorded with the test-page validation evidence below.

### Spectral transport and chromatic lens (batch 99 job 8, LIM-641)

Optional voxel-pathtracer/spectral traces one RGB path, then importance-samples one hero wavelength
in 380-780 nm only at the first dispersive glass interface or active chromatic camera lens.
Earlier contributions stay RGB, and a path without dispersion has no spectral colour noise. It scales dielectric
transmission by the squared incident/transmitted index ratio, retaining separate light-PDF Jacobians.
RGB coefficients remain RGB; the CIE weights do not reconstruct reflectance or emission spectra.
Captures with wavelength set are monochromatic with unit RGB weight; Albedo, normal and depth use hero samples; instance/palette IDs remain centre-ray values. Transparent alpha averages geometric coverage uniformly over wavelengths, or uses the fixed capture wavelength.

Lens settings are immutable at attachment: lensAbbe 0 or 5-200 (default 0), focalLength 1e-6-1e6 world
units (default 0.05). Only camera projection with nonzero aperture uses longitudinal chromatic power.
There is no lateral colour, physical lens stack, diffraction, lens transmission or measured optical
fidelity. Slope correction permits virtual/infinite wavelength focus without singular division.
One sample uses one traversal; no equal-cost convergence or speed claim. The spectralTransport factory
combines this entry with the other optional tracing features through /compose. Root glass and sampling limitations still apply.

Generated stand-in analytic transport and disk-edge tests run on native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility;
plain WebGL2 gives linked unsupported. The spectral transport repair measured 1083 B gzip (previously 1541 B);
its composition factory brings the current entry to 1215 B (unchanged ceiling 1797 B), with inherited root 81091 B gzip. Core plus stage stays 23924 B gzip, under 25,000 B.

## Rectangular building grammar (LIM-642)

Optional procedural/buildings: fixed footprint/floor/component/repeat/window/roof
productions for an oriented rectangle. It is not a general CGA grammar interpreter.
Width/depth .1..1000 m, origin +/-10000 m, yaw +/-2pi; 1..64 floors, heights .1..100 m,
sum<=5000; bayWidth .1..1000 m, ceil(length/bayWidth) equal bays, <=256 per side and
4096 total. Window fractions .05...95. Flat roof or Z-running gable, rise .1..100 m.
Owned Float64 positions, Float32 normals, Uint32 indices and triangle materials.
No arbitrary/concave footprints, recursive custom rules, occlusion, doors, internal
slabs, thickness, UVs or collision mesh. Flush panes partition exterior wall rings.
Face-separated vertices and T junctions form a visual shell, not a welded manifold
solid; downstream solid processing must weld/subdivide first. GPU-independent lazy
Rust/Wasm, abort before synchronous work; dispose releases instance, outputs survive.
Actual WebGPU/WebGL2 value assertions and real loss; Montreal CityJSON measurements
prove envelope dimensions only, not source footprint/facade reconstruction. Remaining
controls are STAND-IN. Shared scope uses2 trig calls versus2 per output vertex, exact
paired coordinate oracle; no elapsed-time/SIMD or production-city claim.
JS 1502 B gzip, ceiling 1758 B; buildings.wasm 31252 B raw / 12794 B gzip.
Core plus stage stays23837 B gzip, strictly below25000 B.

### Any-up staging receivers (batch 56, job 6)

This supersedes the Y-up receiver restriction in earlier batch-56 entries. ContactShadows and AccumulatedShadows accept any finite nonzero up direction and normalize it before GPU upload. Width is projected X unless abs(normal.x) >= 0.9, when projected Z is used; depth is width cross normal. Accumulation's default light is world 8 * normalized up; custom world light positions must clear the caster height along that normal. Existing dimensions, sample and raster precision bounds remain. ### Height-aware grass interaction (batch 77 jobs 3 and 4)

Interactor radius is a sphere in world units, tested at each push-field cell's
bilinearly sampled heightmap height plus the scatter centre Y. Airborne spheres
that miss the surface add no push. The field still stores horizontal vectors,
interpolated at roots, over a camera-centred square; overhangs and multiple
surfaces at one XZ are outside this heightfield representation. Ground sampling
adds four textureLoad reads per field cell; each interactor upload is 32 bytes.
An explosion is a one-frame stamp; existing pushes recover with the usual rate.
The terrain chunks README example holds 16 chunks with 1,024 clumps each and
7/3/1-blade LOD meshes. It makes no huge-area or frame-rate claim.

## Optional Wasm erosion grid

`biomes/erosion-wasm` accepts at most 4,194,304 cells with heights within
+/-33,554,432 mm and spacing 1..1,048,576 mm. It preserves all JS erosion
defaults and exact output. The old JS entry remains capped at 2,097,152 cells.
The Rust module uses Wasm SIMD and no GPU, so WebGL2 uses the same CPU route.
On the pinned unresampled 2048x2048 real DEM, 32 rounds match all five JS output
array SHA-256 hashes and outflow exactly. A fresh integrated instance reports
156,827,648 B linear-memory high water. Including caller input and owned output
requires 244,908,032 B of backing storage, excluding JS object/allocator overhead.
Kernel array reuse eliminates 41,943,040 B of allocations, while input/readback
add 88,080,384 B relative to running directly in JS. This is not a whole-process
memory or elapsed-speed win. Final differences use 1,048,576 four-lane SIMD blocks.

31,905 B raw / 13,036 B gzip lazy asset. Existing erosion entry:
3,014 B, below its unchanged 3,202 B ceiling; biome root 16,516 / 16,819 B.

## Optional RT alpha limits

`bvh/alpha-triangles` preserves original face TEXCOORD_0/material provenance;
`shadows/rt-alpha` snapshots those data into one storage buffer. Five fragment
storage buffers are required, versus four for ordinary RT. WebGL2 and lower
WebGPU tiers use the existing map fallback. Storage costs 16 + 32*faces +
64*masks bytes plus each mask's alpha pixels padded to four bytes, with masks
deduplicated by identity. CPU images must be below 256 MiB and within the device's
buffer limits; each dimension is an integer 1..1,048,576. UV/transform values must
be finite float32; factor/cutoff are 0..1. Four times each masked face's absolute
affine UV bound must fit float32, including the offset, to prevent intermediate
overflow. Repack after UV/material/topology edits.
Core geometry is opaque; model skin/morph positions are bind pose. Unsupported
images/UV sets are reported by modelAlphaMasks.skipped and retain its opaque
policy. The real-GPU traversal/fragment and public Shadows.attach pixel proofs
pass for default/quarter-turn masks, restoration and fallback. RT far ends at
the configured distance; the map fallback instead uses the map's full reach.
Measured gzip entries: bvh root 23,362 / 23,398 B ceiling, bvh/gpu
5,582 / 5,738 B, bvh/alpha 16,513 / 16,873 B, shadows/rt 6,409 / 6,486 B.
New alpha-triangles is 1,125 B (1,381 B ceiling); rt-alpha is 8,739 B
(8,816 B ceiling). No existing ceiling rises. Core plus stage remains 23,924 B.

## Batch 234 FFT ocean

The optional water `/fft` entry uses 16..512 Fourier samples per axis (powers
of two), 1..4 disjoint wavelength bands and a separate 1..1024-cell draw grid.
Its Gaussian linear Phillips/JONSWAP spectra use deep-water gravity dispersion,
periodic patches, choppy displacement, tangent normals and folding foam. DC
and the Nyquist row/column are omitted. Finite-depth dispersion, overturning
volumes and shoreline flow are not solved by this entry. Its square draw grid
is finite and follows the camera by default. A requested CPU snapshot is of
the last rendered frame; rendering never reads the GPU back. One read can be
pending. All buffers are rebuilt on device restoration. Details, size evidence
and correctness reproduction: [water-fft.md](water-fft.md).

is unchanged at 23,924 B in the full rebuilt measurement. Snapshot time,

### Save factory ownership

Save's optional engine entry scopes synchronous factory attachment, state loading
and compensation to the selected scene. It uses the actual engine and public
scene setup; core/stage are unchanged. Rollback removes newly attached plugins
and helpers in reverse order only while their instance is still registered.
Factories own their resources, and arbitrary binding side effects beyond saved
state need their own compensation. No new asynchronous factory API or isolation
from binding callbacks is claimed. The standard Save/check:merge unit suite

## Triangle-mesh lightmaps (batch 54)

`bakeMeshLightmap` (`@margoengine/lightmap/mesh`) bakes on the CPU, one mesh per call, at most 2,048 x 2,048 texels,
4,194,304 covered texels and 67,108,864 rays. Light is direct (with shadows) and AO; bounces, area and emissive lights
are in `./global` for quads only. Overlapping UV charts are counted (`overlaps`), not separated: the later triangle's
light is kept where both centres fall. Dilation averages neighbours across a gutter narrower than twice `dilate`, so
two charts closer than that blend in the gutter (never inside a chart). Overlaps under 1e-3 texels count as touching.

## Directional lightmaps (batch 54)

`bakeDirectionalLightmap` (`@margoengine/lightmap/directional`) stores one main light direction and one directional
colour per texel (world space), not SH or the H-basis: with several lights it is exact only at the unmapped normal and
approximate under a normal map (exact for one light plus ambient). Ambient light and AO are not directional. It takes
the `bakeMeshLightmap` limits and its direct-light-only scope; bounce light has no direction. The RGBA8 direction map
quantizes each component to 1/255 of 2. No GPU shader applies it yet: `directionalIrradiance` is the CPU reference.

## Lightmap rough glass, dispersion and bounce caustics (batch 54)

`bakeRefractedLightmap` (`@margoengine/lightmap/refracted`) rough glass is single-scattering: light the microsurface would
scatter again is dropped into `diagnostics.masked` (about 9% of a normal beam through a 1-unit slab at roughness 0.5,
53% at roughness 0.9), so very rough glass is too dark. Roughness is isotropic and per volume. Dispersion uses Cauchy's
two-term fit (no Sellmeier), wavelengths 380 to 780 nm with out-of-gamut colours clipped, and the event Fresnel at one
wavelength per photon. Bounces (at most 4) are diffuse and use the quad's albedo only (no `surface` callback, no
textures); receivers stay opaque.

## Lightmap irradiance probes (batch 54)

`bakeLightProbes` (`@margoengine/lightmap/probes`) bakes on the CPU, at most 64 probes per axis (262,144) and 67,108,864
rays, 16 to 16,384 gather rays per probe. Each probe is order-3 SH, so a strong light rings: a delta light gives about
6% of its irradiance straight behind it and 9% at 90 degrees, and `probeIrradiance` clamps below 0. The room's light
reaches probes only through its lightmap (one mesh), so one bounce beyond the lightmap; occluders reflect nothing;
emissive surfaces and area lights are not sampled. Probes have no visibility weighting (light can leak through thin
walls between probes), and `@margoengine/environment`'s `LightProbes` cannot load the baked coefficients yet.

## Lightmap denoising (batch 54)

`@margoengine/lightmap/denoise` runs on the CPU, at most 16,777,216 texels (8,192 a side) per call, 1 to 8 a-trous
passes of 25 taps each. It is not energy conserving (a weighted mean per texel, as Dammertz et al. 2010 note). Charts
are filtered separately: neighbouring quads in the world are not neighbours in the atlas, so quad charts a few texels
wide get little smoothing. Without a supplied `variance` the noise is estimated per texel from its neighbours (median
absolute deviation); smooth gradients count partly as noise and are smoothed slightly, and a lone bright texel (a
firefly) is averaged into its neighbours but not clamped. The quad atlas path reads the 8-bit lightmap, so its input
carries 8-bit quantisation; the mesh path reads the float `irradiance`.

## Path-traced lightmap bounces (batch 54)

`bakeGlobalLightmap({ bounceMode: 'path' })` traces at most 8 diffuse bounces, `bounceRays` (1 to 32) paths per texel,
on the CPU, within `maxRays`. Each path vertex reads the direct light of the texel it hits, at that texel's centre, so
light varying inside one texel is averaged (texel-sized bias); there is no Russian roulette (paths stop at `bounces`),
no glossy or metallic bounce (metals reflect nothing) and no light through glass on bounce paths. Quad charts are the
only input: triangle meshes (`./mesh`) have no bounces yet.
