### Tile styling (batch 239 job 1)

`@margoengine/tiles/style` supplies `TilesStyle`: property expressions drive sRGB RGBA, show and pixel point size, with ordered conditions, defines and metadata expressions. The language supports scalar/vector math, comparisons, short circuiting, ternaries, arrays, property paths, interpolation, CSS colours and regular expressions. Expressions are limited to 65,536 characters, 4,096 tokens and 128 parser nesting levels. Wrong output types fail with a coded state error. No arbitrary host methods or JavaScript execution are allowed.

`TilesStyle.decorate` is the renderer's optional `decorate` hook; it binds loaded b3dm batch IDs, pnts batch IDs and point semantics, i3dm instance IDs, and structural attribute/implicit feature tables. Direct model, instance and point bindings accept a property resolver, update without accumulating tint, and restore their saved authored data on disposal. Model bindings follow PBRModel.writeGeometry's existing restrictions on deformed/shared geometry. PBR colours multiply authored vertex colours in linear light; point colours replace the cloud's colour channel. Style alpha uses the existing blend path. Property textures and feature ID texture sampling belong to the later batch jobs, rather than being advertised here. No core or stage source changes.

### FSM invoked services (batch 250 job 3)
Optional fsm/invoke adds state-scoped tasks with unique ids. Stable nonfinal states start tasks outermost first; transient states do not start work. Exit aborts before re-entry, including within one macrostep; common ancestors retain their tasks. done.invoke.id carries {output}; error.invoke.id carries {error}. Sync throws are errors. Old results are ignored by identity, never delivered into a newer state entry. invocations retains the latest record per id. settled resolves after delivery or cancellation and exposes handler failures as rejection. An abort cannot stop JavaScript that ignores its signal, but cancellation releases settled and suppresses its late result. Dispose or the optional external signal cancels all work and prevents new tasks/events. No actor spawning or message-receiving service protocol is claimed by this promise-task entry.

### Save OPFS (batch 255 job 3)

The optional save/opfs entry uses a private subdirectory, default margo-saves, and atomically replaces a file at FileSystemWritableFileStream.close. The API needs a secure origin and navigator.storage.getDirectory or an injected private directory; no fallback hides unsupported OPFS. Keys are well-formed nonempty Unicode, at most 175 UTF-8 bytes. Filenames encode keys so slashes cannot escape the namespace. Each value costs five framing bytes. Interrupted first writes leave empty placeholders hidden from reads/keys. Per-key operations serialize per adapter; separate adapters/tabs use the browser's last-close-wins behavior. This is single-key atomicity, not a transaction across keys or a claim of hardware power-loss durability. Abort is checked at filesystem boundaries before the irreversible close; cancellation during close cannot undo a committed write. Native permission, quota and locking failures propagate. ### Signed safe saves (batch 255 job 4)

The optional save/signed entry exposes signedStorage(storage, key, options), returning the full SafeStorage read/write/delete/keys/check interface. It authenticates each complete safe frame including generation under its physical key using WebCrypto HMAC-SHA-256. Raw keys must have at least 32 bytes; CryptoKeys must be secret HMAC/SHA-256 keys of at least 256 bits with sign and verify usages. Raw key bytes are copied, imported lazily, nonextractable, and never written into the save. The caller owns generating, retaining and distributing a secret key; embedded client application keys cannot resist an attacker controlling that client. Authentication detects edits, format changes, role swaps and cross-key copies. It does not encrypt, prevent deletion, or reject replay of an older authenticated frame in the same physical key. Unsigned legacy saves fail closed, including a runtime legacy:true option. A damaged newest copy recovers from an older authenticated one and invokes onRecover; both bad reject with a coded error. Crypto awaits observe AbortSignal before storage writes. The format costs 37 bytes per copy beyond safeStorage's 24 bytes, or 122 bytes of framing across two stored payload copies. The default provider is globalThis.crypto.subtle; options.subtle supports an explicit provider. Existing safe verify/onRecover options apply. README work is owed in docs/work-lists/readme-owed.md.

Save/signed entry: 2,581 B min+gzip (before: absent, 0 B), ceiling 2,837 B, including the safeStorage implementation it composes. Core plus stage stays 23,950 B. Keeping authentication and recovery together avoids a caller accidentally authenticating only payload bytes while trusting an edited generation or copy role.

### SCXML document subset (batch 250 job 5)
Optional fsm/scxml converts definitions to/from MachineDocument. Input supports the W3C SCXML namespace and version 1.0, state hierarchy, explicit/implicit initial states, parallel state regions, one history pseudo-state per state, single-target event transitions, symbolic guards, and named entry/exit hooks. History fallback must match ordinary initial because the native document has one initial field. Cross-region targets, wildcard/list events, executable transition content, arbitrary script/guard expressions, DTDs/entities, final/invoke/eventless constructs and unknown elements/attributes reject. Final/invoke definitions belong to separate optional runtimes, not MachineDocument. Session name/datamodel metadata is accepted but is not saved.
Native extensions in urn:margoengine:fsm:1 are enabled by default on export and retain delay, cross-fade duration, update hook, region history, transition ordering, arbitrary binding/state names and explicit native region boundaries. A parallel holder with separate hierarchical children is outside this subset. extensions:false produces the common standard hierarchy/event/named-hook subset and rejects native-only fields. This is document conversion, not a conforming SCXML processor: Margo retains exact event names, remembered-parent targeting and common-ancestor transition semantics. The importer never evaluates an expression or invokes a hook. Browser DOMParser is the default; Node must supply options.parser, with no new parser runtime dependency.
Input/output limit: 1 MiB UTF-8; 10,000 XML elements; 128 XML nesting levels; export preflight limits native region nesting to 64 and rejects cycles. Plain XML ids use the ASCII identifier subset; arbitrary native names use generated ids plus namespaced names. XML 1.0 forbidden characters reject. Shared region definition objects are valid; cycles are not.

Optional controls/presentation exports PresentationControls, ScrollArea, ScrollControls, PathControls and MotionPathControls (alias). Presentation rotates one live mesh relative to its starting rotation, defaults to product-only picking (global=false), polar [-PI/2,PI/2], unbounded azimuth, speed=1, zoom=1, snap=false. The optional tween peer is required for this entry's spring API; other entries do not load it.

ScrollArea owns a native overlay scroller and HTML content slot. Defaults pages=1, distance=1, horizontal=false, prepend=false. ScrollControls accepts that element or an application scroller, with equivalent page/distance defaults for a wheel-only surface. Defaults damping=0.2 seconds, maxSpeed=Infinity, eps=0.00001, infinite=false. Native scroll uses actual overflow; wheel fallback uses configured viewport pages. Infinite native scroll recentres at the ends without changing continuous progress. Offset is normalized, delta is signed per-update progress; range/curve/visible use normalized intervals. Native keyboard/touch scrolling stays with the browser.

PathControls drives the camera or an explicitly selected engine mesh, optionally from ScrollControls. A curve implements at(t), optionally length/atDistance for arc-length sampling (Margo Spline fits directly). Defaults loop=true, offset=0, damping=0.1 seconds, focusDamping=0.1 seconds, maxSpeed=Infinity, lookAhead=0.001. Focus is a world point or live mesh; otherwise the view follows the path tangent, including the final non-looping endpoint. Zero-length tangents use -Z, vertical views use +Z up. Points must be finite. Mesh positions use the full inverse parent matrix; orientation removes the parent's rotation and does not model shear from a nonuniform scaled/rotated parent. All classes dispose their owned listeners/plugins; ScrollArea removes only owned DOM. Applications dispose controls before removing the scroll area.

Each operation owns a driver and a promise allocated on creation. No automatic clock; cancelled values remain where last written. Group waits snapshot active work; retain a task to await its removed result. Timeline replay creates a new promise. Rejections must be observed by callers.

### Tween property entry (batch 215 job 2)

New tween/props entry: 3223 B gzip from 0 B. Numeric writable object/vector properties only; destination lists are explicit starts and evenly spaced keys. Frame lists support ordered offsets and segment easing; missing properties hold the preceding key. Relative +=, -=, *= and /= values resolve against preceding endpoints. from/fromTo and explicit keys render their first values immediately. Caller supplies update deltas; local speed defaults to 1. Rejections must be observed. Core/stage unchanged.

### Full tween timeline (batch 215 job 3)

New tween/timeline entry: 3184 B gzip from 0 B. A separate Timeline class holds scalar, array, custom, path and nested timelines. Local speeds are finite > 0 (default 1), repeats integers >= 0 or Infinity, yoyo false. Attached children have one owning parent; their clocks are sampled by that parent. Calls/completions run on playback crossings and never on seek. Nested durations include repeats and divide by child speed. Infinite children make a parent endless; an endless zero-duration repeat rejects. Cancellation freezes the tree, rejects observed finished promises, and preserves signal.reason. Callback errors propagate and reject the owner. Core/stage unchanged.

### Tween control world (batch 215 job 4)

Optional tween/control: 3714 B gzip (previously 0 B). TweenControl is an explicit world, with global timeScale 1 by default and no module-global state. Local speed defaults to 1; either speed may be zero to hold even instantaneous work. overwrite defaults to auto (matching keys, including delayed/paused work), all kills every target key, false coexists. Partial kills preserve surviving channels and their original clock. Whole removal rejects the group's promise; repeats/completions notify once per group. New requests validate before overwrite.

### Scroll pin entry (batch 215 job 5)

New tween/scroll-pin: 2105 B gzip, previously 0 B. pinTimeline accepts a positive finite-duration seekable animation, root or optional timeline. Vertical window/element sources; one viewport distance by default, natural section start, pinSpacing true. Numeric start/distance may be refreshed by functions. Snap is disabled by default; labels (or directional labels), intervals, lists and custom functions select normalized progress. Idle delay 0.2 s, snap duration 0.25 s and scrub 0 s. Root timelines supply a labels map; the optional full timeline supplies labelTimes. Interval stops use constant storage regardless of interval size. No playback callbacks fire on scrubbing. Disposal restores DOM and styles.

### Tween inertia (batch 215 job 6)

New tween/inertia: 2778 B gzip from 0 B. Caller supplies release velocity or a VelocityTracker; sample/release times are seconds. The tracker defaults to a 0.1 s window and 32 samples, with configurable capacity 2..1024; stale release returns zero. Resistance defaults to 6 per second. Endpoints may be numeric, nearest lists or functions of the predicted end; optional min/max bound the selected endpoint. Hard ranges are default; bounce in [0,1) opts into spring overshoot. Rest thresholds are 0.01 units/s and 0.001 units; after maxDuration (default 10 simulated seconds) the exact end is written. Local speed 1 by default, with pause/play and AbortSignal. No wall clock or frame loop starts automatically. Observe cancellation promises. Core/stage unchanged.
Batch 253 vector input: optional input/vector provides VectorInput and wasd. Each vector owns scalar channels <name>.x and <name>.y, which contexts, rebinding and recordings use. Positive y is down. Axes sum and clamp individually, then one radial deadzone (default 0.15) rescales magnitude to [0,1]. normalize defaults false; true gives unit magnitude beyond the deadzone. Diagonals always stay in the unit circle. Additional scalar actions share the same Input; gamepad axes have no axial deadzone in VectorInput. No core/stage change or GPU code. Physical-device feel remains hardware-dependent.

Optional controls/device-orientation exports DeviceOrientationControls and deviceOrientationQuaternion. ### Batch 171 atmosphere on the globe

The new optional sciviz/atmosphere entry composes geo's WGS84 globe with sky/planet's existing Hillaire RGB medium. Importing sciviz root, geo, grids or flow without atmosphere adds no sky dependency to the runtime graph. A GPUDevice is required: WebGPU and webgl2-compat, not the separate native WebGL2 sciviz driver. Perspective cameras only; the observer must remain outside the ellipsoid. Figure model inversion handles arbitrary nonsingular data-to-scene affine transforms.

Data positions use longitude/latitude degrees and geodetic metres above WGS84. Scalar triangle values/masks are retained; points are tangent-disc glyphs with a physical radius (default 10000 m, maximum 1000000 m). Geographic wind uses east/north/up m/s and seconds, converted once at input samples by WGS84 curvature to degree/degree/metre rates. The existing GPU RK4, temporal/spatial interpolation, seeding, trails, respawn and replay remain unchanged. Grid latitudes exclude the exact poles; longitude width is at most 360 degrees, with boundary respawn instead of implicit periodic interpolation. No per-frame CPU particle readback. Linear interpolation of the converted angular field is an approximation to interpolation of local physical vectors.

The medium stretches the polar coordinate by 1/(1-f), mapping the exact WGS84 ground to the sphere used by Hillaire. Transport distances and geodetic normal heights change by at most 0.3365 percent, and phase/solar angles are correspondingly approximated. Geometry is not stretched. Tile chord fragments use the reference ground radius for lighting/transport, avoiding underground integration. This is not exact ellipsoidal, spectral or weather radiative transfer. Data-fragment transport uses 24 steps; background uses 32; existing transmittance/multiple-scattering tables retain their resolutions and method. Radii are at most 100000 km and vertical scattering depth at most 6; exposure -20..20, top-of-atmosphere illuminance 0..1000000 (default 20).

Optional clouds accept geographic shell triangles and scalar density clamped to [0,1], including NaN as empty. They are solar-lit data shells with aerial transport; no inferred cloud thickness, volumetric self-shadow or shadow map. Transparent layers retain the renderer's layer sorting. Globe owns its returned layers until disposed; individually removed layers may retain their CPU records until that owner is disposed. The data coordinates remain inspectable through the supplied arrays and existing layer APIs.

The official NOAA demo uses the hash-pinned public-domain wind.bin. Sigma 0.995 is not a height. Wind at 20000 m, speed colours at 1000 m and reference glyphs at 100000 m are explicitly labelled display placements, not measured atmospheric altitudes. See examples/assets/sciviz/atmosphere.json. No speed assertion, benchmark or core/stage source change.

## Batch 258 image scope

ImageTexture copies straight-alpha RGBA8 sRGB pixels, decodes browser images with AbortSignal, and snapshots canvas/image/video sources. Images default to contain, centered in the content box; cover crops and fill stretches. Source is an integer pixel atlas cell. Nine-slice borders are source pixels times borderScale (default 1); they override fit and shrink uniformly if the target cannot fit both borders. Tint defaults to opaque white. No GPU objects are exposed or borrowed from core.

Cells are cached as 60-pixel tiles with a one-texel neighbor gutter per side. Filter footprints clamp at cell boundaries, and alpha is premultiplied before filtering. UI's colour atlas controls total residency: default 512-square pages, 16 pages; increase colorAtlasSize/maxPages for more images. Its configured atlas limits still throw when exhausted. Source pixel buffers and cached tiles are CPU memory retained with ImageTexture. Dropping it releases unreferenced source storage; tiles already admitted to a renderer atlas remain until atlas eviction or renderer disposal. Edits use a new ImageTexture. Raw preview GL retains its existing encoded-space compositing; complete compatibility follows the WebGPU path. No speed claim or GPU render-target input is made.

Batch 257 job 1, worker/rpc: cloneable arguments/results only, with explicit transfer lists for input and output. A pool owns its workers; a standalone client owns only its subscriptions. Queue default 1024, size default 2, deadline default 30000 ms including queue time. Structured-clone failures are returned as errors. No core/stage changes.

AudioVoiceManager has maxVoices=32 (integer >=0) and linear threshold=0.0001. add(sound,{priority=0,gain=()=>1}) returns a managed transport. All registered decoded-buffer sounds on one listener share the cap, including global, stereo and positional sounds. Larger finite priority wins, then volume/fade/master/distance/cone/custom gain; ties retain registration order. Each frame updates managed poses before ranking. ### Stats geometry entry

`@margoengine/stats/geometry` provides GeometryStats, attach/beginFrame/track/trackDevice/trackGL/pipeline/view/toJSON/dispose. The geometry row and optional third statsReport argument expose triangles, submitted vertices, instances, drawCalls and unknownDraws. Indexed vertices include repetitions; instance totals sum non-empty draw submissions rather than unique scene objects. Triangle strips/fans count assembled candidates before restart markers, degeneracy, clipping or culling. Existing WebGPU pipelines default to triangle-list unless registered with pipeline(); future tracked device pipelines retain their topology. GPU-written indirect data and render bundles are opaque: supply the indirect CPU metadata callback where available; otherwise unknownDraws reports missing observations without inventing counts. Native methods still run with their original receivers. Multiple engine views in the same task accumulate; custom loops call beginFrame explicitly. No core or stage change. Entry: 1,568 B gzip, new ceiling 1,824 B. Root: 4,861 B; report: 1,165 B; combined core + stage: 23,950 B.
@margoengine/input/haptics: 945 B gzip (previously absent), ceiling 1201 B. Cohesive lifecycle retained; no separate fragment entry. Core and stage unchanged.

Batch 253 trigger rumble: optional input/haptics exports triggerRumble, supportsTriggerRumble and structural effect/actuator/gamepad/options types. Pass a native Gamepad (including an XR source gamepad) or adapter. Defaults: duration 100 ms, startDelay 0, leftTrigger/rightTrigger 1, strongMagnitude/weakMagnitude 0, timeout 6000 ms. Durations are nonnegative safe integers; intensities are finite [0,1]; timeout is positive and at most 2147483647 ms. Browsers can cap native durations, commonly at the spec-recommended five seconds. Increase timeout for longer effects. Capability returns undefined for old actuators without an effects list; playback probes them once. Return true means native complete; false means unsupported/disconnected or preempted. Permission/device failures propagate. Abort/timeout stops only the latest call through this entry on the actuator; stop has a separate 1000 ms bound. Stop failure throws AggregateError containing the original reason and stop failure. Without reset, a zero trigger effect stops playback. This entry cannot coordinate effects started externally through other APIs. Physical controller support, visibility/permissions policy and actual trigger motor response remain browser/device-dependent and require hardware acceptance.
- XR skinned hands require all 25 named joint nodes in one glTF skin. Default names are the WebXR joint names; custom names are explicit. Both hands use separate caller-owned models, preserving authored mirroring, hierarchy, inverse binds and weights. Joint transforms are reference-space world poses. Parent transforms must be invertible and yield decomposable local TRS; use uniform model-root scale. No model URLs are fetched implicitly. Animation is loaded lazily. Partial tracking hides the whole hand; dispose restores borrowed transforms. Physical-device validation remains job 1's hardware gap.

- xr/hands: 0 to 2290 B gzip, ceiling 2546 B for the new optional 25-joint skinned hand entry. Core + stage remains 23950 B.

### Batch 254 audio sprites and codec fallback
Optional @margoengine/audio/sprites: 1508 B minified gzip, new entry from 0 B. AudioSpriteBank snapshots named intervals in buffer seconds, offset>=0 and duration>0 wholly within the decoded buffer, loop=false by default. create(name,options) returns a stopped Audio; play(name,options,delay=0) starts an overlapping instance. Every instance shares the original buffer and uses native offset/duration or bounded loop points. Natural ends call the supplied callback and dispose that instance; explicit pause/stop retains it until caller/bank disposal. Bank stopAll preserves the map; dispose/using/listener teardown release owned sounds, never the shared buffer. loadAudioFallback accepts ordered URL strings with recognized extensions or {url,type} candidates with explicit MIME/codec declarations. maybe/probably are eligible in list order. Unsupported types are skipped; each supported resource is fetched/decoded once, trying the next after failure. Abort stops the operation. Exhaustion raises linked failed with AggregateError in cause, or unsupported when no candidate is eligible. In workers pass canPlayType; the default lazily creates an audio element. LoadAudioOptions are forwarded, including signal, cache and custom fetch. canPlayType is advisory and cannot guarantee decode support, multichannel containers or gapless compressed boundaries. Sample-accurate boundaries are verified on decoded WAV PCM; lossy encoder padding needs authored sprite bounds. No core/stage change.
Batch 257 job 3 supersedes the earlier worker pointer-lock gap: WorkerCanvas and ReceivedCanvas expose pointerLocked, requestPointerLock and exitPointerLock. The forwarded worker canvas also supplies the document-shaped pointer-lock members needed by PointerLockControls, with unchanged movementX/movementY counts. Requests must follow browser user-activation/permission policy; a forwarded trusted page interaction can request lock, or the page can request directly in its gesture. Defaults: unadjustedMovement false, timeout 10000 ms, no AbortSignal. Abort/deadline end the wait; the browser offers no native cancellation of a permission request. Raw-input denial is reported, never silently retried. Lock-change/error events and document mouse movement are forwarded; disposal releases only this canvas lock and clears worker state.

### Stats WebGL2 timer entry

`@margoengine/stats/gl` provides GLStats. Custom loops call beginFrame(gl), beginPass/endPass or pass(name, work), endFrame, then poll from a later task. Engine attach wraps the existing graph execution and main draw; attach before other plugins to time their newly registered named passes. Existing custom passes can use pass(name, work) explicitly. Views in one task accumulate into one frame closed in a microtask. Frame milliseconds sum non-overlapping elapsed GPU segments, including gaps between passes; they exclude presentation and pre-graph CPU/update work. Named intervals do not include the gap intervals. TIME_ELAPSED queries never nest. Defaults: maxPasses 128 (1..128), maxPendingFrames 4 (1..8); overfull/backlogged samples are dropped, counters continue, and disjoint/invalid/lost samples clear GPU timings. Unsupported contexts retain draw counts and show unavailable. An already-active application elapsed query causes the profiler to omit that frame. Do not start another elapsed profiler inside an instrumented frame. Context restoration reacquires the extension. view, toJSON and Symbol.dispose are supported. New optional entry: 2,281 B gzip, ceiling 2,537 B; Stats root and combined core/stage remain unchanged.
- XR AR extras require the native module requested before entering AR. Current image targets use marker-tracking/getImageTrackability; set legacy explicitly for image-tracking/getImageTrackingScores. Snapshots copy poses and mesh geometry, but geometry arrays are reused until native lastChangedTime or label changes. Null poses hide displays. DOM overlay and ImageBitmap roots remain caller-owned. Persistent handles belong to the origin/browser, survive tracker disposal, and are deleted only explicitly or when an aborted save created a new unclaimed handle. Native anchor save/restore operations cannot be canceled: abort is checked before and after their settlement so cleanup can complete. No cross-device/cloud anchor transfer or invented tracking fallback is provided. Device permissions and tracking accuracy still need real-device validation.

- xr/ar-extra: 0 to 3033 B gzip, ceiling 3289 B for the new optional DOM, image, mesh and persistent anchor entry. Core + stage remains 23950 B.

Queries snapshot pairs and recheck live membership/rows before visits; new pairs wait until the next iteration. Optional source rows use -1. Target with terms are required and their rows flatten in term order. This is direct pair matching; traversal remains in Relation.
ecs/relation-query: 1023 B min+gzip, new optional entry previously 0 B; ceiling 1279 B. Core plus stage unchanged at 23950 B.

Batch 225 job 1: splines/kinds adds catmullRomSpline (centripetal default, chordal/uniform options; closed=false, divisions=256), CubicSpline and analytic splineDerivative (order=1), splineCurvature and splineTorsion. Parameter t is 0..1; derivatives are global-t derivatives, right-hand at joins and periodic at the closed seam. Nonuniform geometry is tangent-continuous but equal per-piece t does not imply matching derivative magnitudes at unequal chord joins. Curvature is NaN at stationary points; torsion is NaN without an osculating plane. Repeated knots give constant zero-span pieces. Returned Bezier controls are editable using the existing points/updateArcLengths contract. Closed CubicSpline requires coincident endpoints. Arc lengths remain sampled. No GPU implementation or GPU tests exist in this CPU-only package; core and stage untouched.

Batch 225 /kinds: new optional entry 0 -> 2802 B gzip (ceiling 0 -> 3058 B); geometry operations belong together to share polynomial calculations. Core + stage remains 23950 B gzip, below 25000 B; root sources untouched.

### Stats panels entry

`@margoengine/stats/panels` provides StatsPanels, attach/sample/refresh/toJSON/dispose, with four chronological fixed Float64Array histories and a named GPU list. Defaults: samples 120 (2..4096), refreshMilliseconds 150 (16..60000), parent document.body; owned panel width 360 CSS pixels within the viewport. Options.stats borrows an already attached Stats without transferring its ownership. CPU milliseconds come from FramePhases work in the frame task, FPS from the rolling Stats interval, GPU from the latest completed asynchronous sample. GPU history therefore holds the latest valid result between readbacks, rather than pretending each frame has a fresh query. WebGPU samples one encoder in 15, at most 128 passes, preserves existing timestampWrites and needs timestamp-query enabled on the device. Pass descriptors supply names, with deterministic render N/compute N fallback names. WebGL2 uses the gl entry's limits and early-registration naming rules. Memory defaults to tracked WebGPU descriptor bytes created after attachment; without WebGPU, performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize is used only where exposed. Those sources are labelled separately, omit driver padding and are not interchangeable. A custom memory callback can supply another byte measurement, or null. Unsupported readings appear as gaps and unavailable text, never zero. Custom loops may supply PanelSample values directly. Sampling does not write DOM; refresh draws and labels the graphs. Disposal removes owned collectors and DOM, and restores a borrowed Stats graph. New entry: 9,895 B gzip, ceiling 10,192 B. Its bytes provide coherent collector ownership and all four graphs on both backends; splitting would require users to assemble and manage the collectors themselves. Root and core/stage are unchanged.

Windows Playwright WebKit 27.2 exposes neither canvas transfer, worker OffscreenCanvas/RAF nor worker graphics contexts. It selected the original page canvas, retained the input buffer and displayed the same centre pixel, then disposed. Its Safari-shaped user agent and Apple GPU renderer string do not establish an Apple host or native Safari support. Both page hardware probes report no WebGPU adapter. The strict full suite therefore fails on the absent WebGPU/worker capabilities; those assertions were not loosened. Apple no longer updates Safari for Windows, and Playwright WebKit is a separate build. Native Safari/macOS hardware proof remains owed in private/handoffs/finish-later.md; job 4 is DONE under Scott's 95% rule.

## WFC tilesets (batch 237)
Optional wfc/tileset expands X, I, backslash, L, T and F into 1, 2, 2, 4, 4 and 8 distinct variants. ### Batch 245 per-sprite blend modes

The optional `@margoengine/sprites/blend` entry exports BlendLayer, BlendSprite, blendBatches and their types. Modes are normal (default), add, multiply and screen; addBlend creates sprites and blendMode is mutable. Ordinary add sprites use normal. Contiguous visible runs share a draw, with original z/y/insertion order retained. Multiply uses two interleaved draws per sprite to keep uncovered source colour on transparent backdrops. No core or stage change. Atlas pages, nearest/linear filtering, mipmaps, camera, masks, view layers, targets, normal output and lifecycle are inherited; custom fragment shaders are excluded from BlendLayerOptions because the entry owns premultiplication and correction.

Blending uses premultiplied colour in the target's blend space. Add sums colour and alpha, clamped by normalized targets; the other modes use source-over alpha. Smooth sRGB targets blend decoded linear colour; nearest keeps the base layer's numeric texels. Render targets contain premultiplied colour. Intermediate RGBA8 multiply rounding is at most one byte in the asserted single-sprite fixtures. No universal accumulation error bound or speed claim is made. The readback fixtures cover 146 cases on each backend, including sRGB/unorm targets, both filters, transparent/partial/opaque backgrounds, three atlas alpha values, mixed runs, nonzero instance starts and overlapping multiply sprites.

Measured gzip after the upstream core-version guard: blend 8208 B (new ceiling 8464 B), sprites root 7480 to 7613 B, slice 8614 to 8760 B; existing root/slice ceilings hold. The blend entry retains the shared renderer rather than copying it or splitting a cohesive operator API. Skeletal is 7436 B after the upstream guard; pick remains 1933 B. Core plus stage is 24209 B, including the guard already on main. This job does not change their source.

Batch 225 job 2: splines/query provides splineBounds, splineExtrema, intersectSplines, intersectSplineRay and intersectSplinePlane. Bounds and extrema solve each cubic analytically; joins are candidates on all axes and constant coordinates have no isolated stationary roots. Plane equation normal dot point + constant = 0; rays use origin + direction * otherT, so otherT is not world distance unless direction is unit length. Results separate isolated points and continuous overlaps. Defaults: tolerance=1e-7 world units, parameterTolerance=1e-7, maxWork=200000 curve-pair nodes. Increasing maxWork or splitting the curves resolves the explicit limit error; no incomplete result is returned. Parameters within parameterTolerance are merged, so reduce it for closely spaced hits. Interval boxes include a machine-roundoff margin, then hits verify spatial residuals; this is floating-point geometry, not symbolic certification. Closed t=0 and t=1 remain distinct parameter endpoints. No GPU state or GPU tests; core/stage unchanged.

Batch 225 /query: new optional entry 0 -> 3614 B gzip (ceiling 0 -> 3870 B); geometry operations belong together to share polynomial calculations. Core + stage remains 24209 B gzip, below 25000 B; root sources untouched.

Batch 225 gate correction: unchanged water root measures 20210 B gzip after main core-version guard, against prior ceiling 20185 B; optional ceiling becomes 20817 B using standard headroom. Version-skew prevention stays intact; no water/core/stage source changed.


Batch 249 reactive: required/excluded shape changes update one entity per query. Cache order is packed. Optional rows resolve on visit. subscribe defaults to future transitions; initial:true immediately visits existing matches. flush delivers chronological queued transitions, including enter then exit in one window, at the caller chosen system boundary; listener mutations wait until next flush. Unsubscribed listeners receive nothing further. stop detaches and clears without exit callbacks. Field writes do not change membership.
ecs/reactive: 1228 B min+gzip, new optional entry previously 0 B; ceiling 1484 B. Core plus stage unchanged at 23950 B. ComponentStore also permits mixed fields in typed query/tracker APIs.

## WFC 3D overlapping (batch 237)
Optional wfc/overlapping3d learns N x N x N patterns from finite-number voxel labels, X fastest, with N 2..5 (default 2). Input wraps by default; identity symmetry is default, with optional four Y turns or 24 cube rotations and reflections (2, 8 or 48 orientations). Sample limit 1,048,576 voxels, pattern limit 4096; nonperiodic source dimensions must still be at least N. Output defaults to nonperiodic, seed 1, four attempts and 10000 backtracks per attempt; dimensions must be at least N unless periodic. Output limit 1,000,000 voxels and 16,777,216 lattice cell/pattern pairs. Voxel pins constrain every covering pattern, including seams and outer corners. Samples and rules are copied. Chronological backtracking never undoes pins; exhausted budgets throw coded failed with help link, and cancellation preserves the exact reason. CPU-only synchronous solving cannot receive event-loop aborts while running; no worker or Wasm backend is claimed for this new model. Arc propagation is generic within the optional entry; neither core nor stage imports it. Hashing overlap slabs avoids pairwise voxel comparisons; no timing gain is claimed. Memory remains proportional to domains, pattern adjacency, and pinned domains.

## Batch 258 forms scope

Select defaults to the first enabled option and opens a modal listbox; disabled options are skipped. RadioGroup defaults to vertical and Tabs to horizontal. Their selected choice is the strip's single tab stop; arrow commands wrap enabled choices. Tabs owns and disposes the supplied content panels and displays one at a time. Programmatic value assignments do not emit change; user selection does. Checkbox reuses the existing complete checkbox toggle implementation.

ColorPicker defaults to opaque white and exposes HSV, RGB and alpha channels normalized to [0,1], a pointer SV square and six/eight-digit hex editing. value is canonical #rrggbbaa; hue survives zero saturation. The SV display is 64 by 64 colour cells, while selected values remain continuous before 8-bit hex output. attachFormsMirror runs after UiRenderer's ordinary mirror; attachTextInputs supplies the hex editor's native editing. Both return disposable detachers and accept AbortSignal. Human assistive-technology certification and a continuous SV shader remain polish follow-ups, not claims of this change.

Angles are radians; Euler.order is required. makeShear(xy,xz,yx,yz,zx,zy) places xy/xz in column X, yx/yz in column Y, zx/zy in column Z. extractRotation normalizes columns independently, leaving zero columns zero, and does not remove shear. ## WFC hex grids (batch 237)
Optional wfc/hex supports axial, odd-r, even-r, odd-q and even-q layouts; six directions E,W,SE,NW,NE,SW, paired by index XOR 1. Eight-face prism rules append +Y,-Y. Storage is column then row then layer, with copied dimensions, rules and optional boolean/0-or-1 masks. Mask holes return Uint16 sentinel 65535 and ignore edges; pins on holes reject. Defaults: axial layout, no wrapping, all cells active, seed 1, four attempts and 10000 backtracks. Periodic row-offset layouts require even height and column-offset layouts even width, preserving reciprocal seams. Up to 4096 tile IDs, 1000000 stored cells, 16777216 cell/tile pairs; at least one layer and eight faces required for multiple layers. Hex socket expansion preserves all six orientations (or identity) plus optional reflected copies, up to 4096 variants; weights split across variants and underflow rejects. hexCellCenter defaults to pointy radius 1 and layer height 1, with flat orientation also available. Search is synchronous CPU with exact pre-abort reasons, coded budget failure and an undo trail; there is no worker or Wasm backend or global-connectivity guarantee for this entry. Neither core nor stage imports it; no timing claim.

### Property attributes and textures (batch 239 job 5)
Optional @margoengine/tiles/properties exposes readPropertyMetadata and loadPropertyMetadata over a loaded GLTFAsset. Root schema and per-primitive associations remain inspectable; PropertyAttributes.get/row read vertices, PropertyTextures.get/row read UVs, and sample reads texture properties from source triangle list/strip/fan indices and barycentric coordinates. It does not translate an optimized/deformed PBR pick triangle back to a source triangle. Attributes support glTF-accessor-sized numeric values, enums and booleans, sparse overlays, interleaving and matrix padding. Schema defaults, raw noData, normalized values and per-binding offset/scale use the existing metadata decoder.
Defaults: 64 MiB per loaded schema/image resource; packed attribute cache cap four times asset.maxBytes. maximumBytes and maximumDecodedBytes override these bounds. Caller-provided PropertyImage is linear, unpremultiplied RGBA8, top row first. The loader uses the existing optional image decoders (their format limits apply); external schema/image requests accept AbortSignal, a custom fetch and baseURL (otherwise asset.baseURL or current page). PNG bytes remain exact despite transparent alpha. A loaded Draco asset's float cache can read ordinary custom attributes, but signed normalized -1 sentinels and UINT32 require original packed bytes through the accessor callback to avoid silent precision loss. Batch 225 job 3: splines/offset exports offsetSplineAt (exact offset point), offsetSpline (cubic approximation plus ranges/maxError/work), reverseSpline (exact geometry and t -> 1-t). Positive distance follows normal cross source tangent; normal defaults to [0,0,1] and can define a lateral offset of a spatial curve whenever transverse to the tangent. Defaults: tolerance=0.001 world units, maxDepth=20 (0..30), maxSegments=16384 (1..333333), maxWork=1000000 interval nodes, divisions=max(256,8*outputPieces) capped at 1000000. The local approximation has a conservative floating-point interval enclosure plus roundoff allowance; formal exact-arithmetic certification is not claimed. maxError excludes bevel joins, whose ranges have equal endpoints. Output t distributes equally over output pieces, so ranges maps it to source t. Closed paths get a closing bevel if needed. Stationary/parallel-normal source points have undefined nonzero offset and reject with singular; zero offset remains valid. Exhausted depth, work or piece budgets reject with limit and no partial result. Raw offsets retain loops/cusps and do not perform outline trimming or Boolean cleanup. Controls are independent copies, closure is preserved by reverse, arc lengths stay sampled. No GPU implementation, GPU tests or core/stage changes.

### BVH parallel construction (batch 221)

Optional bvh/parallel adds buildParallel(source, options). workers defaults to min(8, hardwareConcurrency - 1), at least 1, accepts integers 1..64 and counts leaf workers plus one coordinator. The shallow frontier targets four tasks per requested worker; actual workers are capped by unfinished subtrees. The existing maxDepth, maxLeafTriangles, bins and strategy apply globally. Every numeric build, planning and packing pass runs off the main thread when Worker exists; source normalization/cloning and final result validation still have linear caller-thread costs. No Worker means the existing synchronous builder on the next microtask, with pre-build cancellation only. Worker builds have a finite positive timeoutMs (default 120000, maximum 2147483647). Abort/deadline/error terminates the coordinator and its nested worker pool. No transfer option: caller buffers stay attached and unchanged, including source face order. Source positions must remain stable until completion; later edits plus refit are supported. SharedArrayBuffer permits one shared immutable position snapshot across leaf workers; otherwise each leaf worker retains one cloned position buffer. This fallback uses additional memory proportional to worker count. Subtree indices/results are transferred. Parallel and serial packed topology/index/face arrays are byte-identical in the retained correctness cases. No speed ratio claimed.

CurveSet supports channel count, channel arrays and variadic flat keys; add/remove/clear/clearKeys and clone preserve independent channel ownership. ## Procedural skeleton trees (batch 230)
`@margoengine/procedural/tree-mesh` adds meshTree, generateParametricTree and meshTreeLODs. TreeSkeleton from /trees is accepted directly. Parent-first XYZ nodes become capped, smooth tapered tubes with duplicated UV seams, arc-length V and tangents. Optional radii and architectural orders override the derived support-length radii. Leaf cards are single, crossed double, or three-plane clusters, with UVs and an owned alpha atlas. Material descriptors carry tint, alpha cutoff, two-sided foliage and bark texture settings. Default seed 1, species oak, recursive levels 2; seven species are available. All per-order defaults and bounds are in the emitted API comments.
Limits: 16384 nodes, 1 million vertices per output part, 65536 planned leaves, 0..4 recursive orders, 1..64 axial sections, 3..32 radial segments, at most 8 strictly increasing LOD thresholds starting at zero. Degenerate edges, cycles, malformed radii and invalid controls reject with a coded error. Synchronous work checks AbortSignal before execution; use a worker for in-flight cancellation. Root-only skeletons produce empty meshes. Fork surfaces overlap within parent tubes, rather than forming a Boolean-unioned manifold. Procedural 64x64 RGBA bark/leaf atlases are authored patterns, not photographic species reconstructions. Mesh LOD preserves branch endpoints and forks; leaf thinning is deterministic and card enlargement is caller controlled. No core or stage changes, no frame-time generator, no speed claim.
Entry size: tree-mesh is 4420 bytes min+gzip (previously absent, 0 bytes). Its optional size ceiling is 4676 bytes; the bytes contain geometry, validation, presets and material atlases, and splitting them would duplicate settings or add asynchronous boundaries to synchronous meshing.

## Plane sections (batch 224)
The optional @margoengine/mesh-edit/section entry exports splitMeshByPlane, trimMeshByPlane and sliceMesh. Plane normals may have any nonzero finite magnitude; normal dot position = offset uses local units. Inputs are closed consistently wound outward PolygonMesh solids, or empty meshes. Multiple components, concavity and cavities are supported. Outputs own arrays, preserve surviving source face IDs/UV interpolation, identify caps and map source faces. Slice returns an orthonormal basis plus CCW contours and CW holes. Tangent-only contacts return no section area and no zero-volume solid. Source data is never changed. Caps use independent unit-square planar UVs.
Classification/interpolation use float64 with no user tolerance, not an exact-predicate claim; resulting faces must pass the existing mesh validity and closure checks. Numerically unresolved or overflowing configurations reject with rescaling guidance. Existing mesh limits apply (200000 vertices/faces, 3-64 corners); clipped large faces are decomposed. Triangulation adds no cap interior vertices and retains collinear boundary points. Cancellation is cooperative between faces/caps. No timing claim; no core or stage bytes added.
Section entry size: 0 to 5299 gzip bytes, with a 5555-byte quality ceiling. The added bytes provide split, trim, slice, provenance and cavity caps in one optional entry; splitting those APIs would duplicate their shared clipping work. Core plus stage remains 24209 bytes in the package build.
### Batch 226 job 2: scene/clone
cloneSubtree(source,{recursive=true,parent=null}) allocates independent meshes in the source owning scene, optionally under a parent of that scene. Geometry/material references remain shared; disposing either tree retains resources used by the other. Metadata cycles and cross-node aliases remain inside the copy; functions/DOM handles reject before allocation. Listeners, engine plugins and constraints are not cloned. A source-descendant target parent is safe because the source list is snapshotted. Core depth limits remain. Failure cleans all newly allocated nodes. ## Procedural PBR sets (batch 230)
`@margoengine/procedural/textures-pbr` exposes createPBRTextureBaker(device or engine). Its bake returns four owned GPUTextures (albedo, normal, roughness and height), width, heightPixels and mipLevelCount. Defaults: bricks, 256x256, seed 1, full mipmaps, normalStrength 1, heightScale 0.05 UV-tile units, roughness 0.7, roughnessVariation 0.3, time 0. Other shared defaults match /textures, with motif-specific default palettes. All colour values and mip arithmetic are linear; convert albedo during export to a format requiring sRGB encoding. Roughness and height are grayscale RGBA8, normals encode tangent XYZ with green +Y and blue +Z. Use a repeat/trilinear sampler. Fire/cloud are material motifs, not volumetric simulation; animated motifs require rebaking at the chosen explicit time, and fire's radiance uses the albedo as an emissive input supplied by the consuming material.
Dimensions 16..2048 and the device limit; complete NPOT mip chains end at 1x1. Existing repeat/grout/seed/offset limits apply; normalStrength 0..8, heightScale/roughness/variation 0..1, time 0..1e6. Four storage texture outputs are required, matching WebGPU's minimum limit. Each smaller mip covers all source texels with exact area overlap, including odd edges; normal vectors are decoded, area averaged and renormalized. No CPU pixel work or readback in the public implementation. The full WebGL2 compatibility layer runs the same shader API, and preview-only fallback engines must install that layer first. Cancellation/disposal/device loss releases incomplete textures; disposal of the baker releases all retained sets. Recreate the baker after device replacement. Mip normals do not preserve unresolved microfacet variance; no BRDF-equivalent filtering claim is made.
Entry size: textures-pbr is 4946 bytes min+gzip (previously absent, 0 bytes), with a 5202-byte optional ceiling. The bytes keep the coherent field, four-map lifecycle and filtered mip pyramid together; splitting would duplicate settings and resource ownership. Core and stage are unchanged.

Batch 249 parallel: SharedWorld has fixed capacity and numeric/tag fields; object/reference components remain on the main thread. SharedComponent adds one 4-byte-per-slot sparse row table beside existing storage. ParallelSchedule defaults to two workers (1 to 32), a 30000 ms per-system deadline (1 to 2147483647), default export and no implicit accesses. ### UI curved panels (batch 259)
`@margoengine/ui/curved` exports `CurvedPanel` and `layoutPanels`. Import `WorldPanels` from `@margoengine/ui/world-gl` for both backends, or `/world` for native WebGPU. Panel dimensions are arc metres; default cylinder radius 2 m, 64 segments per curved axis (4..512 allowed). Width is less than 2*pi*radius; spherical height is less than pi*radius. ## Batch 210 job 1: animation/mixer
New optional entry: 4158 B min+gzip, ceiling 4414 B, previously absent (0 B). It contains action scheduling, binding and blending together; splitting these would add lifetime coordination and async loading to a small synchronous API. Core/stage source and their 25000 B limit are unchanged.
AnimationMixer accepts an existing Animation, PBRModel (creates and owns an Animation in the model scene), or Skeleton; existing Animation clocks are paused and stay paused on release. Clips may be names/indices on glTF roots, parsed glTF clips, or createKeyframeClip results. Actions cache by clip identity, root and blend mode. Defaults: time=0, timeScale=1, weight=1, enabled=true, paused=false, LoopRepeat, repetitions=Infinity, clampWhenFinished=false. Mixer defaults time=0, timeScale=1. Replacement weights below one retain original properties and above one normalize. Additive clips contain deltas (translation/property offset, unit-relative scale, quaternion delta). Property accessor tracks need get/read so original values can be restored. Warps use rates evaluated at each update endpoint, matching the action contract; no frame-partition invariant integration is claimed.
Fades/warps/crossfades take finite nonnegative seconds; zero applies at the next update. Crossfade schedules envelopes, and callers play the destination action. Roots must have compatible track targets; no automatic retargeting or contact-preserving motion alignment is implied. clipAction supports code property bindings and already-bound pointer channels. Uncache releases bindings; stopping the last action immediately restores originals. update(delta) or engine.use(mixer) drives it; do not also drive a borrowed Animation clock.

The mixer intentionally shares the existing animation root and its transitive gltf-pro/model runtime (recorded dependency allowance), rather than duplicating model/deformation ownership or making synchronous model/action construction asynchronous. The 4158 B entry measurement leaves shared bare package imports external; it is not a standalone all-dependencies download size.

## Batch mesh booleans (batch 224 job 2)
@margoengine/mesh-edit/boolean-batch exports batchBooleanMeshes(meshes, operation = 'union', options = {}). Intersection is n-ary; difference is the first solid minus the union of every later solid. Empty list gives an empty mesh. Empty union/subtraction operands are identities; an empty intersection operand absorbs. Inputs are closed outward consistently wound PolygonMesh solids (empty meshes allowed), up to the existing per-mesh limits and 400000 combined input vertices plus faces. Result faceMap is indexed by operand; sources use original operand index and face ID. Inputs may reuse IDs; surviving faces retain original IDs when unique, with createId (default crypto.randomUUID) for collisions. UVs interpolate from original faces, not intermediate results. Output owns all arrays.
All operands and internal shell unions use one exact space; balanced reductions do not materialize intermediate meshes. Rational corners round once, followed by the existing validity-preserving thin-face fold and junction closure. collapsedFaces and nonManifoldEdges retain binary-exact semantics. work records exactSpaces, materializations and treeBuilds, without elapsed-time claims. AbortSignal is checked during traversal and assembly. Existing limitations on unresolved float64 output and single-surface self-intersection remain. No core/stage bytes are added.
Entry sizes: boolean-batch 0 to 10461 gzip bytes (10775-byte ceiling); binary boolean-exact remains 10308 bytes by the same entry measurement. The combined implementation shares exact clipping and final repair rather than duplicating either. Core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.
### Batch 226 job 3: scene/tags
tags(mesh) is a stable DOM EventTarget TagSet, with add/remove/clear/list/size/has and add/remove/change events. Tags are unique nonempty arbitrary strings, insertion ordered; mutation inputs validate before changes. has/findByTag use OR between arguments, AND within nonempty arrays. matchesTags/queryTags accept !, &&, ||, parentheses, quoted tags and unquoted true/false constants, maximum 16384 characters and 64 nested operators. Quoted true/false remain literal tags. An empty boolean expression matches all; empty has alternatives match nothing. Queries include the supplied root, preserve depth-first attach order and stay in its scene. Clone copies independent tag sets without subscribing copied listeners.

new SceneEvents(engine) explicitly observes successful createMesh/setParent/remove calls on existing and future meshes of that engine, with one active observer per engine. Existing parent relationships are not replayed. added is creation or attachment; removed is detachment from a parent or removal from a scene, parent=null meaning scene root; disposed follows mesh removal. Disposing a parent detaches its children under existing core rules. Subscriptions support mesh/scene filters, once, signal and idempotent unsubscribe. Events are immutable snapshots and synchronous after compound attach/clone commit. Failed clone allocation publishes no transient lifecycle events. Listener exceptions reach engine.onError in a microtask. Dispose/Symbol.dispose removes subscriptions and restores only instance wrappers it still owns; external replacement wrappers are preserved. Calls through method references saved before observation or direct private-store writes cannot be observed. Tag mutation listeners follow native DOM dispatch semantics. ## Batch 265 adaptive performance

The optional @margoengine/react/performance entry exports PerformanceMonitor, AdaptiveDpr, usePerformanceMonitor and PerformanceController. Defaults: 250 ms windows, 10 windows per decision, 0.75 required fraction, factor 1, step 0.1, unlimited direction reversals, fallbackFactor 0. Bounds default to [50,57] FPS, or [50,90] when a measured window exceeds 90 Hz. A 60 Hz presentation can therefore recover quality. FPS is frames divided by summed measured milliseconds; observed refresh is a high window average, not a display capability query. It is cadence, not GPU execution time. A sample prop accepts measured milliseconds or null from an application's collector; default intervals use the monotonic performance clock without the engine's delta cap. Hidden tabs and unsampled demand frames discard incomplete windows. Active slow frames remain measurements. Snapshots retain at most 4096 frame intervals per window while all intervals count toward the average. A direction reversal beyond flipflops fixes the factor at fallbackFactor until reset.

AdaptiveDpr defaults to min 0.5, max 1, pixelated false. Fractions apply to the Canvas's native resolution, not CSS layout. A package-owned target scales scene raster dimensions; native MSAA stays intact. Reduced frames add one full-canvas presentation triangle. Scale 1 returns to the original renderer, allowing exact restored pixels. Multiple holds use the lowest scale and nearest presentation if any requests it. Named Scenes and Canvas views retain their scene, camera, layers, clear and scissor. Explicit offscreen targets and tracked XR eye targets retain their owner's resolution. Picking uses original Canvas view coordinates. Removing the last hold destroys its texture immediately and retains only logical picking until the next Canvas draw; engine disposal always releases the adapter. Resources recreate after device restore. WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer are supported; native preview reports unsupported. No timing or throughput gain is claimed during the build phase.

Adaptive performance size: optional entry 0 -> 5619 B minified gzip, ceiling 5769 B. Keeping measurement, presentation and picking in one optional entry avoids duplicate lifetime and asynchronous render boundaries. Core + stage stays 24209 B on the current main baseline.

Adaptive diagnostics use stable MargoError codes and help links. The final React root is 10259 B gzip, React XR 4159 B; the performance entry above includes coded presentation-owner diagnostics.
Batch 219 job 1: optional geometry/nurbs-edit supports immutable rational curve/surface knot insertion and degree elevation on either surface axis; knot parameters and interior multiplicity/continuity are preserved. Unclamped inputs are restricted to the same active domain with clamped endpoints for elevation. Default insertion/elevation count is 1; zero copies, invalid counts and excess multiplicity reject. Trimming accepts retained UV polygons or closed 2D rational curves, holes and multiple islands; regions outside [0,1] are clipped. Default slices/stacks=32, trimTolerance=0.0001 UV units. Surface tessellation has explicit resolution, no model-space error guarantee. Trim curve sampling inherits the existing 12-level subdivision limit. Polygon intersection snaps to its 2^26 grid and features below two steps may disappear; cell pieces retain separate vertices and normals from their own side of knot creases. Degree elevation uses floating-point homogeneous arithmetic, not symbolic arithmetic. Surface file parsing remains in loaders. New entry absent -> 11646 B gzip, ceiling 11996 B; refinement and trim operations share surface evaluation, clipping and triangulation, so splitting would fragment the editing workflow. ## Mesh repair (batch 224 job 3)
The optional mesh-edit/repair entry exports repairMesh(input, options). Input is a polygon soup with unique nonempty face IDs, xyz vertices and index loops; corner UVs are optional. Defaults: distance 0 (exact duplicates), fillHoles true, maxHoleEdges 256. Up to 200000 input vertices and faces and 4096 corners per input face; output remains within standard PolygonMesh limits. Near welding is non-chaining and keeps the earliest eligible position. Nonfinite positions and invalid-index faces are discarded and named; structural array/ID errors reject. Missing or invalid UV corners reset to [0,0] with diagnostics. Concave/warped polygons split through existing mesh editing rules; unresolved, pinched and degenerate polygons are discarded.
When more than two faces compete for an edge, descending face area then input order select the retained manifold subset. A contradictory orientation constraint removes the encountered conflicting face and reports it. Disconnected vertex fans split identities. Existing hole filling uses triangles, refine false and fair false, so it adds a closure without moving surviving scan vertices; holes above maxHoleEdges stay open and are reported. Nested closed shells orient by solid-angle containment (cavities inward). Self-intersections and intersecting-shell intent are not reconstructed or certified. readyForBoolean checks closed opposing edge incidences and positive volume, followed by the actual solid validator; it is false for empty, open or zero-volume output. It does not promise valid geometric self-intersection behavior for arbitrary damaged scans. Result fields include every removed face/vertex, flipped/filled face, weld/fan counts and source face/vertex maps. Source and output arrays are independent. Cooperative AbortSignal checks bound work between traversal steps; no interactive latency claim.
Repair entry size: 0 to 9631 gzip bytes, with a 9920-byte ceiling. The optional entry includes the established hole filler and topology validation so repair stays complete; splitting them would add API complexity without reducing bytes when closure is needed. Core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.

Source connectivity, offsets, cell types, point/cell/global FIELD data and source cell IDs for every drawn primitive survive. Numeric arrays retain float64 precision; rendering positions remain float32. Structured coordinates are x-fastest; ORIGIN defaults to [0,0,0] and SPACING/ASPECT_RATIO to [1,1,1]. `maxCells` defaults to maxTriangles; existing vertex/triangle bounds remain. `surface: 'outer'` suppresses shared volume faces; `'all'` retains them. Both readers reject inexact 64-bit integer values. Binary native `long` is eight bytes, matching the existing legacy reader. ### Pixel-exact area queries (batch 199 job 3)
`@margoengine/selection/area` exports AreaPicking and AreaPickingOptions. Attach instead of Picking, retaining ordinary pick/pickMany and add(source). `rect({x,y,width,height}, view?, signal?)` accepts CSS pixels and normalizes negative dimensions; `polygon(points, view?, signal?)` accepts 3-4096 finite xy vertices and uses even-odd filling. Only included raster pixel centres count, including fractional CSS/DPR boundaries; empty/fully clipped regions return no hits. Results are unique visible triangle IDs, preserving model, primitive and instance identity, in first raster occurrence order. Each area query owns one cropped r32uint target, one depth32float target and a 256-byte-pitched staging buffer. Default maxPixels is 16777216, additionally bounded by device texture dimensions and maxBufferSize. AbortSignal is checked before queued work and after mapping; pending GPU resources remain alive through completion and are destroyed in finally. Point capture defaults false and may be enabled separately. Concurrent area and ordinary point calls retain separate operations through the engine queue. ## Batch 210 job 2: animation/playback
New optional entry 1817 B min+gzip (previously 0), ceiling 2073 B. It intentionally imports the existing Animation root/model runtime; the reported size leaves shared bare package imports external. Core/stage source stays unchanged, below 25000 B.
Import Animation (alias of PlaybackAnimation) from animation/playback for plain play/pause/seek and existing deformation with loop/finished events, finished promise, loop modes and total traversal counts. Defaults inherit loop=true and speed=1; loopMode defaults LoopRepeat (LoopOnce with loop=false), repetitions=Infinity, timeScale=1, no signal. LoopOnce always uses one traversal. Negative timeScale plays backward; play starts negative-rate clips at their end. Ping-pong counts each traversal. A multi-boundary update emits one loop event with signed loopDelta, while the final boundary emits finished once after the terminal pose.
play renews completion, rejecting an interrupted run with AbortError. dispose and constructor signal abort reject pending completion; waitForFinished accepts independent cancellation without stopping playback. seek accepts nonnegative total seconds, emits no events and resets traversal counting; use play to renew a finished run. Events use on or EventTarget-style listeners; listener signal cancellation is supported. Loop counts must be safe positive integers or Infinity, and boundary jumps must be countable as safe integers. A zero-duration clip finishes once, without an infinite loop.

### Optional CPU occlusion on the full WebGL2 layer

`@margoengine/culling/webgl2` supplies `WebGL2Culling` for opaque core meshes on
both the full WebGL2 layer and native WebGPU. It rebuilds a 128 by 128 CPU depth
buffer each view using actual triangles, then redirects compacted 96-byte rows.
Resolution accepts integers 1 through 2048. It uses no hardware queries, no GPU
readback and no previous-frame visibility. `readCounts()` returns the last view's
counts synchronously. Use one redirect owner per batch. Picking and shadow data
stay complete. Surface-changing core shaders disable occlusion for that frame.
The preview renderer is unsupported. Models and dynamic GPU-only geometry retain
their existing cullers; this entry culls core batches. Near-plane-crossing triangles,
triangle seams and partially covered cells can retain hidden objects. This is
conservative excess drawing, never an excuse to cull visible surfaces. CPU work
scales with occluder triangles and covered software cells; no speed claim is made.

Nonnegative finite HDR RGB is normalized by one scale >=1 into linear RGBA8; row orientation is flipped with the exported UV1. Quantization error is bounded by scale/255 per channel. readLightmap copies RGBA8 data, checks width/height 1..4096 and scale 1..1e20. applyLightmap uses UV1, the free material extension slot, and replaces direct and ambient illumination while preserving material colour, metalness and emission. It owns its texture, restores the previous slot on disposal and rebuilds on device restoration. Existing custom material extensions must be removed first. The three analytic irradiance channels (0.5,1,2) import within quantization bounds; both backends draw (56,56,56) through the existing PBR Neutral display curve, invariant under a large increase in engine light. No Cycles film/BSDF or speed equivalence claim.
Batch 219 job 3: optional geometry/teapot exports teapotGeometry(size=1,segments=10,options={}). Y-up, centered, size is the half-height with familiar Blinn proportions. Positive size must remain representable after scaling into Float32 positions; overflow and complete underflow reject. segments is an integer 2..175, keeping all 32 patch grids below core's million-vertex limit. options.body/lid/bottom default true; body includes handle and spout. fitLid=true expands the lid horizontally by 14/13 to meet the inner rim; blinn=true uses the familiar historical squashed shape, false restores 4/3 height. UVs cover [0,1] per patch, normals use analytic derivatives and inverse-transpose scaling, and degenerate pole normals sample derivatives 0.000001 inward. Material indices are body=0,lid=1,bottom=2. Cusp triangles are omitted; the full shape has 32*(segments+1)^2 vertices and 64*segments^2-8*segments triangles. The historical model retains intersecting handle/spout/body surfaces and a separate lid, without a solid interior. Very coarse tip/knob facet chords can oppose exact corner normals because of high curvature; default and dense resolutions agree at every corner. New entry 0 -> 2339 B min+gzip, ceiling 2595 B; model data, validation, parts and shared patch evaluation belong together rather than duplicating the evaluator across part entries. Core + stage remains 24209 B. The margoengine/geometry/teapot alias is generated from the same entry.

The optional objects entry draws all map layers in map order, cells in renderOrder (orthogonal) or geometric painter order, and objects by stable y or explicit index. Collection images retain native dimensions, animation and flip bits. Tile-object size, anchor, rotation and scaled tileset offset are respected. Image layers support either-axis repeat, offsets, parallax, tint and opacity. Text and non-tile objects remain data. ### Headless GIF and exporter palette (batch 209)
Entry bytes (min+gzip, bare package imports external): headless/gif 118 B (new, ceiling 374 B), exporters/palette 2,597 B (new, ceiling 2,853 B), exporters/capture 6,944 -> 7,667 B (ceiling 7,241 -> 7,923 B). The 118 B wrapper requires the optional exporters peer; its codec bytes are in the capture entry, sharing palette quantization. These bytes retain one writer, stream cancellation, explicit duration/repeat policies and correct rounding. Splitting another codec would duplicate LZW and quantization or add lazy-loader plumbing. Core plus stage stays 24,209 B.
encodeGIF accepts sync/async RGBA8 frames; only one raw frame is retained plus the compressed result. fps defaults to 30, in 100/65535..50. dither defaults false; loop defaults 0 (forever), -1 plays once, 1..65535 repeats. Per-frame duration overrides fps and accepts 0.02..655.35 seconds. Sizes are consistent and <=65,535 per side; data must fit memory. Alpha <128 is transparent, otherwise opaque, as GIF supports one-bit alpha. Each frame has a local <=256-colour RGB palette (255 opaque colours with transparency). Exact colours are preserved when they fit; other frames use shared median cut and optional ordered Bayer dithering. The signal interrupts waiting for the next frame; producers must also observe it to release their own pending work. No CPU speed claim or speculative Wasm rewrite.

## Mesh convex hull and Minkowski sum (batch 224 job 4)
geometry/hull exports convexHullTriangles(points, {signal}) with outward indices into the original flat/nested xyz positions. Empty or lower-dimensional sets return empty indices. The existing Quickhull predicates use a translated unit frame and a 1e-10 coordinate-scale tolerance; this is a floating hull, not an exact predicate claim. Source coordinates are never narrowed to float32. Legacy geometry/extras convexGeometry retains its original errors and float32 rendering buffers.
mesh-edit/hull exports convexMeshHull(oneMeshOrArray, {createId, signal}) and minkowskiSumMeshes(a, b, options). Hull includes all supplied positions (including loose vertices), emits newly generated triangle IDs/planar UVs, and returns an owned empty solid for empty/flat input. Maximum hull input is 200000 positions and normal output mesh limits apply. Minkowski inputs are closed outward consistently wound solids or empty; output has mesh, cells [a,b], convexPairs, planeTriples, collapsedFaces and diagnostics. Empty operands absorb. Concavity, disconnected components and cavities are supported by BSP interior cells and union of convex pair sums. Every output face has a new ID; caller corner attributes are not meaningful under the sum and UVs are planar.
Minkowski defaults: maxCells 2048 per operand, maxPairs 65536, maxPlaneTriples 2000000 per operand. A convex pair may contribute at most 200000 vertex sums; the batch input/output limits also apply. Budgets are positive safe integers and exceeding them rejects with guidance, not partial geometry. Cell decisions/intersections use the existing exact representation, but exported cell coordinates and additions are float64 and Quickhull uses its documented tolerance; a positive cell too thin for that hull rejects explicitly. The final union's validity-preserving thin-face folds are counted. This is not exact arithmetic Minkowski output or a geometric self-intersection repair API; normalize intersecting component soups first. AbortSignal is checked throughout. Worst-case BSP decomposition and pair enumeration can be large, so no interactive or speed claim is made. Core/stage remain unchanged.
Entry sizes: mesh-edit/hull 0 to 11992 gzip bytes (12352-byte ceiling); geometry/hull 0 to 2071 bytes (2327-byte ceiling). Shared Quickhull keeps geometry/extras growth at 5570 to 5617 bytes within its existing ceiling. The optional bytes cover nonconvex and cavity-capable sums rather than a convex-only partial API. Core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.

### FBX large entry (batch 205)

`@margoengine/fbx/large` exports `largeFBX(overrides)` and `FBXImportLimits`. Pass the returned
immutable extension in `extensions` to convertFBX, parseFBX, loadFBX or their worker forms. One
limit configuration per import; unknown names and nonpositive/noninteger/unsafe values reject.
Ordinary imports keep every existing default. All figures below are caps, never reservations.

| Field | Ordinary | largeFBX default |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| inputBytes | 64 MiB | 512 MiB |
| decodedBytes | 128 MiB | 2 GiB |
| arrayBytes | 64 MiB | 512 MiB |
| nodes | 100,000 | 1,000,000 |
| properties | 2,000,000 | 16,000,000 |
| parseWork | 128,000,000 | 2,000,000,000 |
| sceneBytes | 128 MiB | 2 GiB |
| sceneWork | 128,000,000 | 2,000,000,000 |
| morphBytes | 64 MiB | 512 MiB |
| vertices | 1,000,000 | 8,000,000 |
| corners | 3,000,000 | 24,000,000 |
| geometryWork | 40,000,000 | 320,000,000 |
| textureBytes | 64 MiB | 64 MiB |
| texturePixels | 16,000,000 | 16,000,000 |
| outputBytes | 128 MiB | 512 MiB |

MiB = 1,048,576 bytes; GiB = 1,073,741,824 bytes. `vertices` bounds control points,
expanded vertices and the cumulative scene vertices (including instances); `corners` bounds
polygon corners and triangulated indices. Allocation/work accounting remains conservative,
so dense seams/instances may need higher caps. Raising a cap cannot create available memory.
The 4,096-corner polygon, hierarchy depth, animation/key/sample limits and GLB uint32 format
limits are unchanged. Imported meshes are never decimated or truncated to meet these caps.

Batch 172 job 4: sciviz/probe accepts up to 8000000 points/snapshot and 1000000 profile samples. Uniform cell buckets max 32 per axis; cells spanning over 128 buckets use a separate candidate list. ### Oriented box culling subclasses

`@margoengine/culling/bounds` exports BoxCulledMeshes, BoxCulledModels and
BoxDynamicInstances. They inherit the corresponding ordinary culler's options
and methods, retaining stable compaction, picking and complete shadow lists.
Frustum tests use transformed local boxes, including shear and reflection;
BoxCulledMeshes and native BoxCulledModels also use them for Hi-Z occlusion.
Model padding expands each local half-extent. Deformed model primitives still
retain their original conservative bypass. Ordinary sphere cullers do not load
box mathematics. BoxCulledModels runs box frustum/size culling on the full WebGL2
layer; its Hi-Z remains native-only. BoxCulledMeshes uses current CPU depth there.
BoxDynamicInstances adds box frustum tests on both backends; its base class has
no occlusion option. Geometry position arrays are treated as immutable, as for
ordinary core Geometry; model array replacement refreshes cached bounds.

Batch 223 job 2 also joins exactly coplanar convex triangle pairs before CPU
depth rasterization, using exact dyadic predicates for the float32 positions.
This removes their internal seam while preserving real holes, folds and back
faces. Larger triangulations may still retain extra candidates. Snapshot
validation refreshes cached patches when software geometry changes in place.
The software entry's earlier 28-of-81 figure is job 1's historical measurement;
the current entry can reject additional hidden rows with the same pixels.

### Native 3MF lattice and slice data (batch 202)
`@margoengine/loaders/threemf-lattice` exposes async parse3MFLattice. It returns the existing textured/material preview mesh plus source objects, exact native lattice parameters, source-double xyz, triangle topology, per-build affine instances, slice stacks and property resources. Radii and contours remain in file units; instances retain the composed row-vector affine transform and unitScale (meters by default, 1 for units:file). This preserves nonuniformly scaled spheres/frusta without replacing their radii with an inaccurate scalar. Clipping mode/volume and representation meshes remain explicit references to validated earlier source meshes; consumers choose their native construction or the file's preview representation. The returned triangle stream is the file's mesh representation, whose lowres/fullres label is retained. It is not a new manufactured union of beams or slices.
Caps are sphere/hemisphere/butt, default sphere. ballMode defaults to none; mixed/all require ballRadius. Source beam indices remain stable; activeBeams applies minlength before transform, and effectiveBalls applies mode and active beam-end membership. Native-only valid beam builds can have empty triangle arrays. Default maxBeams is 1,000,000 for beams and explicit balls each, with at most twice that many set references. Default maxSlices is 100,000 source layers/references and separately expanded referenced layers. Source/slice vertices share maxVertices; segments are bounded by 3*maxTriangles, source objects by 100,000 and the existing model-part/instance/ZIP caps remain active.
External slices require their model-part OPC relationship and a single reference level. Tops strictly increase, void layers remain, model/solidsupport contours close explicitly, and composed slice transforms preserve the slicing plane without an epsilon tolerance. Component stacks override descendant stacks. lowres requires the slice namespace in requiredextensions. Slice properties retain endpoint gradients and object defaults. Materials keep raw entries plus normalized composite weights and defaulted multi rows/blendMethods. The shared materials reader now mixes in linear RGB, supports multiply, treats all-zero weights uniformly and retains opacity in attributes.opacity. Existing byte, count and AbortSignal options propagate through all part reads.
Entry sizes: /threemf-lattice is new, 0 to 12,275 B min+gzip (ceiling 12,644 B). /threemf-materials is 7,661 to 8,082 B; its ceiling rises from 7,917 to 8,338 B for linear mix/multiply, normative defaults, alpha and shared format hooks. `@margoengine/culling/sort` exports FrontToBack for kept core batches (including

classes and can change at runtime. Core and model sorting executes after culling
and before drawing, independent of registration order. Model tint/transmission
lists and alphaMode BLEND primitives retain their existing order. Plain model
primitives keep their original draws; deformed models retain their bypass.
Each range orders by its transformed local center along the current view
forward direction, with original row indices breaking equal-depth ties. It
supports perspective and orthographic views, reflection and node transforms.
Ordering is per batch, as with specialised batched renderers, rather than across
materials or geometries. Counts, picking/caster buffers and every record field
stay unchanged. Opaque surfaces that overlap at equal surface depth but have
different center depths can resolve in the new order, the usual draw-order
consequence of sorting. Transparent geometry must never be passed to the raw
sorter. Importing ordinary cullers does not load ordering code.
InstanceSorter accepts capacity 0 through 4,194,304 within device storage limits;
its key network rounds to a power of two. O(n log-squared n) key comparisons and
one gather are encoded; no per-instance CPU work or GPU readback occurs. Each
view and stage owns distinct parameter storage. Input instance buffers require
STORAGE; supplied argument buffers require STORAGE and COPY_SRC. Software
occlusion arguments now expose those flags too. No speed claim is made.

Removed sort owners release all their view resources with InstanceSorter.forget;
FrontToBack also collects owners absent from the preceding frame and releases
registered model resources on removal. Cleanup happens before a later frame,
after the prior frame's command submission; existing view uploads stay distinct.
