### Graph transition offsets and interruption (batch 211 job 3)

GraphTransition.offset defaults to 0, accepts finite 0..1 and sets destination entry time relative to its longest clip. Events start at that entry, including a marker exactly at the offset. Crossfades retain their own seconds clock, so a large offset cannot prematurely end an uninterruptible fade. interruptionSource is none, current, next, both (alias current-next), current-next or next-current. Default next preserves existing behaviour; legacy interruptible:false defaults to none, and an explicit source overrides it. Each source checks transitions in declaration order, with any-state rules eligible for that source; only the selected rule consumes triggers. Source clocks advance for exit-time checks and chained interruptions retain their selected source. Manual animator.transition uses next semantics. Snapshots retain optional fade.fromTime and reject nonfinite/negative source times. Graph controller parameter/trigger and interruption-policy state is separate from Animator playback snapshots.
Entry costs: graph 9,719 -> 10,177 B gzip, ceiling 10,011 -> 10,483; layers 10,281 -> 10,730 B, ceiling 10,436 -> 11,052. The bytes keep source selection and graph clocks in one implementation, avoiding an incompatible alternate controller entry. Core and stage unchanged.

## Mesh-surface scatter (batch 231 job 2)

scatterSurface(geometryData, count, options) from @margoengine/scatter/surface returns owned transforms, positions, normals, uvs and colors arrays. Defaults: seed 1; scale [1,1]; yaw [0,2*pi] radians; align 1; offset 0; source matrix identity; no weights or painted colours; no cancellation signal. Count is 0..1000000. Source triangles must have positive weighted area even with count 0. Vertex weights are nonnegative and interpolated linearly within each triangle. Areas are measured in world space after options.matrix, including nonuniform scale; normals use its inverse transpose. Arrays and source geometry are not mutated. Sources and outputs must fit finite f32 values; placements are nonsingular affine world matrices with uniform scale. Use an identity TexturedScatter model root for world placements, or convert into that root's space.

Output costs 112 bytes per placement (16 matrix, 3 position, 3 normal, 2 UV and 4 colour floats), plus the sampler's triangle CDF and transformed source copies when a matrix is supplied. Alignment is the shortest rotation from world +Y, then optional local yaw; the antipodal -Y case chooses +X as its turn axis. Offset is along the sampled normal. No mesh-to-heightmap projection: cliffs, roofs and undersides are sampled directly. Resample when source geometry or weights change. Entry gzip 0 to 1259 bytes, ceiling 1515 bytes; core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.

Batch 205 job 4: `@margoengine/fbx/surfaces` exports `surfaces`, an optional extension on page and worker conversion. It tessellates Nurb/NurbsSurface and Patch geometry, including older inline Model geometry after legacyFBX normalization, independently of extension ordering. NURBS orders 2..32, positive rational weights, open/closed/periodic nets and every nonempty knot span use loaders/nurbs. FBX Step controls subdivisions per span; absent Step defaults to four times degree. Bezier cubic, BezierQuadric quadratic, Cardinal cubic, uniform cubic BSpline and Linear patch bases may differ on U and V. Open Bezier nets require 1 modulo degree control points; closed nets add their seam point; Cardinal open spans interpolate the interior controls and closed spans wrap. Closure wraps the necessary weighted rows/columns. Parametric UVs, analytic/pole normals, FlipNormals, material links, model transforms and animation remain in the ordinary FBX path. The output is the whole parametric surface, not trimmed topology. Control-point skin/morph deformation cannot in general be represented exactly by one glTF vertex bind position; it fails with coded unsupported/help and a polygon-bake remedy, rather than misapplying original control-point indices to generated vertices. ### Weighted bone masks (batch 211 job 4)

animator/masks provides createBoneMask(nodeCount, entries?, defaultWeight=0) and addWeightedLayer(owner, {clip or graph, mask, weight?, blend?}). The builder returns a mutable Float32Array in glTF node order; entries are unique [node,weight] pairs. Weights and defaultWeight must be finite 0..1. An attached mask has exactly one value per model node and is read and validated every frame. Each value affects its own node; ancestry is not expanded automatically. Effective influence is layer strength times bone weight; zero retains the lower pose and one applies full influence. Defaults are layer weight 1 and override mode. Additive uses the owner's loaded local pose and identity scale delta on a zero reference axis. Morph weights use the corresponding node influence. Vertex skin weights remain asset data. The returned StateLayer exposes its independent graph controls and shares the layers entry's class identity. Disposal removes the complete layer; owner pause/speed and lifetime apply as for graph layers.

### Painted 2D geometry (batch 247 job 1)
`@margoengine/lighting2d/sdf` exports `SDFScene2D`, consumed as borrowed `GILighting2DOptions.painted`. Source alpha at least alphaThreshold (default .5, always positive) defines opaque axis-aligned pixel cells; RGB is linear straight albedo. Separate emission defaults to source, uses RGB times alpha times emissionIntensity (default 1, nonnegative), and only occupied cells emit. Black art blocks without emitting. Camera defaults {x:0,y:0,zoom:1}, top-left origin, pixels per world unit, independent of the receiver camera. Changes are sampled every GI frame before cascades. Inputs are single-sample 2D single-layer RGBA/BGRA unorm/sRGB or RGBA16/32 float TEXTURE_BINDING textures of matching dimensions; textures and the SDFScene2D are borrowed by GI. Source and output must be distinct textures. sRGB textures decode on load. HDR needs a floating emission image and output.
The exact sampled-centre signed distance field stores R distance in pixels, G occupancy in rgba32float (16 B/pixel). All-empty/full opposite-class distances use finite magnitude 1e10. Three GPU passes plus scratch cost 48 B/source pixel plus 32 B uniforms (row 8, hull 16, squared 8, field 16); scratch buffers must fit device maxStorageBufferBindingSize/maxBufferSize and dispatches must fit maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension. The transform is exact at pixel centres, not a continuous vector outline; opacity is thresholded, not transmissive. Nearest opaque cell emission terminates each ray, including inside a source. No frame-rate or general transport-error claim. Painted surface reflection and temporal reuse are batch 247 job 2.

### Cluster hierarchy and task-based readback (batch 222)
The optional /clusters entry accepts core Geometry (positions/normals), with 4-256 triangles per leaf (default 124), 3-256 distinct vertices per rendered meshlet (default 64), parent ratio in (0,1) (default 0.5), and AbortSignal. The current builder is synchronous after its lazy simplifier import; cancellation is checked between regions and by simplification. A tree, rather than regrouped DAG, preserves all inter-region boundaries exactly; a heavily split-normal mesh or dense region boundary can limit simplification. The error is a conservative accumulated vertex displacement bound; the sphere projection is an error estimate, not a raster-space Hausdorff guarantee. Each selected meshlet uses a core mesh/draw, with normal engine frustum culling; no GPU selection, virtual streaming or Nanite throughput is claimed. cinematic/physical-lens is optional: new entry 0 to 589 B minified gzip, budget 845 B. Core plus stage stays 24209 B. Settings must be finite and positive, focus beyond the focal length. @margoengine/lines/debug exports DebugLines, ArcLine and arcPositions. DebugLines drawLine/drawLines/drawArc queue for the next rendered frame and clear on the following rendered frame, including zero delta. Great-circle arcs default to height 0 and center [0,0,0], interpolate endpoint radii linearly, and use radial midpoint height. Coincident directions and antipodes are deterministic; an endpoint at the center rejects. These are spherical paths, not ellipsoid/geographic projections. Endpoint float32 positions are exact copies. ### Batch 218 transition presets

The optional transitions/presets entry supplies slide, push, zoom, iris, cube, page-curl, swirl and fade-through-color. transitionPresetWGSL returns the custom WGSL function contract without GPU work; createPresetTransition and createLivePresetTransition validate then attach frozen or live versions. Parameters: direction [1,0] normalized from any finite nonzero 2-vector, softness 0.02 in [0,0.5], center [0.5,0.5] in the unit square, color opaque black in normalized RGBA, strength 1 in (0,8] for zoom/swirl, easing linear (also quadratic ease-in, quadratic ease-out, cubic Hermite ease-in-out). These easing names describe polynomial remapping, not CSS keyword cubic Bezier values. Direction affects translated and rotated geometric treatments; isotropic zoom/iris/swirl remain center-based. Softness affects reveal/boundary coverage; fade and continuous distortions have no reveal edge. Cube is an analytic two-face rotation, with background color outside the projected cube. Curl rolls the image around a fixed radius 0.15 UV cylinder with shaded reverse side, not physical paper simulation. Exact endpoints, trusted-code assumptions, captures, output formats, cancellation and ownership follow the custom/live entries.

### Painted GI and temporal intervals (batch 247 job 2)
`GILighting2D.temporal` defaults true; false recomputes all intervals, and resetHistory() forces the next rebuild. Identical frames retain spatial/angular cascade and finite-bounce surface buffers, and their compute invocations return before tracing. Source and emission RGBA comparisons are exact on GPU. Any alpha, color, emission, source transform, cutoff or gain change invalidates painted intervals. Analytic geometry, emitters, lights (including nested masks), layer, cascade options, view camera and output dimensions are compared on CPU. No old radiance is blended into changed input. A camera move rebuilds rather than reprojecting; ambient is applied at presentation and needs no interval rebuild. Device replacement and changing painted/no-painted mode discard all GI history. One SDFScene2D snapshot per command encoder serves multiple consumers; submit a manually managed frame before starting another. GI borrows the painted scene and textures.
Painted occupied cells have four outward surface slots; internal faces are inactive. Each exposed face gathers 32 cosine-weighted directions per requested bounce from the preceding order, at its midpoint offset .001 source pixels into empty space. Painted RGB clamps to [0,1] for reflectance and multiplies the configured albedo; emission retains HDR. Finite bounce orders 0..4, source resolution, interval reach and angular quadrature limits still apply. GI is now covered by the named opaque visibility, energy, finite-bounce, painted-input and temporal correctness fixtures; no general physical-exactness, converged transport, continuous vector-outline or frame-rate claim is made. Historical README exceptions and no-history language await the README phase.
SDF adds 32 B/pixel exact RGBA history and a 16 B change flag to its previous 48 B/pixel transform storage (80 B/pixel plus 48 B fixed uniforms/flag). Painted GI surface buffers use 192 B/source pixel (two persistent fields and immutable zero order, four vec4 faces each), plus analytic patch geometry and cascade storage. Analytic surface fields use 96 B/patch including zero order, replacing the earlier 64 B/patch. Changed-input comparisons and distance generation still run every frame; presentation traces the near connectors. Reuse avoids surface gathers and upper-cascade interval traces, not every GPU operation.

Batch 247 job 2 sizes: SDF 2,667 to 2,911 B min+gzip, inside its 2,923 B ceiling; GI 9,670 to 10,348 B, ceiling raised 9,961 to 10,659 B under Scott's optional-size ruling. The bytes buy painted diffuse face transport, exact temporal change detection/reuse and owning-scene disposal. Splitting the trace/bounce contract into another entry would add synchronous adapters without removing that work. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B with no source changes.

cinematic/ortho is new: 0 to 2877 B minified gzip, budget 3133 B. Optional brain changes 3089 to 3161 B, budget 3262 B; core plus stage remains 24209 B. ### Compute shape entry (batch 274 job 1)
The optional @margoengine/compute/shape entry adds concatenate(arrays, axis=0), stack(arrays, axis=0), flip(x, axes=all), tile(x, repetitions), repeat(x, counts, axis=null) and pad(x, widths, options). Concatenate axis=null flattens; repeat omitting its axis flattens. Negative axes normalize against the output rank for stack and input rank otherwise. Joining promotes element types; other operations preserve dtype. Every output owns its buffer. CPU, WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility share the same logical indexing. f16 uses the existing shader-f16 device requirement and is unavailable on CPU.
Pad defaults to constant zero; scalar constantValues is converted to the input dtype. Modes: constant, edge, wrap, reflect (excludes endpoints), symmetric (includes endpoints). Widths may be one nonnegative integer, a shared pair, or one pair per axis. Nonconstant padding cannot fill an empty source axis. This entry does not expose NumPy callable/statistical/ramp padding or odd reflection. Tile prepends singleton axes or repetition factors as required by the Array API. Repeat counts may be a number or a host list of length one/axis length. Counts stay on the host to determine output shape. Arrays are bounded by device storage limits and signed 32-bit gather indices; split larger inputs.

`scatter/attributes` adds `AttributedScatter` over fixed `ScatterInstances` batches. `setColorAt(index,rgb,batch=0)` sets a nonnegative finite linear RGB multiplier; `getColorAt` returns a copy. `setAttributeAt(index,name,components,batch=0)` and `getAttributeAt` use the declared scalar/vector sizes 1..4. `AttributeOptions.shader` defines WGSL `scatterAppearance(position:vec3f,color:vec3f,data:ScatterAttributeData)->ScatterAppearance`. Position is world space before rooted wind. Result fields are position and color; both passes call it, so translation/custom deformation keeps matching shadow geometry. Data has `color:vec4f` and (when declared) `custom:array<vec4f,N>`; scalar/vector tails are zero-padded. Default function returns its position and colour inputs. Geometry normals stay those of the batch; a position modifier does not supply a new normal. Custom data is consumed by this shader path, not merely retained on CPU. Existing vertex colour/occlusion, emission, wind, detail, translucency, roughness and metallic fields retain their bindings.
Attribute storage costs `16*(1+N)*instanceCount` bytes on GPU and the same retained CPU data, per batch, within both device maxBufferSize and maxStorageBufferBindingSize. ## Batch 212 job 3: mixer/fx
FX entry: 3,680 B gzip, budget 3,936 B. New optional JSON chain entry includes chorus, flanger, phaser, tremolo, vibrato, auto-filter, auto-pan, distortion, bitcrusher and authored waveshaping. Root/core/stage unchanged. Each createFX has input/output, named AudioParams, dispose and Symbol.dispose; createFXChain rolls back failures/abort and prefixes parameters by index; createBusFX inserts an owned chain after bus gating, before post sends, independently of native root effects.
Modulation defaults rate 1 Hz (0..20), depth 0.5 (0..1), sine (also triangle/square/sawtooth), initial phase 0 degrees; spread 180 degrees for chorus/tremolo, otherwise 0. Auto-pan is linked stereo. Mix defaults 0.5 for chorus/flanger/phaser, 1 for other effects. Delay centre defaults 0.02/0.003/0.005 s for chorus/flanger/vibrato, range 0..0.1, minimum actual read 1 sample, depth sweeps centre*(1+depth*LFO), linear fractional interpolation. Delay feedback default 0 (-0.95..0.95); no artificial 128-frame minimum. Phaser uses 6 allpass biquads (integer 1..32), frequency 400 Hz (10..0.45*sampleRate), octaves 3 (0..8), q 1 (0.1..40, linear quality factor); auto-filter uses one lowpass with the same exponential sweep. Sweeps clamp at 0.45*sampleRate. This models canonical digital effects, not a particular analog pedal. Wet zero copies input bits, wet one copies processed bits including signed zero.
Bitcrusher defaults bits 4 (integer 1..24), sample/hold reduction 1 (integer 1..128); nearest quantisation, no saturation. Distortion amount 0.4 (0..1) uses (1+k)*x/(1+k*abs(x)), k=100*amount, with 8193 curve samples. Waveshaper accepts 2..65537 finite float32 JSON samples. Native input lookup saturates outside [-1,1]; oversample none (default), 2x or 4x. Colour amount/curve, waveform, spread, phase, stages and channel layout are construction settings; numeric worklet controls and mix are automatable. Worklets support explicit speaker channels 1..32 (default 2); auto-pan requires 2. Requires secure AudioWorklet and blob CSP permission except native colour effects. Caller owns headroom for resonant filters/feedback and chain tails. Tests cover deterministic quantum independence and actual rendered audio on both backends; no speed, other-browser, anti-alias certification or perceptual-equivalence claim.


### Batch 218 GLSL transition import

The optional transitions/glsl entry translates user-authored GLSL ES 1.00 with vec4 transition(vec2 uv) into the custom WGSL contract. translateGLSLTransition is pure; createGLSLTransition and createLiveGLSLTransition validate asynchronously before attaching. progress and ratio are supplied, along with getFromColor/getToColor and the from/to sampler2D aliases. GLSL UVs default to bottom-left; flipY:false preserves top-left coordinates. Additional uniform values are snapshotted as constants from options.uniforms or // = JSON annotations. Vectors, column-major matrices and fixed arrays use flattened component arrays; boolean values or 0/1 are accepted for boolean components. Numbers must fit finite 32-bit values; integer uniforms must fit their signed/unsigned type.

Preprocessing supports object/function macros, conditionals, define/undef, and version 100. Expressions use typed precedence parsing, including scalar/vector arithmetic, matrix operations and casts, struct/array access, overloads, swizzles, short-circuit boolean expressions and conditional side effects. Structured if/for/while/do control flow and copy-in/copy-out out/inout parameters are lowered to WGSL. No extra textures or arbitrary binding interface is supplied beyond the two transition images. Other GLSL versions are refused when declared. This is a transition-function importer, not a complete vertex/fragment program or an external include loader. Source is limited to 65536 UTF-16 units, 32768 tokens, 128 nested statements/expressions, 64 macro expansion rounds and 262144 expanded units; uniform arrays have at most 16384 elements. The custom wrapper also limits emitted WGSL to 65536 units. Compiler diagnostics carry failed and a help link; GPU compilation, cancellation, exact endpoint bypass and shader trust requirements follow the custom entry. Shader execution itself is not bounded by these parser limits.

Native GLSL and WGSL may round floating-point arithmetic differently, especially at exactly-on-texel-boundary nearest samples. Pixel fixtures choose coordinates away from those ambiguous ties and compare with the existing one-byte unorm tolerance. No bit-exact arbitrary GLSL or speed claim is made.

Batch 218 job 3 glsl entry is 15718 B gzip (new entry, before 0 B), with a ceiling of 16190 B. The compiler carries a real parser, preprocessor, typed aggregate/control-flow lowering, diagnostics and both validated factories. Splitting those mutually dependent stages would complicate deterministic diagnostics and lifecycle without improving shader quality. Core + stage stays 24209 B.

Batch 244 job 3: CRT adds `colorBleed` [0,1], default 0, and `chromaticOffset`, `redOffset`, `greenOffset`, `blueOffset`, each a horizontal number or [x,y] source-pixel tuple in [-32,32], default 0. Symmetric offset adds to red and subtracts from blue; independent offsets add on top. Positive offsets select texels to the right/below, so those channel images move left/up. Effective combined offsets may reach 64 source pixels. Color bleed retains source luma and alpha, filters I with normalized 5-tap and Q with 9-tap horizontal binomials, then clips to the premultiplied gamut. Offsets use bilinear sampling with edge-repeat borders; alpha is the maximum selected channel alpha. Tube beam/mask/brightness modulate the processed color; glow still adds the unshifted raw-source 3x3 halo. Both effects default off and preserve all previous CRT pixels, including exact boundaries. This is a selectable composite-video look, not RF encoding, dot crawl, interlacing or a calibrated TV standard. No extra pass or intermediate image; no timing claim.

Batch 244 job 3 min+gzip: pixel/crt 2816 -> 3775 B, ceiling 3072 -> 4031 B. These optional bytes retain one CRT pass with independent RGB sampling, YIQ chroma filtering and existing restoration/lifetime plumbing; splitting would add pass wiring or duplicate source processing. Core plus stage remains 24209 B.



### Streamed SOG (batch 238 job 3)
splats/lod-sog accepts v1 and unversioned pre-release lod-meta.json, null/omitted environments, sparse leaf levels, optional errors and relative arbitrary chunk paths. Each chunk is unbundled SOG v2/v3 with 1 to 3,000,000 records. All small metadata is fetched up front with concurrency 8 to validate runs/counts and choose a uniform SH degree; textures remain lazy. Spatial depth limit 128. Complete non-overlapping single-level chunk runs and supplied totals must agree. A referenced chunk is decoded whole, then its range is copied. cacheChunks defaults 2 (0 disables completed caching), plus active loads and the existing SplatLod node cache. Independent caller aborts share requests; disposal aborts all loads.
SplatLod structural nodes have count 0 and refine unconditionally; the renderer never calls their load. Minimum coarse coverage must fit the fixed-slot budget, otherwise construction rejects with the required budget. Slot-count and splat-count limits both constrain refinement. Errors are used only with lodErrors true; otherwise radius * cbrt(max(0,1-count/finestCount)) estimates omitted detail. Environment stays selected regardless of camera distance. No transition blending or new training algorithm.
SOG v3 preserves exponential-map rotations, squared opacity through 1.5625, 24-bit labels and SH degree 4 (25 RGB coefficients including DC). Unused blind attributes are ignored as permitted by the format. Images use the existing lossless WebP decoder. Extended opacity is retained until the existing fragment alpha cap min(0.99, opacity*Gaussian), preserving extra off-center coverage. Colours retain the existing first-order display/linear SH conversion. encodeSog chooses v3 for extended opacity or degree 4, otherwise v2. SPZ v3, .splat and Gaussian PLY reject opacity above 1 rather than wrapping/clipping; SPZ v3 rejects degree 4. Standard PLY now carries degree 4.

Shared degree-4/v3 support takes data to 22,273 B (prior ceiling 22,135 B, raised to 22,942 B) and animate to 20,381 B (prior ceiling 20,263 B, raised to 20,993 B). The bytes retain a single validated data representation and codec instead of splitting degree/opacity formats. Root splats 32,073 B; lod 30,582 B; progressive 31,464 B; formats 20,705 B. ## Lightmaps drawn at draw time (batch 54)

`@margoengine/lightmap/apply` adds the bake as indirect light (diffuse reflectance times occlusion times the bake),
the way `Material.lightMap` does; it does not turn off live lights the bake already holds. A glTF-pro material record
that already has a material extension (clearcoat, a custom one) is refused, since a record holds one extension. A core
mesh needs its lightmap UVs passed (`uv1`), is drawn by a materials stand-in in the engine's default scene, and its
stand-in copies colour, roughness, metalness and sidedness only (no core textures). A live GPU baker must share the
model's GPU device. WebGPU only for glTF-pro models.

## Batch 196 non-XR stereo

Optional cameras/stereo is 3,144 B min+gzip (previously 0 B), ceiling 3,400 B. StereoOutput.render replaces the application's engine.render call in its frame loop; it uses two scene draws and one fullscreen packing pass, with one plugin update per pair. Default mode side-by-side, eye separation 0.064 world units, convergence at the camera target, source engine.camera, source camera layers, default scene, unswapped eyes, column stripes and phase 0. Infinity focus gives parallel frusta. StereoRig also preserves custom projection hooks; orthographic eyes correctly have no depth disparity. The packed output is display colour (RGBA8 eye textures); anaglyph is the published red/cyan Dubois transform in linear light. Two RGBA8 eye targets use 8 * eyeWidth * eyeHeight bytes, plus core's normal render attachments. Rows/columns refer to physical backing pixels; a physical barrier needs calibrated optics and pixel-aligned presentation. On automatic canvas resize the projection follows the new aspect immediately and eye resolution catches up on the next frame; exactSize canvases give caller-controlled physical dimensions. No XR session or automatic engine.start takeover. Dispose the output before its engine. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility work; native WebGL-only engines reject.

### Curved text (batch 248 job 4)
`@margoengine/text/curve` provides CurvedText, curvePoint and PathText. CurvedText extends Text, wrapping the entire local X/Y block around local Y at signed curveRadius (default 1; Infinity is flat). Default curveSegments is 8 horizontal subdivisions per glyph, integer 1..256. The analytic cylinder uses [r*sin(x/r), y, 2*r*sin(x/(2*r))^2]; glyph UVs and outline/shadow layers interpolate over the subdivided surface in one block draw. Anchors, lines, shaping, font styles and transform/mesh placement are preserved. Layout/caret/selection coordinates remain in the unwrapped plane; hitTestSurface maps a cylinder-local surface point back to that plane. That inverse is principal-angle only, so blocks winding more than one revolution need an application-supplied winding choice.
PathText accepts a TextPath with positive finite length and sample(distance) returning position/tangent/normal in local world units. startOffset defaults to 0; closed defaults false (out-of-range glyph midpoints hide), true wraps distances. Glyphs align rigidly to normalized orthogonal path frames as in SVG textPath align; whole shaped runs remain joined. Line baselines offset along the frame normal. Global transform and mesh attachment apply after path placement. Each visible nonspace shaped item is one Text draw. Call update after editing owned options, font state or path; addTo/removeFrom and dispose manage renderer membership, including rebuilds. Billboard is refused for PathText because the path owns glyph orientation; CurvedText supports a billboard cylinder. Arbitrary paths are supplied via the public frame interface, not parsed from SVG strings. No core or stage additions.

## Batch 212 job 4: mixer/dynamics
Extended dynamics entry: 2,856 B gzip, budget 3,112 B. New optional gate/expander/three-band compressor with explicit linked speaker channels 1..32 (default 2), fixed construction options, AudioWorklet/CSP/AbortSignal/owned bus lifecycle as the existing worklet entry. No lookahead (latencyFrames 0), automatic makeup, clipping or true-peak limiting. Crossover phase is inherent; flat magnitude does not mean sample-identical input. Use existing worklet limiting after this stage for peak safety.
Gate defaults threshold -40 dBFS (-120..0), hysteresis 3 dB (0..40), hold 0.05 s (0..10), floor -Infinity (silence, or -120..0 dB), attack 0.001 s and release 0.1 s (0..10). Peak >= threshold opens; while open, peak >= threshold-hysteresis resets hold. Exactly holdFrames below-closing-threshold samples remain open, then closing begins. Expander defaults threshold -40, ratio 2, knee 6 dB, range 80 dB (0..120), makeup 0; below-threshold slope ratio and a quadratic knee join continuously to unity. Band defaults threshold -24, knee 6 (0..40), ratio 4 (1..100), attack 0.003, release 0.1 (0..10), makeup 0 (-24..24). Attack/release are one-pole gain time constants: compressor attenuation/recovery, gate/expander opening/closing; zero jumps. Pure expanderCurve returns output dB and handles silent -Infinity.
Multiband crossovers default [250,2500] Hz, ordered 10..0.45*sampleRate; separate low/mid/high BandDynamics. Each split is two cascaded Butterworth biquads per low/high path (24 dB/octave). Low-band high-crossover phase compensation keeps the unity sum flat. Per-band detector is linked maximum absolute sample. Ratios 1 and makeup 0 retain the crossover's allpass response. Tests prove independent RBJ convolution, closed-form knees/gains and flat impulse-response magnitude across the spectrum; real renders beside both backends. Headroom, perceptual tuning, other browsers and performance remain unmeasured. No core/stage change.
## Batch 173: optional transfer classification
`@margoengine/sciviz/transfer` adds joint value/gradient histograms, rectangle, triangle and Gaussian classifiers, 1D ordered preintegration, CT/MRI/PET display presets and an owned HTML editor. LUT resolution is 2..2048 per axis; default 256 for widgets, 128 for preintegration. Colours are linear light, opacity per reference voxel. Points and widget coordinates use physical scalar units and scalar units/data unit for gradients. Histograms require 2+ samples per axis, at most 64 million samples, x fastest; NaN/nonfinite centres or derivative neighbours are excluded. Histograms own two float64 scratch arrays (16 bytes/sample) and a 4-byte count per bin. Scalar values/gradients outside the selected histogram axes clamp to the edge bins.
Volume textures retain signed normalized scalar values outside the display range so their gradients remain meaningful; binary16 limits normalized values to [-65504,65504] and rounds them. Histogram derivatives use original CPU values; render derivatives use the half-float, trilinearly sampled field. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported. The separate native `sciviz/webgl2` fallback, bricked volumes and extracted isosurfaces do not consume this scalar VolumeLayer API. The editor can bind any existing scalar VolumeLayer without recreating its data; function points are resampled into the layer's existing range. Slice colours update with the same classifier. Slice opacity remains its independently specified opacity.
Preintegration uses 8..2048 midpoint samples (default 128), linear scalar variation over an ordered front/back segment and RGBA8 output. Generate for the layer's `step=1/quality` and density. Regenerate after changing quality/density for the most accurate colour integral. The marcher corrects opacity when step/density differ, but unpremultiplied integrated colour remains an approximation in that case, at clipped segment endpoints and in the existing 2048-sample cap. Gradient classification is evaluated at march samples, not preintegrated in 2D. MIP is scalar-maximum projection, not a 2D classification maximum.
The HTML component has no import side effects, supports add/select/delete, pointer/key translation, colour/opacity, rectangle extents, Gaussian sigma and explicit triangle vertices. Disposing the editor removes DOM/listeners and restores the layer's original classifier. Preintegration and histograms accept AbortSignal and yield during work. No timing or superiority claim. ## Batch 212 job 5: mixer/pitch
Pitch entry: 2,366 B gzip, budget 2,622 B. New optional time-domain transposer emits exactly one frame per input frame, with linked read-head phase for explicit speaker channels 1..32 (default 2). Defaults: pitch 0 semitones (-48..48, fractional), windowSize 0.1 s (0.005..1, fixed at construction), delayTime 0 s (0..1), feedback 0 (-0.95..0.95), mix 1 (0..1), antiAlias true (boolean). Pitch/mix/feedback/delayTime are native audio-rate controls; setPitch validates schedule atomically and defaults to immediate, or an exponential fade settling about 98% over seconds. Zero wet and default unison preserve bits, including initial samples. Unison with configured delay/feedback reads a fixed delay, minimum 1 sample for feedback.
Two half-cycle-offset read heads use complementary Hann weights and linear interpolation. Nonzero-pitch wet delay spans additional delay plus 1..windowFrames+1 samples; there is no single fixed latency. Source event times/duration stay on the same clock, with that bounded wet tail; keep feeding zeros to flush it. Memory per channel is ceil(sampleRate+windowFrames)+4 float64 samples plus filter state, allocated once. No per-sample allocation, FFT, offline resampling or timer. Upward antiAlias filtering is two Butterworth biquads at 0.45*sampleRate/ratio before the delay; aliases can remain and high frequencies are attenuated. Linear interpolation also rolls off high frequencies. No formant preservation, transient protection, speech-quality, polyphonic transparency or alias-free claim; this is the requested delay-line effect class and can have window coloration. Feedback is a creative transposed delay, not pitch-preserving echo. Requires secure AudioWorklet and blob CSP permission. Abort/disposal and bus-owned inserts follow the other optional worklets. No core/stage change; tested in Edge beside both backends, other browsers/listening/performance unmeasured.

### Shaped and variable-font extrusion (batch 248 job 5)
`text/extrude` accepts `shapedRuns`, ordered visual glyph IDs with xAdvance/yAdvance/xOffset/yOffset in em units, optional UTF-16 cluster and zero-based line. It respects ligatures, reordered RTL runs, mark offsets, vertical advances and multiple runs per line without remapping IDs through cmap. Letter spacing applies between distinct supplied clusters; omitted clusters space each glyph. A FontLike.shape(text) provider is called once when runs are absent; without either input, the existing Unicode cmap path remains. This is a shaping-result interface, with no built-in script shaper or network dependency. Normalize shaper positions by its font scale and use the same font instance and axes as the run.
`parseFontOutlines(bytes,{variations})`, FontOutlines.withVariations(values) and extrudeText's variations option select instances; omitted axes use fvar defaults, out-of-range values clamp, unknown/nonfinite axes fail with a linked coded error. variationAxes exposes tags/min/default/max. TrueType supports gvar shared/private/intermediate tuples, sparse contour interpolation, composite offsets and phantom widths when HVAR is absent. HVAR supports index maps and short/long delta rows, including null subtables. avar version 1 piecewise remapping is supported; later avar versions reject explicitly. CFF2 supports 32-bit INDEX counts, FontDICT/FDSelect formats 0/3/4, local/global subroutines, private and charstring blend/vsindex, implicit program termination and a 513-value stack. Existing 96-hint, 10-subroutine, 100,000-token and 16,384-flattened-vertex budgets remain; malformed ranges/counts reject. CFF1 and static TrueType behavior remain covered by the existing tests. Glyphs remain unhinted; font-wide MVAR/VVAR metrics are not consumed because block line height and supplied vertical advances own placement here. Parsed instances currently reparse their source bytes; no timing claim.
The existing optional extrude entry grows from 10,834 to 14,894 B gzip; its ceiling is raised in the same commit. Those bytes add the complete font-instance and positioned-run path in one parser; a split would duplicate sfnt state or add an asynchronous stateful bridge to the synchronous extrusion API. Core/stage and the text root are unchanged by this job, at 24,209 B combined and 16,860 B root respectively.

Batch 248 accepted precision follow-up: this unhinted outline path currently retains floating-point normalized axis coordinates rather than enforcing the OpenType 16.16 then 2.14 normalization round trip. The default/static and tested FontTools floating-instance results match; exact fixed-coordinate interoperability is tracked in known-bugs.md for the fix phase.
### Batch 240 job 1: voxel custom block models

`@margoengine/voxel/models` defines a block as a union of 1 to 64 axis-aligned boxes, with finite cell coordinates 0 <= min < max <= 1. Each face has a UV rectangle (flips allowed) and texture layer 0..2047; animated layers must fit the same 2048-layer atlas bound. `modelState(id, orientation)` selects one of 24 exact proper cube orientations, identity 0. This is a discrete cube rotation, not an arbitrary-angle box rotation. Prepared metadata is structured-cloneable and the input box/UV arrays are copied.

`meshBlockModels(world,cx,cy,cz)` extracts model surfaces with exact box-union interior removal and neighbouring opaque/same-type boundary occlusion. It preserves interpolated UVs when clipping a face. Scalar sky/block light modulates vertex colour, with existing material PBR lighting, emissive/cutout/translucent options and caller texture-layer materials. `await VoxelModelRenderer.create(engine,world,{material?},signal?)` requires the optional materials peer and is updated after lighting and before engine.render. It streams on chunk add/remove and world edits and observes light changes without consuming world.dirty. It owns default materials and chunk meshes; callback materials/textures stay caller owned. Renderer meshes use the materials pipeline's existing frustum culling and shadows integration.

Queries and VoxelCharacter sweeps use exact boxes, VoxelPhysics builds model triangle surfaces, and scalar, worker and RGB lighting preserve model orientation and whole-face coverage. The existing flood light representation remains one byte per cell, as with slabs; it does not resolve separate disconnected light regions inside a cell. The packed quad renderer leaves these models to the optional renderer. Waterlogging, the GPU octant mesher and voxel path tracing do not acquire a custom-model feature in this job. No speed claim or new core/stage code.

### Voxel-net rooms (batch 242 job 1)
Optional /rooms owns independent VoxelServers in one process, one bound endpoint per world (public proxy endpoints may be supplied). Default capacity is 16 including reserved and parked seats; reservation life is 15,000 ms. Codes are unique 1 to 32 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/hyphen, random 12 hex characters by default. Listing is a synchronous snapshot API for an application's HTTP or app-message lobby, with no built-in account service. ### Batch 214: limit-aware swivel
The optional kinematics-constraints/joint-limits entry provides JointLimitSet and jointLimitPredicate for SolveOptions.acceptPose. A caller supplies local rest-relative quaternions for every candidate joint. Euler bounds use Rx Ry Rz order and radians within -pi..pi; hinges enforce an axis and signed bounds; cones enforce swing plus optional twist. Defaults: unrestricted hinge twist, cone axis +Y, unrestricted cone twist, 1e-7 radian acceptance tolerance. Null limits mean free joints, but missing, nonfinite and zero rotations reject. A 180-degree swing has undefined twist and rejects restricted twist intervals. Bounds are copied at construction. Candidate rejection leaves accepted solver history untouched; predicate inputs are scratch copies that cannot alter the checked pose. This tests supplied rotations, not unsupplied rig orientation or future motion.

## Batch 173: labels and registered multi-component volumes
Optional `@margoengine/sciviz/labels` adds `fusionVolume`, `FusionLayer` and `labelLegend`. One drawable, one fullscreen triangle and one march combine 1..4 sources; each source is categories, RGB, RGBA or 1..4 independent scalar components. Components are interleaved, x fastest. Arrays and transfer results are snapshotted. Each source retains its own dimensions and invertible affine unit-box-to-data mapping, with no registration resampling. Bounds default to [0,nx-1,0,ny-1,0,nz-1]; transform replaces bounds. Dimension and category counts obey the device's 3D/2D texture limits (palette needs one extra transparent slot). Each dimension is at least two.
Category IDs are exact unsigned 32-bit integers, including zero and 4294967295; never interpolate them. Unlisted IDs are transparent but retain distinct boundaries. Each listed category has linear-light RGBA and an optional separate outline RGBA and integer framebuffer-pixel width 1..16 (default 1). Eight nearest-category neighbours per radius detect label-to-label and external boundaries at each ray sample. This is a projected neighbourhood outline, not a smoothed subvoxel segmentation or mesh. `setLabels` atomically validates and snapshots replacements; `labelLegend.update()` refreshes accessible HTML text after edits.
RGB/RGBA channels are linear light, default divisor 255 for byte arrays and 1 otherwise; alpha shares that divisor. RGB opacity defaults to 0.1; RGBA uses its alpha. Colour and intensity sampling is trilinear; component functions are evaluated at 256 physical scalar values into binary16 RGBA tables, and source scalar components are normalized/clamped to their declared range in binary16. No gradient or preintegrated component functions in this entry. Component and source weight default 1; zero hides them. `TransferFunction.evaluate` can supply a 1D function directly; update a snapshotted function by rebuilding the layer.
Default optical mixing sums extinction and weights colours by optical depth; over gives earlier sources/components priority at each sample; maximum selects the largest corrected opacity (earlier wins ties). All three mix before front-to-back ray compositing, never as separately sorted volume draws. Quality defaults to 1.5 samples per projected voxel; density defaults to 1. Step opacity uses distance through each source's voxel coordinates. Each ray caps at 2048 midpoint segments and terminates at alpha >0.9999. Small features thinner than a step can be missed; increase quality within the cap. No native WebGL2 fallback driver; WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported. Internal opaque-geometry termination is the separate volume-quality job, not supplied here.
Entry min+gzip: 6292 B (new, formerly 0), ceiling 6548 B. Sciviz root remains 52045 B and core+stage remains 24209 B. Palette ownership, transforms, component mixing and the one march remain together; splitting would fragment the same source lifecycle without removing full-feature bytes. The MSD demo reduction is 60x60x39, gzip 180024 B intensities and 661 B labels; see its source record for exact output sizes/hashes. Data are demo-only CC BY-SA 4.0, separate from engine source. OpenNeuro RGBA uses the existing CC0 T1.

### Voxel-net recording and replay (batch 242 job 2)
Optional /replay records the exact per-recipient outbound message stream using server.onSend, including welcome and spawn; attach before clients join. Default queued bytes 64 MiB, hard per-message bound 16 MiB. Overflow and I/O errors stop recording and reject flush/close. MVR1 carries protocol version 6, tick rate, recipient id, tick and raw payload; a complete-file footer is mandatory. readVoxelRecording has a default 256 MiB file limit, configurable; playback holds validated records in memory. Files include names, application messages and resume tokens and belong with private bug reports. Select one recipient and use a fresh VoxelNetClient/world with no-op send; advanceTo is forward-only, play defaults to speed 1 and a 1-hour hard bound with AbortSignal. Playback completion means packets delivered to receive; chunk decompression completes asynchronously through the normal client. Seeking backward requires a fresh client/world. This reconstructs server-visible states, not unsent predicted local inputs or deterministic server execution. No GPU work.

Voxel-net /replay entry: 0 -> 3584 B min+gzip, ceiling 3840 B. Server is 18031 B and rooms 19424 B, within existing ceilings. Core + stage unchanged at 24,209 B.
### Value clips (batch 206)
Optional usdz/clips exports valueClips({timeCode?,maxClips:10000,layers?}), valueClipFrames(), ValueClipPlayer and loadValueClips(). The resolver selects a stage pose (default startTimeCode or 0), preserving local/weak-layer strength, descendant namespaces, clip-set order, manifests/defaults/blocks, interpolation gaps, linear/held typed interpolation, quaternion slerp, retiming/holds/reversal/jumps, layer offsets and integer/fractional templates. composition() supplies synchronous layer/archive composition; composeUSDFiles/parseUSDFiles discover external clip files automatically. A manifest query reads the active clip and adjacent clips; absent manifests and interpolateMissingClipValues may require all clips, as in USD. maxClips bounds total candidate files across clip sets; existing maxBytes/maxDepth apply to every clip.
The frame iterator has inclusive start/end and a finite nonzero directional step (default 1). ValueClipPlayer.setTimeCode() is asynchronous and serial, retaining the old model until a new complete frame is ready, including changing topology. dispose aborts a pending request and releases the model. loadValueClips initializes timeCode 0 unless supplied. cacheBytes defaults to 64 MiB of encoded data retained across frames, not a cap on the files/decoded geometry required to resolve the current frame. ### VFX moving space (batch 270 job 1)
Optional vfx/space supplies space.mode (world default, local follows the emitter), column-major rigid space.transform (identity default), inheritVelocity (0..1, default 0) and ratePerDistance (0..1,000,000, default 0). # Batch 185 job 2: volume and array storage

`@margoengine/shader/compute-volume` adds `storageVolume(width, height, depth, options)` and `ComputeVolume`. Default dimension is `3d`, format `rgba16float`, filter `linear`, wrap `clamp-to-edge`; pingPong and readWrite default false. `dimension: '2d-array'` uses integer z as the layer. `coord(i)` maps x-contiguous invocations; `uv(coord)` returns normalized voxel centres (for arrays sample with xy plus the original integer z). All 16 existing storage formats support typed load/store, a single mip and one sample. Integers and unfilterable float32 use load; readWrite requires an r32 format and the WGSL language feature. One image cannot be read and written in one pass without readWrite; pingPong reads the previous image and swaps after a writing dispatch. Device limits bound each axis and array layers; total voxels must fit u32. Data is tightly packed x, y, z and must match the exact byte count. Loss or disposal resets copies to CPU data, not computed state.

### Indexed fragmented MP4 and WebM (batch 269 job 3)
`video/demux` openDemuxedVideo takes URL, Blob or ArrayBuffer and returns the existing frame/seek/step/timestamp/dispose interface. Supply complete initialization and media segments concatenated in one file. First video track only; audio ignored. MP4 retains the AVC, single description and rate-1 edit contract, now with trex/tfhd defaults, tfdt, trun offsets, signed/unsigned composition offsets and duration-zero fragment edits. WebM supports VP8, VP9 and AV1, SimpleBlock/BlockGroup, all lacing modes (laced timing requires DefaultDuration or BlockDuration), unknown-size Segment/Cluster and explicit keyframe flags. Encrypted/transformed tracks and duplicate visible timestamps reject with coded errors. Files and indexes remain fully buffered; GOP decoding is exclusive per request. ## Batch 203 standalone compression
Zstandard is an optional entry over the existing clean-room decoder: concatenated and skippable frames, checksums, a caller destination, default 256 MiB output and 128 MiB declared window. ## Batch 173 job 3: sciviz/cinematic
`cinematicVolume(figure, volume, options)` wraps an existing composite VolumeLayer, shares its scalar and classifier textures, hides the base drawable and restores its previous visibility on disposal. No core or stage imports of cinematic lighting are added. Ordinary slices remain available. Gradient and preintegrated classifiers are accepted; preintegration is treated as local diagonal extinction for secondary paths, not a claim of exact nonlocal preintegrated transport. Source gradient surface shading is replaced by scattering lighting.
All three expensive modes default off. Ambient radius defaults to 8 smallest scene voxels, 8 directions (1..64) and 8 integration steps (1..256). Shadows default to 32 steps (1..2048), toward [0.4,0.6,1]. Ambient radiance defaults [0.3,0.3,0.3], directional radiance [0.7,0.7,0.7]. Path tracing defaults g=0 (-1<g<1), 8 bounces (1..32), albedo 0.9 ([0,1]), seed 1 (uint32), 4096 accumulated samples (1..16777216). Paths converge to the chosen finite-bounce, piecewise-constant integration model, not an unbounded-bounce exact solution. Local AO applies to the deterministic march; path tracing computes ambient visibility by physical path escape instead. Each segment uses the classifier's per-voxel alpha as extinction, scaled by density and the smallest scene voxel. Both ray direction and light distance use scene metric, preserving nonuniform volume transforms. The primary/each scattering march caps at 2048 segments and widens the step to cover the box; shadow/local integral resolutions are explicit quality controls.
Accumulation uses two RGBA32float images plus an RGBA32uint work image (48 bytes per viewport pixel), one integration pass then a display triangle. Counters are always available, so even the unlit wrapper pays those passes and writes compared with ordinary VolumeLayer. `cost({signal})` reads exact last-frame scalar fetches, shadow rays, ambient rays and collisions, with a 30-second mapping deadline. Camera matrix, transform, density, quality, clips, classifier/source replacement and resize reset accumulation. Call reset() after externally updating an existing GPU source texture. configure() validates atomically, snapshots inputs and resets. Sources rebuild through VolumeLayer after device replacement; lighting clears its own history. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are tested; native GL fallback is unsupported and fails before allocation.
Scene-depth termination is owned by batch 173 job 4; this entry currently has the same opaque-interior limitation as the ordinary volume path. Multiple translucent drawables sort as whole layers, not interleaved samples. The EMD-8117 demo contains 64^3 original density samples, reduced from 192^3 at stride 3, without intensity scaling. This is an educational view, not medical evidence.

### Compute dense decompositions (batch 274)

The optional compute/decomp entry returns owned f32 arrays in the input context. It handles real finite matrices, arbitrary leading batches, broadcast solve RHS matrices (only 1-D RHS is a vector), strided/expression inputs, square/tall/wide/reduced/full and empty factors. Arithmetic is f64 in a lazily loaded per-call Rust SIMD Wasm instance on every backend, including native WebGPU and compatibility; GPU inputs incur a readback and results an upload. This is a correctness route, with no device-native decomposition or speed claim. Singular solve/inv, non-positive-definite Cholesky, nonsymmetric eigen/Cholesky input, nonfinite input, f32 output overflow and iteration exhaustion reject. det(singular)=0 and det(0x0)=1. SVD values descend; symmetric eigenvalues ascend. Real symmetric inputs must match across their diagonal exactly; complex/Hermitian arrays are outside compute's supported dtypes. Limits: each matrix dimension and RHS column count <=4096; 16,777,216 f64 workspace words by the checked algorithm bound, and that many f32 output elements per call; Jacobi maxSweeps 100 by default, 1..1000 configurable. Cancellation covers loading, readbacks and batch boundaries (event-loop yield each 16 matrices), not the middle of a synchronous matrix factorization. Concurrent calls own separate Wasm instances; no arena survives a call.

### Adaptive events (batch 195 job 3)
quality/events adaptiveEvents(handler, options) returns run(...args), regress, setMoving, flush, moving, pending and disposable lifecycle. Defaults: interval 100 ms during motion, debounce 120 ms after start/change/end, no sources or signal, performance.now and native timeout clock. Interval/debounce are nonnegative through 2147483647 ms; interval also accepts Infinity to suppress all motion picks. Control events reset the inactivity timer; setMoving(true) remains in force until false or a later regress timeout. At rest there is no intentional throttle. Queued calls retain only the latest arguments and resolve all coalesced callers with that invocation's result; active async calls finish first, so results cannot arrive out of order. Click/drag handlers stay direct. Rest immediately flushes queued input; a stationary pointer with no queued request is not polled or repicked. flush bypasses the interval without overlapping an active call. Handler rejection reaches every corresponding caller; disposal/abort rejects queued and active result promises, cancels timers and subscriptions, and ignores late completion without cancelling the caller-owned GPU task. No idle polling and no scene/core changes. Applications pass an AbortSignal for owner disposal. Native and compatibility picks tested.

New entry 0 to 3,340 B min+gzip; shared reflector 11,355 B, refractor 11,312 B, cube-camera 5,756 B, prefiltered 3,693 B; core + stage stays 24,209 B. Reflection uses Schlick Fresnel (ior default 1.5, allowed 1..4, metalness default 0, allowed 0..1) mixed with baseColor (default #808080). Inherited color tints the reflection. baseColor is an artist-selected constant linear floor term, not direct-light shading. All options are live uniforms.

Inherited roughness (default 0) sets the maximum mip blur. Captured geometry at the plane stays sharp; its world normal distance / blurDistance (default 10 metres, a positive normal float32 from 2^-126 to 3.4028234663852886e38) scales the blur, saturating at the maximum. Empty depth takes maximum blur. Actual inverse oblique projection works for perspective and orthographic captures; there is no assumption of an ordinary depth projection. Up to eight existing box-filtered mips: this is mip blur, not a GGX convolution or screen-space ray tracer. Normal maps distort the lookup; Fresnel uses the geometric plane normal. The standard Reflector's visibility, passes, layer selection, transform convention, capture-only mode and lifecycle remain in effect. Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 compatibility are supported; the lightweight WebGL2 preview still refuses the capture.

### Precipitation cover (batch 236 job 2)
Optional weather/cover is 1,539 B min+gzip, new from 0 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. PrecipitationCover takes an unattached WeatherFX and reuses its top-down depth map (graph order -3) for rain, core Puddles and Snow (order -0.5) and GLTFWeather (cover option). WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility. Bias defaults to 0.02 m (finite, 0 or more). The map is the WeatherFX square of side 2 x Weather radius centred on the camera, at WeatherFX resolution (default 50 m over 256 texels): surfaces outside it count as exposed, so set radius to reach the sheltered surfaces in view. A receiver is sheltered by the highest occluder of the four texels around it: every point under an occluder at least one texel wide stays dry, and up to one texel past an edge does too. Receivers are tested at the shaded point; with multisampling an edge pixel is shaded at its centre, which can lie up to a pixel outside its surface, so a surface that ends exactly at a shelter edge can show a one pixel exposed fringe. Give shelters a small overhang. The capture splash and lens passes are not installed.

Static snapshots require setGeometry after edits; full compatibility supported, native preview refused. Reflected Fresnel branches, roughness, dispersion, absorption and heterogeneous/nested IOR are excluded; source bias is 1e-5 of footprint size. ### Batch 186 job 2: shared shadow atlas
ShadowAtlas from /shadow-atlas replaces LocalShadows on one Clustered instance, retaining its maxLights (1..16, default 4), casters, PCF/PCSS, biases, receiveShadow and clipping. It allocates one depth32float array layer, resolution squared times four bytes, plus a 4096-byte uniform table of guarded rectangles. Default atlas 2048, minimum face 32, maximum face 1024, texelDensity 1. Dimensions are powers of two from 16 to 16384, minimum <= maximum <= atlas, limited further by the device. Point/hemisphere lights retain six faces, spots one; directional cascades and area faces share the image.
Point/spot face demand follows the conservative projected world-range box clipped to the viewport. A near-plane intersection requests full viewport demand; a wholly behind-camera bound requests minimum demand. Authored resolution caps demand. Directional/area faces use authored sizes or maximum face size. All tiles are square. Least-screen-important lights lose one resolution level at a time until all faces fit, retaining every face. If minimum demand cannot fit, RangeError asks for a larger atlas or lower minimum; lights are never silently dropped. At most 256 logical faces. Relocation or any dirty face clears and redraws all active tiles, preserving untouched maps correctly; clean frames use the existing cache. This trades additional redraws on mixed static/dynamic light sets for one predictable allocation. No incremental tile-clear or hysteresis claim.
Deterministic packing proof: sixteen six-face lights at 16 texels use 24,576 rasterized depth texels; four six-face lights requesting 64 texels use 61,440 after fitting a 256 atlas. Both retain every face. This is a work count, not a wall-clock speed result. Source tests cover non-overlap, input immutability, priority, camera-driven viewport changes and caching. Real GPU tests cover point, spot and combined rectangle/sphere filtering on native WebGPU and full WebGL2.
Min+gzip: shadows 11,791 -> 12,052 B (existing 12,145 B ceiling); new /shadow-atlas 0 -> 14,027 B, ceiling 14,448 B. The optional entry reuses the complete caster pipeline rather than duplicating render ownership. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.



## Batch 136: clean-room Draco encoder

The default exporters/draco entry loads one optional Rust/Wasm SIMD encoder on first compression, in a browser worker or in the Node process. The public compressDraco API, abort behavior, GLB preservation and caller-supplied Emscripten encoderPath remain compatible. Sequential and standard/valence EdgeBreaker preserve oriented triangles; independent attribute seams share exact values. Prediction and quantization are described in clean-room.md. A packet is at most 256 MiB, 16,777,216 input points, 50,331,648 indices and 255 attributes; each attribute has one through four components. Floats must be finite. Normal quantization accepts 0 or 2 through 30 bits; a one-bit octahedron has no positive reconstruction range and is rejected. Other quantized floats accept 1 through 30 bits, or 0 for exact values. Fan splitting can increase output point count, which the result and GLB accessors report.

Initial replacement measurement: 181,081 -> 89,161 B min+gzip, with Wasm 156,788 B raw / 58,216 B gzip. The complete proof version below is 91,248 B min+gzip, with Wasm 160,900 B raw / 59,962 B gzip. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. The old prebuilt encoder files have now been removed from source and distribution. No end-to-end speed claim. The byte-output bridge uses eight Wasm boundary calls regardless of output length, rather than one GetValue call per output byte. This counts bridge calls only, not encoding arithmetic or wall-clock time. Quiet speed-phase timing is owed.

At default settings the development comparison preserves exact oriented corner identities and Margo/native-prebuilt decoded result equality on the real fixtures listed in clean-room.md. Box stream 119 vs 130 B; Fox 7,086 vs 7,566 B; the small refrigerator primitive's bounded seed choice gives 352 vs 358 B without changing decoded attributes. This is corpus evidence, not a universal compression-ratio guarantee for arbitrary inputs. The portable normal fixture's maximum Euclidean direction error is below the opaque old encoder at 2/3/8/10/16/24 bits, without weakening its bounds. More settings/corpus evidence belongs to the following proof job.
Batch 191 post/curvature is LDR view-dependent ridge/valley enhancement, not an object-space curvature measurement. Ridge/valley 0..100 (default 1), radius integer 1..16 px (2), gradient threshold 0..1 (0), relative linear-depth rejection >0..1 (0.02). Signed xyz normals come from owned SceneTargets or an any-size callback; supplied normalSpace is world (default) or view. Core meshes capture automatically; optional models use add(model). Empty normals, clear depth and rejected neighbours cannot add silhouette shading. Camera right/up convert world normal derivatives to view space, including rotated and orthographic cameras. The owned capture has the same rgba16float normal/depth footprint as Pixelate. Normal-provider identity is selected at setup; removing a supplied callback later is a tracked configuration defect for Pixelate and Curvature, while changing the texture returned by a stable callback works.

Batch 191 job 6: post/curvature 0 -> 8940 B min+gzip; core plus stage unchanged at 24,209 B.

## Scientific datasets (batch 176 job 1)
The optional @margoengine/sciviz/datasets entry normalizes structured curvilinear, rectilinear, mixed PolyData, unstructured, multiblock and partitioned inputs to an AnalysisGrid-compatible DataSet. Fields and geometry are owned snapshots; source cell IDs, sparse blocks, names and top-level block IDs are retained. Composite topology is concatenated without welding separate blocks. Flattened arrays are the intersection of block field names; heterogeneous fields remain available on the original blocks. Shared field widths must agree. Use each block when a field is not common. Empty blocks are null. Source dimensions live under dimensions, not the regular-image dims discriminator. Existing pipeline, contour, clip, calculator, probe and glyph entries consume the normalized type directly. Contours of line cells return points, and matching isolated vertices are retained; clipping supports these dimensions too. Constant line cells do not emit infinitely many contour points.

Defaults: maxPoints=1000000 (allowed 1..10000000), subdivisions=2 (1..64, rounded upward to a power of two). Source cells are bounded by maxPoints and output cells by 4*maxPoints; tessellated points are bounded by maxPoints. Lagrange curve/triangle/quad/tetrahedron/hexahedron/wedge orders 1..10 use equispaced nodes. Quadratic curve, triangle, quad, tetrahedron, hexahedron, wedge and pyramid use the standard 3/6/8/10/20/15/13-node spaces. Explicit referenceNodes may permute the standard lattice. Higher-order cells are uniformly approximated with interpolated simplex vertices; callers raise subdivisions for finer approximation. This is deterministic h-refinement, not adaptive error-controlled refinement or an exact curved-cell filter. Matching generated nodes share original-ID interpolation keys across cells. Independent composite blocks remain independent, including ghost boundaries; ghost arrays are retained, not implicitly removed.

PolyData source order is vertices, lines, polygons, strips. Polygons must be simple and planar (relative planarity threshold 1e-10); concave polygons are ear clipped. Polyhedron face streams must be closed and consistently oriented with planar simple faces. Nonconvex cells use a face-plane arrangement, limited to 4096 regions per source cell, and signed solid-angle interior classification. Generated interpolation uses mean-value coordinates with boundary handling and affine checks. Arrangement point merging uses 128*Number.EPSILON times the source diagonal. Self-intersecting surfaces and degenerate cells are not supported input. Linearized filtering follows the existing filter entry's numerical domain and interpolation policy; source curved-cell interpolation is not re-evaluated after each filter.

Readers: .vtr, .vts, .vtu, .vtp, .vtm, .vtpd/.vtpc, with numeric VTK payloads decoded by @margoengine/loaders/vtk-xml. Raw-appended arrays use its bounded range reader; metadata sniffing and composite XML are bounded by maxBytes (default 64 MiB). Every retained array is decoded when creating the owned dataset. Composite references resolve against the input URL or baseURL, or an explicit files map; nesting is limited to 64 and cycles reject. Relative string inputs use baseURL, or document.baseURI in a browser. Files must fit the specified per-read and decoded-array limits. All numeric point/cell tuples are retained; scalar defaults to the first one-component point field. PLOT3D covers whole-grid 2D/3D, single/multiblock, formatted Fortran D/E exponents, stream binary and 4-byte-record-marker unformatted, both byte orders, 4/8-byte coordinates and optional iblank. Defaults: 3D, formatted, multiblock, no blanking; binary defaults little endian, float64, record markers. Options explicitly disambiguate variants. Iblank is retained as an array, not a rendering mask. Solution Q/function files, plane-record layouts and 8-byte record markers are not claimed. The NASA originals use the supported formatted whole-grid variant. No file is fetched or GPU device created on import, and cancellation preserves its exact reason. No core or stage change and no measured speed claim.

Dataset entry size: 35,806 minified bytes and 13,072 gzip bytes, previously 0, optional ceiling 13,423 bytes. The entry keeps topology normalization, interpolation, nonconvex scientific-cell decomposition and VTK/PLOT3D adaptation together; splitting would add cross-entry orchestration for the same bytes to users of this one feature. Core plus stage remains 24,209 gzip bytes.
### Batch 217 job 3: scroll and range playback

Optional cutscene/scroll exports RangePlayback and ScrollPlayback. Range defaults: entire timeline, iterationCount 1 (nonnegative fractions and Infinity supported), normal direction, speed 1. Directions are normal, reverse, alternate and alternateReverse. update(delta) runs the borrowed player's skip() for each crossed leg, preserving instant order; seek resets each repeated leg without firing its start instant. At most 1000 boundaries per update; larger deltas reject before mutation. play resolves true at completion, false on pause/stop, rejects on AbortSignal; pause resumes progress, completion restarts. Instants stay on the player, iteration/finish events on the controller. Controllers own advancement, so pause the base player and update the controller only.

Scroll defaults: window, physical y axis, start 0, end current maximum scroll offset, whole timeline range, scrub 0 seconds (immediate), automatic events/frames true. Pixel offsets and seconds are clamped to the supplied interval. A positive scrub is an exponential time constant; automatic smoothing settles to the target within 1e-7 seconds. automatic false uses update(delta) from the app's clock. refresh() re-reads content bounds; resize and scroll events refresh automatically. No-scroll sources hold the start. Physical horizontal offsets can use explicit signed start/end for RTL layouts. Abort/dispose cancels callbacks and keeps the borrowed player usable. No renderer or core additions, and no speed claim.

Batch 217 job 3 measured min+gzip: new scroll entry 0 to 2,048 B, ceiling 2,304 B. The optional entry combines clock ownership and cleanup for both timeline drivers; splitting those controllers would add entry and integration complexity. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

## Batch 177 job 2: statistical charts

Student-t critical values support positive fractional residual df through 100000, including LOESS df below one. Bracketing rejects critical values above 1e150 with a remedy to increase residual df; no fixed-range clipping or unconverged fraction is returned. The continued fraction has a 2048-iteration hard limit and checked relative convergence. The low-df regression includes independent SciPy values at df 0.2 and 0.5.

Entry gzip sizes: `/stats` absent (0 B) to 6,719 B, initial ceiling 6,975 B; `/maths` 5,703 B to 8,854 B, ceiling raised from 5,959 B to 9,120 B. Sharing the math functions between direct transforms and chart marks avoids independent implementations; splitting the public CPU utility entry would add import orchestration and break the requested `/maths` access. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

`/stats` creates owned CPU marks and standalone vector SVG with axes, ticks, titles and labels; it introduces no Figure/core/stage API or GPU pass. Error bars support x/y symmetric or asymmetric amounts, caps and points. Box plots use interpolated quartiles, median, Tukey adjacent-value whiskers and outliers; violins use 96 Gaussian KDE queries over data range plus three bandwidths, maximum half-width 0.4 per category. Area and pre/post/mid step lines preserve missing-data breaks. Signed area/bar stacks keep separate positive/negative bases, with optional independent unit normalization. ECDF is right-continuous, two-sample Q-Q interpolates common midpoint probabilities, 2D density is a diagonal Gaussian KDE, and hexagons expose exact input membership. All mathematics is also exported from `/maths`.

Defaults: SVG 800x480, padding 58 px (minimum 24), white background, empty title/x/y labels, six categorical colours, automatic linear axes with nice ticks; point radius 2.5 px, line width 1.4 px. Box width 0.6; whisker multiplier 1.5; area baseline 0; stack kind area, normalization off, bar width 0.8 of smallest positive x gap; step mode post; density queries 32x32 (2..256); hex radius supplied in data units. Silverman bandwidth uses sample SD and IQR/1.34; constant observations use 1% of max(1,abs(value)) before the Silverman factor. Optional bandwidths must be positive. Violins independently normalize maximum width, not sample count. Named box/violin groups label the categorical x axis. Stack series use category colours in input order.

Linear and LOESS confidence defaults to 0.95, accepted range (0,0.999]. OLS needs three paired finite samples and nonconstant x. LOESS local degree is one, span 0.5, two robustness iterations (integer 0..10), at least three neighbours and three finite pairs. Tricube weights exclude the furthest selected neighbour. Queries default to sorted observed x; optional `at` permits explicit positions. Local zero-weight or nonpositive residual-df cases reject with a suggested remedy. LOESS intervals condition on final robust weights and are approximate pointwise mean bands, not simultaneous, prediction or extrapolation guarantees. Missing xy pairs are removed from statistical fits; area/step drawings retain gaps, stack NaN contributes zero. Errors must be nonnegative magnitudes; signed NASA lower errors are converted to magnitude only when drawing their bars.

Inputs are finite with magnitude at most 1e100, with NaN denoting missing. At most 100000 observations per series, 100000 Q-Q queries, 1000000 stack cells, 4000000 sample/query or LOESS fit/sample pairs, and 200000 SVG marks. This bounds allocations/work; reduce the dataset or query resolution beyond it. Maths is synchronous and owns results; import has no DOM, network or global side effects. Argument failures are linked RangeErrors carrying code `out-of-range`. No speed gain, exact confidence coverage, journal layout or new interactive Figure claim. The 13-chart real-data demo includes downloads and a 390 px layout.
Batch 175 optional entry min+gzip: sciviz/omezarr 0 -> 20,866 B, recorded ceiling 21,492 B. These bytes include the shared Zarr region reader, store validation, scalar adapters and codec pipelines. Keeping them together preserves one reader and source contract; splitting the entry solely for a smaller recorded size would duplicate validation or require additional imports for a cloud source. Core and stage source are unchanged.
Batch 175 core plus stage measurement: unchanged at 24,209 B gzip, below the 25,000 B gate.

### Compute Rust SIMD CPU backend (batch 274 job 3)

createCpuWasm from compute/cpu-wasm returns the existing CPU API, with f32/i32/u32 values and all existing built-in CPU operations. Custom WGSL remains unsupported. Every context loads an isolated SIMD-required Wasm instance on demand; creation accepts AbortSignal and normalizes load/compile failures to a coded MargoError. Numerical calls are synchronous and cannot be interrupted mid-dispatch. No GPU or worker is required. Arrays remain normal owned host buffers, so memory growth never invalidates an array or a returned readback. The transient packet limit is 8,388,608 f64 words (including descriptors and parameters); larger work rejects with RangeError and can use smaller stream chunks. The module has a 512 MiB memory ceiling. Transcendental operations use host Math imports; exact A/B equivalence is against the JavaScript CPU backend on the same host. Expression intermediates cross the bulk bridge; there is no wall-clock speed claim. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B gzip. Final entry and Wasm sizes are recorded with the job's size gate.

### Batch 195 job 2: resource quality knobs

`@margoengine/quality/knobs` exports `textureResolutionKnob`, `particleKnob`, `renderTargetKnob` and `msaaKnob`. Live ladders default to scales [1, 0.5, 0.25], weight 2, with custom names/scales/weights. A `FeatureScaler` or `watchFeatures` accepts the first three. Texture and target knobs require a device, original texture and synchronous `bind(texture)` callback; level zero and disposal restore the caller-owned original. Reduced allocations are released after rebinding. Recreate knobs and caller-owned resources after device loss.

Texture resolution accepts a retained matching ImageBitmap/canvas and RGBA8 (linear or sRGB) single-layer 2D texture with COPY_DST and RENDER_ATTACHMENT usage. It prefilters with the browser's high-quality canvas resampler into one-mip textures; sampler filtering is caller-owned. The original remains allocated for exact restoration, so no total-memory reduction is claimed. Target sizes allocate genuinely smaller single-sampled colour textures with the original format and usage. Their contents are redrawn. `bind` updates the view and any dependent resources together; omit caller depth to let the engine manage matching depth. Custom history/depth remains the consumer's responsibility.

Particle levels multiply live VFX rate, followed by a final zero-birth level. Existing particles finish normally; capacity, explicit bursts and simulation work remain unchanged. Level zero restores the original option, including its absence.

Accepted limit: live MSAA change needs an engine re-create. `msaaKnob.apply(0|1)` records 4|1 samples only. It intentionally is not a live FeatureKnob, so the scaler cannot attribute savings to a change that did not happen. Dispose existing engines, call `prepare()` and then public `Engine.create`, rebuilding scenes/plugins. `prepare` applies the existing page-wide quality tier and returns effective samples; phones and exactSize remain single-sampled. Keep that tier stable while engines live, including device restore. No renderer internals or core/stage changes.

Entry size: quality/knobs 0 to 2,181 B min+gzip, initial ceiling 2,437 B; generated umbrella alias 60 B. Resource allocation/restoration and deferred selection share one cohesive optional API; a split would complicate lifetime management without improving quality. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. No speed claim.

### Batch 201 job 3: glTF audio emitter entry
`@margoengine/gltf-pro/audio` exports applyGLTFAudio and its controller/options/emitter types. The caller supplies an AudioListener; no context is created on import or by glTF metadata loading. KHR_audio_emitter and MSFT_audio_emitter remain draft formats. Audio-only glTF scenes are accepted when nodes/scenes reference audio metadata. Selection uses options.scene, else doc.scene or 0, and only that scene's reachable nodes/global emitters. KHR sources retain independent gain, loop and autoPlay; emitter gain multiplies source gain. Defaults are gain 1, no loop/autoPlay, inverse distance, refDistance 1, unlimited maximum distance (the largest Web Audio finite float), rolloff 1, omnidirectional shape, full cones 2*pi, outer gain 0 and -Z forward. MSFT defaults are exponential distance, refDistance 1, maxDistance 256, rolloff 1, gain 1, no looping or auto play, +Z forward; explicit cone half angles convert to full Web Audio degrees, absent cones remain omnidirectional. Scene emitters must be global. The inherited audio package panning default is HRTF and its live source panningModel setter remains available.
Embedded bufferViews, data URIs and safe relative/external URIs share each decoded clip within an attachment. maxDownloadBytes defaults to 64 MiB, decoded PCM has four times that budget, maxSources defaults to 256; raise the named option for larger content. Data MIME types are audio/wav and audio/mpeg; embedded bufferViews require a MIME type. Cancellation is prompt even while native decodeAudioData finishes privately. No media streaming is implied. Playback remains subject to the browser's user-gesture policy.
MSFT weighted choices are made on new play triggers, with nonnegative finite weights, at least one positive weight, and options.random in [0,1). options.autoplay true explicitly triggers either dialect; false disables authored autoPlay. sync(time,playing,animation) follows MSFT events and compensates missed frames, pause/resume offsets, stop, backward seek and paused scrubbing; repeated synchronization reuses the event's weighted choice. Call it with the animation clock each tick. Legacy EXT_property_animation is a separate optional extension; this reader consumes authored property values and the required event contract. Dispose releases this attachment's sounds, never the caller's listener/context, and model disposal invokes it. No core/stage change or speed claim.
