Wasm is 160,900 B raw and 59,962 B gzip; core plus stage stays 24,209 B. The added 2,087 entry bytes buy a second attribute traversal and complete normal-prediction candidates that close all observed ratio losses. RAW symbol alphabets are bounded below 2^20; histogram/model/order storage peaks at 16 MiB in wasm32. Wider alphabets retain tagged coding. These are size/work-count measurements; timing is deferred.
### Batch 173 job 5: direct curvilinear and spherical volumes
Optional sciviz/curvilinear snapshots finite node geometry and scalars (NaN masks missing nodes). General structured cells use trilinear inverse mapping, a stackless spatial cell tree and 24 Newton iterations per candidate; singular or sign-changing corner/centre Jacobians reject. Caller must supply an injective, non-overlapping grid; the validation is not a proof of global injectivity. Spherical axes are strictly increasing, radii positive, latitude in [-pi/2,pi/2], longitude unwrapped across at most 2 pi with a duplicated endpoint for periodic fields. Node indices are x/longitude fastest. Scalar textures retain the root volume's binary16 precision; topology is float32. Masked interpolation support stays transparent, without filling holes.
ReferenceStep is the physical opacity distance (default smallest nonzero grid edge); quality controls samples per reference distance. At most 4096 segments cover each ray, widening the step when necessary. Discrete midpoint sampling can miss sub-step features; quality/refStep control that error. Gradient classifiers use physical finite differences; preintegrated classification shares step/density conventions. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported; the native GL-only sciviz driver is not.
Coordinate slices accept fractional indices and tessellate the original coordinate surfaces; spherical slices have node-spaced polygon silhouettes. Outline stride defaults to 8, retains all boundary curves and uses one-pixel lines. Owned source stays hidden, with classifier/density/mode/clip controls on layer.source; dispose the mapped layer to remove its source and all sections. Geometry and missingness are immutable; create a new layer to replace data.
NOAA demos use public-domain modified subsets: NEXRAD straight measured rays (no refraction or earth-curvature correction), WOA23 five-degree stride/11 original depth levels, depth exaggerated 231.67x. Attribution, processing and SHA256 records sit beside the binary subsets. No timing or speed claim.

Mapped entry size: @margoengine/sciviz/curvilinear 8220 B min+gzip (ceiling 8476 B); new entry previously absent, core + stage unchanged 24209 B.
### Batch 186 job 3: point-light cube cookies
CubeProjectorLights in /cube-projector is a ProjectorLights superset. Use setCubes for point-light entries and inherited setProjectors for spot images on the same light list. Entry i belongs to clustered light i. Cube faces are +X,-X,+Y,-Y,+Z,-Z, equal square RGBA8 images with top-to-bottom rows; side 1..4096, at most 16 distinct cube/colour-space pairs and 16,777,216 combined face texels, at most 1024 indexed entries. Pixels are copied on setCubes. Null/unset entries multiply by one, spots ignore cube entries and point lights ignore spot images. At the emitter origin, direction is undefined and the cookie is neutral.
Defaults: sRGB encoding, identity emitter-to-world quaternion. Rotation accepts finite nonzero quaternions, normalized with scaled arithmetic to avoid overflow. Filtering is bilinear at the supplied image level, seamless across edges with the specified three-face corner average. Decode sRGB and multiply alpha before interpolation. No derivative-based mip selection or HDR/float face input is claimed. Cube storage is one additional binding and at most the next power-of-two buffer capacity, bounded by device storage limits; existing spot storage remains shared. Restore recreates storage from copied bytes; disposal releases both cookie kinds.
Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 production shaders prove all six colours, face UV orientation, edge continuity, corner average, rotation, sRGB/alpha and mixed spot/cube isolation. Min+gzip: reconstructed prior projector 2,639 B -> 2,720 B, inside its 2,871 B ceiling; new cube-projector 0 -> 4,493 B, ceiling 4,716 B. Composition avoids duplicate spot upload and lifecycle state. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.




### View-driven geography (batch 180 job 1)
New optional sciviz/geo-lod, no core or stage edits. Defaults: projection mercator, maxZoom 15 (range 0..24), tileBudget 64 selected leaves, tilePixels 256 physical pixels, cacheTiles 128 resident tiles, concurrency 6 tile jobs (imagery and elevation fetch concurrently per tile), fadeSeconds 0.3, segments 32 (1..256), skirt 1000 metres. Cache must exceed the selected budget to retain a root fallback. Coarse fallback plus fading children may draw at most twice the leaf budget; residency is capped independently by cacheTiles. CPU pixels and meshes are retained for device restore. Missing imagery (404 or undefined) keeps a cached ancestor; other errors reject ready and remain in error without retry. Frame-driven loading needs continuing rendering or explicit updateView; ready waits current requests only, with an optional signal. Disposing aborts requests and drops resources.
Flat Mercator/equirectangular and WGS84 globe use XYZ Mercator source bounds, ending at +/-85.05112878 degrees latitude (polar caps are outside this raster source). View selection uses conservative projected bounding boxes, not terrain occlusion. Heights and skirts are metres; elevation is a pixel-centred bilinear grid. No vertical datum conversion is inferred. geoTerrainStreamSource wraps longitude and clips latitude at a fixed level, resampling to TerrainStream.tileTexels (2..1024); the caller supplies TerrainStream's physical tileSize, origin and colours. quantizedGeoElevation calls tiles/terrain's decoder lazily, rasterises pixel centres, rejects incomplete coverage and does not infer a geographic tiling scheme. Native WebGL2 preview is refused by requireGPU; WebGL2 compatibility uses the same draw path. No wall-clock speed claim.

Geo-lod entry size: new 0 to 7261 B min+gzip, ceiling 7517 B. One optional entry retains a cohesive view/cache/height/render lifecycle. Core plus stage unchanged at 24,209 B.
Batch 181 job 1, complete WebGL2 route: sciviz/fallback exports createFallbackFigure. Calling
it explicitly installs the shared compatibility layer for the page, even with native WebGPU.
Importing it performs no installation or Wasm load. The full tier requires highp fragment
precision and EXT_color_buffer_float; unsupported hardware rejects with coded unsupported.
The smaller sciviz/webgl2 preview attacher is unchanged. All normal Figure layers use the full
shared route, including 3D volume textures, slices, axes, bars and bricked page tables. CPU
isosurfaces share Margo's cases and vertex layout and use at most floor(maxStorageBufferBindingSize/96)
triangles. They retain their source and rebuild on device restoration; caller-owned lost GPU
sources retain the existing hide-and-recreate contract. Installation is page-wide; dispose
figures before the app uninstalls it. Concurrent native WebGPU and compatibility contexts in
one page are not provided by this factory.

Correctness bound in fallback-browser.mjs: at most 2% of all pixels differ by more than 8/255
in any RGB channel and mean maximum-channel error <=1/255, including edges/background.
Observed on the dev PC: zero differing bytes for seven 192x144 fixtures (real head samples,
surfaces, composite/MIP volumes, slices, CPU/GPU isosurfaces, bars and heatmaps). Device
replacement preserves the isosurface bytes exactly. These fixtures do not prove every
possible dataset or every GPU matches exactly. Demos head, stars and wind accept
?backend=webgl2, retaining their original licensed data. No timing or rival speed claim.

## Batch 177 job 3: specialised charts

The optional sciviz/charts-extra entry is 7292 B gzip (new entry, previous 0 B, ceiling 7548 B); core + stage remains 24,209 B. It provides polar/wind rose, ternary, candlestick/OHLC, pie/donut, sunburst/squarified treemap, Sugiyama Sankey/alluvial, radar and UTC calendar heatmaps. All paths, own axes/scales, labels and data titles export as vector SVG with no raster fallback. Layout coordinates are 1000x600, export width/height are positive and default to those values. Hierarchies: 10,000 nodes, 64 levels, nonnegative leaves, internal sums. Flow graphs: DAG, 10,000 nodes, 50,000 input/expanded vertices, 129 layers; one global width scale, default 12-unit padding/16-unit nodes/8 sweeps. Cyclic graphs reject; flow imbalance is shown as a source/sink, never silently rescaled. Long links use dummy vertices. Alluvial categories are stage-specific and adjacent transitions aggregate; individual records are not separately colored through shared categories. Calendar years 100..9998, UTC, Monday start by default, missing days empty. Wind speeds below 0.5 are calm; calm remains in percentage denominators; 16 sectors and [0,2,5,10,Infinity] speed breaks default. Radar domains are per spoke; polar radius is linear or positive logarithmic. Standalone layouts do not add DOM interactions or modify Figure.

### Compute NN extras (batch 274 job 4)

compute/nn-extra adds BatchNorm, GroupNorm, ConvTranspose2d, LSTM, GRU, upsample and Upsample. All support Tensor gradients and the existing JavaScript CPU, Rust SIMD CPU, WebGPU and compatibility routes. Data and parameters use the context's float32 primitives. Norm eps defaults 1e-5 and affine defaults true. BatchNorm accepts rank >=2 and a channel axis (default 1); training needs >1 value per channel. Running mean starts at zero, variance at one; momentum is the new-batch contribution (default 0.1, null cumulative); trackRunningStats defaults true. Inference uses saved buffers. GroupNorm takes NCHW-style [batch,channels,...spatial], channels divisible by groups, and the same statistics in train/eval. Module stateDict/loadStateDict include nested module state; BatchNorm stores running mean, running variance and batch count in addition to learned parameters. Batch count persistence uses f32, so integer counts above 16777216 lose unit resolution.

ConvTranspose2d input is [N,C,H,W], weight [inChannels,outChannels/groups,kh,kw]; stride/dilation default 1, padding/outputPadding 0, groups 1, bias true. Output padding must be below stride or dilation. withOutputSize selects dimensions in the stride-derived output range. Output geometry is (input-1)*stride-2*padding+dilation*(kernel-1)+1+outputPadding. Metadata uses O(outputH*outputW*inChannels/groups*kernelH*kernelW) indices/masks per group and a batch-offset table; backward scatter sums overlapping float contributions in the backend's order. Use smaller batches/images to respect device buffer limits; no tiling is claimed.

Recurrent input/output is [time,batch,features] by default (batchFirst false). numLayers 1, bidirectional false, bias true, dropout 0. Dropout applies between stacked layers while training. LSTM uses i,f,g,o gates; GRU uses r,z,n, with reset applied after recurrent candidate projection. run returns sequence, final h and LSTM c, with state shape [layers*directions,batch,hidden]. Optional lengths mask padded output and retain previous state for each batch item. forward returns sequence only; run's returned tensors share a differentiation graph and must remain alive through their backward uses. States are explicit, never held between calls. Recurrent state/table storage grows with sequence length through the tape.

Upsampling takes [batch,channels,1..3 spatial axes]. Choose size or scaleFactor (default 2), nearest by default. Linear/bilinear/trilinear use half-pixel centers unless alignCorners true; bicubic is 2D with a=-0.75 and clamped edges. Nearest uses floor(outputCoordinate*inputSize/outputSize). Scale-derived sizes floor their products. Interpolation metadata is O(outputPixels*taps^rank), with 1/2/4 taps per spatial axis. It does not implement antialiased downsampling. Different data layouts compose the existing permute operation.

Measured sizes: compute/nn-extra 0 to 20860 B gzip, ceiling 21486 B; compute/nn 19137 to 18873 B; compute root remains 39851 B and core plus stage remains 24209 B. One optional entry shares tape/selection helpers; a split would duplicate them. No wall-clock speed claim.
### Depth, MSAA and mip targets (batch 271 job 1)
`@margoengine/creative/targets-depth` exports DepthTextureRenderTarget, a TextureRenderTarget (cube, array or 3D; rgba8unorm or rgba16float) with per-surface depth, 4x multisampling and mip generation. Defaults: depth true, depthFormat depth32float (also depth24plus, depth24plus-stencil8), samples 1 (1 or 4), per pass depthLoadOp clear and clearDepth 0 (reversed Z, as the engine). Each mip and layer or volume slice owns its own 2D depth texture (multisampled when samples is 4); depth is not resolved or mipmapped, since WebGPU has no depth resolve. At 4x, cube and array layers resolve straight into their layer; a volume slice resolves into a 2D scratch that is copied into the slice when the pass ends. generateMipmaps(encoder) fills mips 1 and up from mip 0 with an exact area-weighted box footprint, so odd sizes (5 to 2 to 1) weight edge texels by their covered fraction; volumes also filter across slices. Allocation, counting colour, retained depth, multisample colour and volume scratch, is capped at 256 MiB per target. restore(device) drops every attachment and pipeline; callers redraw. On the WebGL2 layer, volume slices drawn with depth go through the layer's 2D stand-in (two blits per such pass; operational playbook 3.2). Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 are checked; no speed claim.

Depth target entry: before 0 B, after 3398 B gzip, optional ceiling 3654 B. TextureRenderTarget gains one protected textureUsage() hook (COPY_DST for the volume resolve copy); the /targets entry stays within its ceiling. Core plus stage remains 24209 B.
### Batch 1 package test discovery

The umbrella npm test command discovers tests/*.test.js, matching its current test directory and the repository coverage invariant. This manifest-only repair changes no runtime entry, API or size ceiling; other test extensions and nested directories are outside that existing invariant.




## Typed tables and cross-filter (batch 174 job 2)

`@margoengine/sciviz/table` is an independent optional entry, 12,324 B min+gzip from 0 B, ceiling 12,694 B. `@margoengine/decoders/snappy` is 1,250 B from 0 B, ceiling 1,506 B. The bytes buy scalar CSV/Arrow/Parquet readers, null/int64 preservation, indexed filters and deterministic aggregation; splitting the table API would complicate shared column and filter identity. Core + stage stays 24,209 B.

Tables borrow immutable equal-length typed columns. Dictionary strings use Uint32 indices; validity is a separate bitmap. Integer and time values retain signed/unsigned 64-bit storage. Wide decimal and opaque binary scalars are lossless dictionary strings (unscaled decimal with its scale, or hex). Readers accept flat scalar tables, not nested/repeated arrays, tensors, encrypted/external Parquet chunks, obsolete LZO/Hadoop LZ4 or Arrow view layouts. Flatten nested sources before reading. Arrow files and streams support dictionaries, replacement/delta dictionaries and LZ4-frame/Zstd buffer compression. Parquet supports flat row groups, v1/v2 pages, plain, dictionary, RLE, delta binary/length/prefix and byte-stream-split encodings, six modern codecs and page CRC. The readers default to 100,000,000 rows and 536,870,912 input/decoded-block bytes; overrides are explicit. Streaming/range reads belong to the separate large-series job.

Range filters are [lower, upper); set filters use exact typed equality, including explicit null. Dimensions intersect; a cleared dimension passes nulls. Every dimension builds its own index once. Boundary/set changes touch only changed row spans/postings and changed bitmap words; first-time indexing and switching filter kinds are full-index operations. Duplicate row values are retained.

Aggregation supports up to 4,096 1D/2D bins per call, final upper edge included. Host classification uses numeric column values; supplied GPU context performs all count, valid-count, sum, minimum and maximum tile reductions. Mean uses the merged sum/valid count. Rows without a valid coordinate do not enter bins. Null/nonfinite values do not enter numeric statistics. Counts are exact Uint32. Numeric inputs round to f32, each tile adds in fixed source order, and host totals merge in float64; this is not exact-real or float64-input summation. A tile's sum error relative to its f32 inputs follows gamma(255) times its absolute input sum, before host rounding. Rescale values if f32 inputs/tile sums overflow. Empty numeric bins return NaN. CPU fallback follows the same tile order. No timing or rival-throughput claim is made.

The 10,000,000-row correctness proof repeats the 4,096 licensed TLC observations, selects 9,670,406 rows and compares every bin statistic with an independent exhaustive reference on WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility. The linked demo selects 2,211 observations below two miles and changes both rendered charts.
## Batch 178 PDF and math
See [publication limits and evidence](sciviz-publication.md). TeX subset: 16384 characters, 64 nested grammar levels, explicit failure for unsupported commands and missing glyphs. PDF: one page, figure-generated SVG operations, 128 nested SVG levels; caller-supplied fonts outlined rather than embedded/searchable. Native MathML and em-based outline layouts have documented font-specific appearance differences. New optional math entry: 0 to 4750 B min+gzip (ceiling 5002 B); PDF: 0 to 5434 B (ceiling 5700 B). Sciviz root changes 55802 to 56339 B for shared owned label/export lifecycle, within its 56635 B ceiling; export-vector measures 3956 B. Core + stage unchanged at 24209 B. Keep parser/layout together and PDF graphics/object ownership together: splitting adds import/lifetime complexity without removing any necessary operation. No performance measurement.

## Engineering file readers (batch 176 job 2)
Six optional entries: sciviz/hdf5, /cgns, /xdmf, /exodus, /openfoam and /ensight. No new core or stage code. FileOptions maxBytes defaults to 64 MiB per read/metadata object/decoded selection; normalized geometry uses the existing DataSet maxPoints/subdivisions bounds. Integer values outside JavaScript's safe precision reject explicitly. Readers take AbortSignal; lazy HDF5 files support dispose and Symbol.dispose. In-memory companion files use exact resource names via files or resolve; remote files use baseURL or the source URL.
HDF5: superblocks 0..3 including user blocks, object headers 1/2 and continuations, legacy local-heap symbol tables, compact links and dense links in fractal heaps, v1/v2 B-trees, compact/contiguous/chunked arrays, single/implicit/fixed/extensible/v2-B-tree chunk indexes including allocated pages, missing chunks as fill values, fixed numeric/string and variable-string data, deflate and shuffle. HDF5 2.0 layout version 5 filtered chunk records are also accepted. Numeric hyperslabs read only intersecting chunks or contiguous rows; opening does not decode dataset payloads. Attribute name projection avoids decoding unrelated reference/compound attributes. Metadata signatures, ranges and index structure are checked; HDF5 metadata lookup3 checksums are not currently verified. Unsupported shared/huge heap messages, virtual/external datasets, arbitrary compound/array/vlen numeric datatypes, applied filters other than deflate/shuffle and nonstandard float encodings reject by name. Deflate verifies its Adler checksum.
CGNS/HDF5: structured Cartesian/cylindrical grids, unstructured linear and common quadratic/complete order-two cells, mixed sections and NGON/NFACE polyhedra. Primary cells follow base cell dimension; boundary elements do not inflate solution tuple counts. FlowSolution selection defaults to the first solution; Vertex/CellCenter fields are retained. All matching bases/zones become independent blocks. ADF files require conversion through CGNS tools. Boundary condition subtrees, rind arrays, non-node/cell solutions, external CGNS links and uncommon higher-order element families remain outside this entry's current semantic projection.
Xdmf 2/3: XML/HDF/raw Binary data items; numeric endian/precision; strided HyperSlab and JOIN; basic XML path references; uniform/curvilinear/rectilinear/regular and mixed linear/quadratic/polyhedral grids; spatial composites and selected temporal collections. timeIndex defaults 0. Other Function expressions, subset grids, arbitrary XPath/XInclude and compressed Binary items require writer materialization. Structured Dimensions and origin/spacing are converted from slow-to-fast file order to x-fastest dataset order.
Exodus: classic/64-bit-offset NetCDF through the existing /netcdf reader and NetCDF-4/HDF5 storage through /hdf5; coordinates, finite-element blocks, selected nodal/element/global time results, entity maps and node/side sets. timeIndex defaults 0. Results defined on only some blocks remain on elementBlocks with their true block IDs; only fully defined results enter flattened cell arrays. CDF-5, grouped assemblies, arbitrary polyhedral Exodus blocks and edge/face result families are not projected.
OpenFOAM: polyMesh points/faces or faceCompactList/owner/neighbour/boundary; ascii and raw binary, label/scalar widths 32/64 and either byte order; volume/point scalar/vector/tensor internal fields, patch values and owner extrapolation where no patch value is written. Defaults mesh=constant/polyMesh, time=0, fields=[], boundaries=true. Named patches become independent polydata blocks. Calculated boundary values must be written by the solver; this reader does not execute boundary-condition code, includes or dictionary macros. Multi-region/decomposed cases can be resolved as separate calls.
EnSight Gold: ascii, C binary and Fortran record binary geometry; unstructured common linear/quadratic, nsided/nfaced and structured/rectilinear/uniform blocks; scalar/vector/tensor node/element files; case wildcards and timeIndex selection. littleEndian defaults true. Full transient file-set scheduling, partial/undefined result records, material/species files, complex constants and uncommon structured flags are not interpreted. Original part and source-cell boundaries remain intact. These are file-format limits, not speed or universal-format claims.

Engineering entry gzip bytes (new entries, each before 0 B): sciviz/hdf5 8990 B; sciviz/cgns 18306 B; sciviz/xdmf 19254 B; sciviz/exodus 20029 B; sciviz/openfoam 10566 B; sciviz/ensight 11539 B. Combined core plus stage remains 24209 B. The optional entries retain complete reader ownership, numeric decoding and dataset normalization; splitting them solely for smaller individual numbers would add cross-entry orchestration without reducing an importer's total bytes.

LoadedModel.pbr exposes the underlying PBRModel; LoadedModel.animation is a paused player or null for static glTF. Existing fit/signal, transform, raw-buffer and destroy contracts remain. CPU bounds are bind-pose bounds. Requires a WebGPU device, native or supplied by the WebGL2 compatibility layer; the native WebGL2 preview has no PBR device. The optional entry is 1,660 B gzip (previously 1,473 B); core + stage root stays 24,209 -> 24,209 B, zero added bytes, below 25,000 B. No runtime core or stage-root change and no speed claim.
